q: 一致性哈希要解决的核心问题是什么？
options: 让哈希函数的输出更难被反推或碰撞，提升系统的加密安全性
把敏感业务数据做端到端加密，防止被中间人窃取
把数据分布到一组服务器上，并在节点增减时把重新分布的数据量降到最小
优化单机数据库的索引结构，让单节点查询延迟更低
why:
一致性哈希是分布式系统的基础算法：解决「数据放哪台服务器」的问题，且在节点数量变化时只移动一小部分数据。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Consistent hashing distributes data across a cluster while minimizing how much data must move when servers are added or removed.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: Make the hash function's output harder to reverse or collide, improving cryptographic security.
Encrypt sensitive business data end to end so it cannot be intercepted.
Spread data across a set of servers while minimizing how much data must move when nodes join or leave.
Optimize a single database's index structure for lower query latency.

options: 复制（replication）
分片（sharding）
归档（archiving）
缓存（caching）
why:
分片是把数据水平拆分到多个实例；随之而来的第一个问题就是「哪条数据存到哪个实例」——这正是哈希分配策略要回答的。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Sharding means distributing data across multiple database instances, which raises the question of which data lives on which instance.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

几乎每个 key 的目标库都变了——绝大部分数据要跨库搬迁，所有实例负载暴涨

Almost every key's target database changes — most data must move across instances and load spikes everywhere.
Nothing needs to change; the database automatically adapts to the new modulo result.
Only about a quarter of the data moves, and it is all newly written data.

q: 一致性哈希的关键洞见是什么？
options: 换用密码学强度更高的哈希函数，减少碰撞概率
把所有数据复制到集群里的每一个节点，读写都本地完成
把数据和服务器节点都安排在同一个环形哈希空间（hash ring）上
用二叉搜索树按 key 范围组织节点，走树形路径查找
why: 核心思想：数据和数据库都映射到同一个圆环上；key 的归属由「环上顺时针遇到的第一个节点」决定，而不是由节点总数决定。
why_en: The key insight is to place both data and servers on a circular hash ring so ownership no longer depends on the total node count.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["hash key"] --> B["point on ring"]
  B --> C["walk clockwise"]
  C --> D["first node owns key"]
options_en: Switch to a cryptographically stronger hash function to reduce collisions.
Replicate all data to every node in the cluster so reads and writes stay local.
Place both data and server nodes on the same circular hash space, the hash ring.
Organize nodes in a binary search tree keyed by range and walk the tree to look up a key.

q: 补全一致性哈希的查找流程：
text: 先把 key 做哈希、定位到环上的一个点，然后沿{{顺时针}}方向走，遇到的第一个{{节点}}就是这个 key 的归属；节点增减时只有{{相邻区间}}的 key 需要移动。
why: 「环 + 顺时针找下一个节点」就是一致性哈希的全部核心；正因为归属只看相邻关系，节点变化的影响才是局部的。

q: 实际系统中，哈希环的取值空间通常是？
why:
0-100 只是教学简化；生产环境常用 0 到 2^32-1（约 43 亿个刻度）的哈希空间，刻度足够密，几百个虚拟节点也很少互相重合，分布仍然均匀。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Production hash rings typically span zero to two-to-the-32nd-minus-one so even hundreds of virtual nodes rarely collide and stay evenly spread.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: Zero to one hundred
Zero to two to the thirty-second power minus one
Zero to one thousand
Zero to two to the eighth power minus one

q: 虚拟节点（virtual nodes）是怎么实现的？
options: 为每个节点单独采购多台物理备用整机，接口层做故障转移热备份
把节点名加不同后缀（vn1、vn2…）分别哈希，让一台物理机出现在环上多个位置
提前把整个哈希环硬编码切分成固定的一百个等份格子，每个节点认领若干格
用虚拟化技术把每台物理机替换成若干独立运行的虚拟机实例
why: 一台物理节点 = 环上多个点：哈希「DB1-vn1」「DB1-vn2」等得到多个位置，各节点的虚拟节点自然交错混排在环上。
why_en: Each server is hashed under several name variants so it appears at many ring positions, naturally interleaving with other servers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["DB1 vnode A"] --> B["DB2 vnode A"]
  B --> C["DB1 vnode B"]
  C --> D["DB3 vnode A"]
options_en: Buy several extra physical standby machines per node and fail over at the interface layer.
Hash the node's name under different suffixes (vn1, vn2, ...) so one physical machine lands at multiple ring positions.
Pre-partition the whole ring into a hardcoded one hundred equal slots and have each node claim a share.
Use virtualization to replace each physical machine with several independently running virtual machines.

The whole hash ring must be rebuilt offline while every node recomputes its position.

The new node can join the ring but delay taking traffic until an operator flips it on.

The new node automatically becomes the cluster's primary once it joins the ring.

q: 「节点数变化时要移动多少数据」——取模哈希 vs 一致性哈希？
options: 两者在节点数变化时都会移动全部数据，没有本质差别
取模平均只移动约一半数据，一致性哈希反而要移动全部
取模几乎全量重排；一致性哈希只移动受影响相邻区间的 key（有界的一小部分）

q: 哪个查找逻辑是正确的一致性哈希？
options: node = nodes[hash(key) % len(nodes)]
node = 与 hash(key) 数值最接近的节点

pos = hash(key)，取环上从 pos 顺时针遇到的第一个节点（找不到则回绕到最小位置的节点）
why: 一致性哈希 = 在有序节点位置里找第一个 ≥ pos 的节点，越界则回绕到第一个；选项 A 是取模分片，「最接近」也不对——方向必须是顺时针。
why_en: Correct lookup finds the first node clockwise from the key's position, wrapping to the smallest position if none is larger.
whenOtherWins: 若用固定哈希槽方案（如 Redis Cluster 的 CRC16 mod 16384），查表槽位映射即可，不需要环上二分查找。
codeSample:
pos = hash(key) % RING_SIZE
# node_positions 已排序；找第一个 >= pos 的位置
idx = bisect_left(node_positions, pos)
node = ring_nodes[idx % len(ring_nodes)]  # 越界回绕到环起点

node = the node whose position is numerically closest to hash(key)

大多数分布式数据库把复制和一致性哈希配合：失效时靠现成副本顶上，不用搬数据

why: 副本预先跨可用区放好；主副本失效后 leader election 选新主、quorum 确认即可继续服务，不用搬数据；代价是切换瞬间有短暂延迟尖峰。

q: Cassandra 在环上是怎么复制数据的？
options: 只在主节点存一份，其余节点完全没有任何副本数据
每次写入都随机挑选几个节点复制，位置完全不固定
把数据复制到环上连续的 N 个节点，节点失效时由幸存副本继续提供读
把所有数据复制到集群里的每一台节点上存一份
why: 副本沿环顺时针存在连续 N 个节点上；某节点失效后，它负责的区间少了一份副本，但读写直接打到幸存副本继续服务；代价是容错余量下降，得尽快补齐副本数。
why_en: Replicas sit on N consecutive nodes around the ring, so a failed node just leaves one partition a replica short while reads and writes continue on the survivors, and the system needs to backfill a replica soon to restore its fault margin.

  B --> C["Next node replica"]
  C --> D["Next node replica"]

q: 既然故障靠副本顶，什么时候才会真的搬数据？

q: Redis Cluster 把 key 空间固定切成 16384 个槽，而不是切成 100 个或几百万个，这个数量级选择背后的设计考虑是什么？
options: 槽太少会让每槽覆盖太多 key、切分不精细；槽太多会让心跳传播的槽位图变笨重——16384 是折中
这只是历史遗留的随意选择，和心跳带宽、负载切分粒度都没有关系
槽数必须和物理节点数量完全相等，16384 意味着当年设计支持这么多节点
槽数越多每次写入越快，16384 恰好是让哈希计算耗时最短的数字
why:
16384 = 14 位槽位图，正好能塞进心跳包的合理大小；再大会让每次 gossip 传播的位图变笨重，再小则每个槽扛的 key 太多、负载切分不够细——这是 Redis 给出的折中点。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Redis picked 16384 slots as the sweet spot: enough granularity to split load finely, while keeping the per-node slot bitmap small enough to gossip in every heartbeat without bloating it.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: Redis Cluster 用 CRC16(key) mod 16384 决定槽位，每个节点通过 gossip 协议向其他节点广播自己认领的槽位图。
options_en: Too few slots means each slot covers too many keys and load-splitting is too coarse; too many slots makes the gossiped slot bitmap unwieldy — 16384 is the middle ground.
It's just an arbitrary legacy choice unrelated to heartbeat bandwidth or split granularity.
The slot count must exactly equal the physical node count; 16384 was the era's design ceiling for nodes.
More slots always means faster writes; 16384 happens to minimize hash computation time.

scenario_en: A CDN has K content URLs and N edge nodes. Nodes join and leave, and we do not want each membership change to remap most cached content.
q: CDN 内容映射该用简单取模还是一致性哈希？
q_en: Should CDN content mapping use simple modulo hashing or consistent hashing?
options: 用一个中心数据库记录每个 URL 具体存在哪个边缘节点上
每次请求都随机挑一个边缘节点去存放内容
按固定顺序轮询分配给各个边缘节点存放
一致性哈希：内容 URL 哈希到环上，就近顺时针归属边缘节点
why: 假设哈希均匀：取模从 N 加到 N+1，约 K×N/(N+1) 个 URL 会换节点；100 个节点加 1 个，接近 99% 会重映射。一致性哈希只让新节点接管一段环，平均搬 K/(N+1)。
why_en: With modulo hashing, adding one node remaps about K times N over N plus one keys, while consistent hashing moves only about K over N plus one keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点集合很小、几乎不变，简单取模或静态映射表也够用；一致性哈希主要赢在节点经常变化时。
options_en: A central database records exactly which edge node holds each URL.
Randomly pick an edge node to store the content each time.
Assign content to edge nodes in a fixed round-robin order.
Consistent hashing: hash the content URL onto the ring and assign it to the nearest clockwise edge node.

flowchart LR A["简单取模 hash(url) % N"] --> B["N 变 N+1"] B --> C["多数 URL 换节点
约 K×N/(N+1) 要搬"] D["一致性哈希环"] --> E["新节点插入一段区间"] E --> F["只搬相邻区间
约 K/(N+1) 要搬"]
tradeoff: 简单取模（实现最简单但节点变化时大搬家）vs 一致性哈希（实现复杂些但迁移量小）

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 hash(key) % N 选择节点；N 一变，旧 key 的余数关系也大多会变。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点放到同一个环上，key 归顺时针遇到的第一个节点；节点变化只影响相邻区间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places keys and nodes on one ring, assigning each key to the next clockwise node so membership changes affect only nearby ranges.

q: 补全一致性哈希的一句话总结：
text: 把数据和服务器都放到{{环}}上、沿{{顺时针}}走找归属节点；节点增减时只有{{相邻区间}}的数据需要移动，其余原地不动。
why: 实现细节可以复杂，核心图景极简：一个圆环 + 顺时针行走。这句话就是面试里 30 秒讲清一致性哈希的骨架。
why_en: Arrange everything on a ring and walk clockwise, so only the adjacent range of keys moves when membership changes.
q_en: Fill in the one-sentence summary of consistent hashing:
text_en: Put data and servers on a {{ring}}, walk {{clockwise}} to find the owner, and only the {{adjacent range}} moves when nodes join or leave.

q: 把「从取模分片演进到一致性哈希 + 虚拟节点」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 选型：一致性哈希——数据与节点放同一个环上，顺时针定位
缓解：虚拟节点把每个节点打散到环上多个位置，失效负载均摊
需求：数据分片到多台实例，且节点会因扩容/故障增减
残留代价：节点失效时其全部数据砸给唯一的顺时针邻居，负载翻倍
问题：取模哈希在节点数变化时几乎全量 key 重新映射
why: 需求（动态节点）→ 问题（取模全量重排）→ 选型（哈希环）→ 代价（邻居接盘过载）→ 缓解（虚拟节点）。这条链就是面试的标准叙事。
why_en: Dynamic membership breaks modulo hashing, the ring localizes movement, its neighbor-overload cost is then fixed by virtual nodes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求：节点会增减"] --> P["问题：取模几乎全量重排"]
    P --> C["选型：哈希环+顺时针"]
    C --> K["代价：失效负载砸给单个邻居"]
    K --> M["缓解：虚拟节点均摊"]
tradeoff: 取模哈希（简单但节点变化时全量搬迁）vs 一致性哈希+虚拟节点（局部搬迁+失效负载摊薄）

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash ring wraps the hash-value space into a circle onto which both data and nodes are mapped.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node technique hashes a physical server under several name variants so it occupies multiple ring positions for more even load.

q: 把「热点问题的识别与缓解」推理链排成正确顺序：
steps: 缓解：把热 key 复制到多个节点，读请求负载均衡（最常用）
现象：个别 key（如霉霉演唱会）流量是其他 key 的 100 倍
后果：承载热 key 的那个节点被流量打爆，成为热点
进阶：key 加盐打散，或自适应再均衡自动搬迁
认识：一致性哈希均衡的是 key 分布，不是流量
why: 现象（超热 key）→ 认识（哈希只均衡 key 不均衡流量）→ 后果（单节点被打爆）→ 缓解（复制读副本）→ 进阶（加盐/自适应）。
why_en: A wildly popular key overwhelms one node because hashing balances keys not traffic, mitigated first by replication and then by salting or adaptive rebalancing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个节点因承载了流量远超其他节点的 key 而被过度请求压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot spot is a node overwhelmed by disproportionate traffic because it holds an especially popular key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持有同一份数据只读拷贝的节点，用来分摊读请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica holds a read-only copy of the data used to spread out read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给热 key 追加随机后缀拆成多个物理 key，分散到不同节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key-space salting appends a random suffix to a hot key so it spreads across multiple physical keys and nodes.

scenario: 面试官追问：「你的分布式缓存节点挂了一台，怎么保证既不丢缓存价值又不搬大量数据？」
q: 最完整的回答思路是？
options: 把那台挂掉的节点直接重启，数据就能自动完整恢复
一致性哈希只影响该节点区间 + 虚拟节点把冲击摊薄 + 副本直接顶上，无需搬数据
把整个缓存集群的数据全部推倒重建一遍才能继续用
把全部流量临时切换到数据库，彻底绕开缓存层
why: 三层递进：环把影响局部化、虚拟节点把冲击摊薄、复制让故障处理零搬迁——这正是「一致性哈希与复制配合实现容错」的关系。
why_en: Combine the ring's localized impact, virtual nodes spreading the load, and replication so failures are absorbed without moving data.
whenOtherWins: 若数据可容忍全部重建（纯缓存、回源成本低），也可以接受简单方案：挂了就让相应 key 未命中、自然回填。
options_en: Just restart the failed node and its data recovers automatically and completely.
Consistent hashing limits impact to that node's range, virtual nodes spread the hit, and replicas take over directly with no data movement.
Tear down and rebuild the entire cache cluster's data before it can be used again.
Temporarily route all traffic to the database, bypassing the cache layer entirely.
tradeoff: 组合方案（环局部化+虚拟节点摊薄+副本零搬迁）vs 简单粗暴方案（全量重建或直接打库）

termDefinitions.meaning: 给一台物理服务器在环上生成多个哈希位置的技术，用来让负载分布更均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node technique hashes a physical server under several name variants so it occupies multiple ring positions for more even load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份数据的多个拷贝，分布在不同节点上用于容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a copy of the same data kept on a different node for fault tolerance.

适合缓存仍有副本、且要控制故障冲击面的场景。

The combined answer limits the range with the ring, spreads pressure with virtual nodes, and serves from replicas.
Full rebuild throws away cache value and warms everything again.
Bypassing the cache shifts the failure pressure to the database.
optionDirectness_en: Fits a temporary process hang where local data is still intact.
Fits when cache data has replicas and the failure blast radius must stay bounded.
Fits small systems where cache loss is acceptable and origin reads are cheap.
Only fits short emergency degradation if the database has enough headroom.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Here a real machine failure may not restart, and it does not explain low data movement.
Here survivors serve immediately and failed load is spread across several nodes.
Here many misses hit the origin and recovery latency rises.

q: 「关系型数据库不能扩展」这个说法，正确的评价是？
q_en: How should you evaluate the claim that relational databases cannot scale?
options: 完全正确，SQL 到百万用户必挂
SQL 确实无法做任何水平扩展
常被夸大：读副本/分片/缓存都能扩展 SQL
只有 NoSQL 才能上规模
options_en: Completely true — SQL always collapses once you hit a million users.
SQL genuinely cannot scale horizontally at all.
Often exaggerated: read replicas, sharding, and caching all scale SQL.
Only NoSQL can operate at that scale.
optionMeanings: 说关系型完全无法扩展、一定会在百万用户时挂掉
关系型数据库从根本上无法做任何形式的水平扩展

只有 NoSQL 技术栈能支持大规模应用
optionMeanings_en: Relational databases absolutely cannot scale and will crash by a million users.
SQL can never do any form of horizontal scaling.
Relational can scale via read replicas, sharding, connection pooling, and caching; Facebook and Airbnb are built on relational foundations.

optionDirectness: 百万级并不会让 SQL 自动失效，瓶颈要看查询和架构

NoSQL 只在模型或规模信号明确时才值得替换默认 SQL
optionDirectness_en: A million users do not automatically break SQL; the bottleneck depends on queries and architecture.
Read replicas, sharding, and caching all give relational systems room to scale.
Use relational as the default, then add read or write scaling for bottlenecks.

optionScenarioImpacts: 这种绝对化说法会被认为是过度简化，没有理解关系型的实际能力

你展示了对关系型扩展方式的深入理解，显得成熟理性
这种说法是误导——NoSQL 有自己的问题，关系型在大厂仍是主流
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This absolute claim sounds simplistic and shows you don't understand relational's real capabilities.
Another absolute — you ignore how relational databases scale when paired with good architecture.
You demonstrate mature understanding of relational scaling techniques and cite real examples.
This claim misleads — NoSQL has its own tradeoffs, and major companies still rely on SQL.
why:
扩展性短板被夸大了：配合读副本、分片、连接池和缓存，关系型撑起了世界级大厂。扩展靠的是围绕数据库的架构，不只是数据库本身。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
The scalability knock on SQL is exaggerated: with read replicas, sharding, pooling, and caching, companies like Facebook and Airbnb run on relational foundations.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 索引不是免费的。它的代价包括哪些？（多选）

q: 补全面试常考的索引家族：
text: 通用默认用 {{B 树}}；极端写入负载用 {{LSM 树}} 存储引擎；纯精确匹配可用 {{哈希}} 索引；经纬度邻近搜索用 {{地理空间}} 索引；全文搜索用 {{倒排}} 索引。
why: 五类索引各解一类问题：B 树是万金油，LSM 吃写入，哈希只做等值，地理空间管 2D 邻近，倒排管文本。面试先想清楚查询形态再选。
why_en: B-trees are the default, LSM trees serve write-heavy workloads, hash indexes do exact matches, geospatial indexes handle proximity, and inverted indexes power text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写的存储引擎，靠内存缓冲和后台合并优化写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a storage engine that turns random writes into sequential writes using an in-memory buffer and background merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

q: B 树节点的大小通常被设计成正好匹配什么？
options: 一个磁盘页，典型为 8KB
一个 CPU 缓存行（64 字节）
一个内存页（4KB 固定）
整个表的大小
why:
8KB 是磁盘页这个硬件给定值，不是公式推导出来的；B 树节点对齐它，一次 I/O 正好读满一个节点，这是后续对比 LSM/哈希索引 I/O 效率的基准。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Eight kilobytes is a given hardware constant, not a derived number; aligning B-tree nodes to it means one I/O reads one full node, the baseline for later I/O comparisons.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: 面试官追问：为什么 Postgres 把 B 树节点大小固定设计成这个数字，而不是随便选。

text: 新写入先进内存中的 {{memtable}}（有序结构）；同时为持久性顺序追加到 {{WAL}}（预写日志）；memtable 写满后冻结、整体刷盘成不可变的 {{SSTable}}；后台的 {{compaction}} 进程定期合并文件、清理重复和已删除条目。

（内存有序结构）"] W --> L["WAL 顺序追加
（持久性）"] M -->|写满冻结| S["SSTable

全内存没有磁盘 I/O 要迁就，哈希 O(1) 优势兑现
因为哈希表占用的内存比 B 树更少
因为这个场景需要支持范围查询
why: 哈希索引的甜蜜点是内存数据库：Redis 主结构就是哈希表，MySQL MEMORY 引擎默认哈希索引。一旦涉及磁盘，B 树对 I/O 更友好，通常更优。
why_en: Hash structures shine for in-memory stores like Redis and MySQL's MEMORY engine where exact-match lookups dominate and there is no disk I/O pattern to optimize for.
whenOtherWins: 数据落磁盘时选 B 树——它对磁盘 I/O 模式的处理效率更高，等值也几乎不慢。
options_en: Because a B-tree simply cannot be built in memory at all.
With no disk I/O pattern to optimize for, hashing's O(1) advantage pays off.
Because a hash table uses less memory than a B-tree.
Because this scenario needs to support range queries.
tradeoff: 内存中等值查找速度 vs 磁盘场景下的范围查询灵活性

q: 给 latitude、longitude 各建一个 B 树索引来做「5 英里内的餐厅」，为什么行不通？
options: 因为 B 树不支持 DECIMAL 数值类型
因为两个索引会互相冲突报错
两个 1D 索引解 2D 问题：交集还是大矩形
经纬度字段根本不能建立索引
why: 先用纬度索引会命中全球同纬度长条上的所有点；两个索引求交则得到远大于目标圆的矩形结果集。2D 邻近问题需要理解空间关系的索引。
why_en: Two separate one-dimensional B-trees cannot solve a two-dimensional proximity problem: the latitude range is a strip around the globe, and intersecting both indexes yields a rectangle far larger than the search circle.

q: geohash 的核心思想是什么？
options: 把地球投影到平面网格再取模
递归四等分区域并编码，2D 变 1D 字符串
给每个城市分配一个随机数字 ID
用 R 树的矩形逐个包裹坐标点
why: 想象把世界四等分并标号，再对每格继续四等分——geohash 就是这个过程的 base32 编码。近处的两家餐厅往往共享「9q8yyk」这样的前缀。
why_en: Geohash recursively subdivides the world and base32-encodes the path, turning a 2D location into a 1D string where nearby places usually share a prefix.
options_en: Project the earth onto a flat grid and take a modulo.
Recursively quarter regions and encode them, turning 2D into a 1D string.
Assign every city a random numeric ID.
Wrap each coordinate one by one in an R-tree rectangle.

q: geohash 的「真正优雅之处」在于它和什么老朋友的组合？

哈希索引：O(1) 定位任何坐标

why: 2D 坐标变成有序字符串后，B 树擅长的前缀匹配和范围扫描恰好就是邻近搜索所需；半径查询再补扫相邻单元格即可。复用现有 B 树设施是它流行的根本原因。
why_en: Once locations become ordered strings, a regular B-tree handles proximity search as simple prefix range scans, plus a few adjacent cells for radius queries.
options_en: Index geohash strings with a B-tree; proximity search becomes a prefix scan.
Bloom filters: probabilistically rule out far-away points.
Hash indexes: locate any coordinate in O(1).
LSM trees: absorb high-frequency location updates.

q: 当前推荐使用哪条命令做半径搜索？
options: GEORADIUS restaurants -122.4194 37.7749 5 mi
GET restaurants:nearby:precomputed:list
GEOSEARCH restaurants FROMLONLAT -122.4194 37.7749 BYRADIUS 5 mi
ZRANGEBYSCORE restaurants:distances 0 5
why: GEOSEARCH 是现行推荐（GEORADIUS 已废弃），配合 GEOADD 写入坐标；Redis 底层用 geohash 高效找出附近的点。
why_en: Use GEOSEARCH with FROMLONLAT and BYRADIUS since GEORADIUS is deprecated, and Redis implements these geo commands with geohash under the hood.
whenOtherWins: 在 Postgres 生态里做同样的事，则用 PostGIS 的 R 树系空间索引；需要更灵活的形状（多边形、路网）时 R 树更合适。
codeSample:
GEOADD restaurants -122.4194 37.7749 "Restaurant A"
GEOSEARCH restaurants FROMLONLAT -122.4194 37.7749 BYRADIUS 5 mi

GET on a single precomputed key called restaurants:nearby.

q: 把「浏览器输入 URL 到拿到网页」的步骤排成正确顺序：

steps: TCP 三次握手建立连接
DNS 把域名解析成 IP 地址
服务器处理请求并准备响应
客户端发送 HTTP GET 请求
TCP 四次挥手关闭连接
服务器发回 HTTP 响应
why: DNS 解析 → TCP 握手 → 发请求 → 服务器处理（多数工程师唯一控制的延迟）→ 回响应 → 挥手断开。一次「简单」请求背后是多轮包交换，层层都有延迟。
why_en: A web request resolves DNS, performs the TCP handshake, sends the HTTP request, waits for server processing, receives the response, and tears the connection down.

    C->>S: HTTP GET
    S-->>C: HTTP 响应

q: 补全 TCP 三次握手：
q_en: Complete the TCP three-way handshake.
text: 客户端发 {{SYN}} 请求连接；服务器回 {{SYN-ACK}} 确认请求；客户端再发 {{ACK}} 完成连接建立。断开则用 FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK 四次挥手。
why: 三次握手建立、四次挥手拆除——每个不复用连接的请求都要重复这套流程，这是后面讨论持久连接和负载均衡的伏笔。
why_en: TCP opens with a SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake and closes with a four-way FIN and ACK exchange.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: SYN
    S-->>C: SYN-ACK
    C->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 连接已建立

q: UDP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does UDP have?
options: 无连接：没有握手和连接建立，开销小、延迟低

No delivery guarantee: a lost packet triggers no notification.
No ordering guarantee: packets can arrive out of order.
Automatic deduplication with exactly-once delivery.

why: 实时音视频、在线游戏、DNS 查询都是 UDP 的主场：应用能自行处理偶发丢包/乱序，低延迟远比完整重传值钱。

options_en: TCP, to guarantee every audio packet arrives.
QUIC, and wait for it to become mainstream.
UDP: speed over reliability, and the client absorbs the occasional loss.
HTTP polling.

optionMeanings: TCP：可靠传输协议，握手建连、丢包重传。

why:
UDP 头固定 8B；TCP 基础头 20B，带 options 可到 60B。这个数字的用途不是背诵，而是提醒你：TCP 用额外字节和状态换可靠性、流控、拥塞控制。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
UDP's 8-byte header versus TCP's 20-to-60-byte header is a reminder that TCP pays extra bookkeeping for reliability, flow control, and congestion control.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: HTTPS 在 HTTP 之上加了什么？
q_en: What does HTTPS add on top of HTTP?
options: TLS/SSL 安全层：加密防窃听
压缩层
缓存层
负载均衡层
why:
HTTPS = HTTP + TLS/SSL，请求响应内容在传输中被加密。做公开网站，用 HTTPS 没有商量余地。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
HTTPS adds a TLS security layer that encrypts communications against eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks, and public websites use it without exception.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: A TLS/SSL security layer that encrypts against eavesdropping.
A compression layer.
A caching layer.
A load-balancing layer.

q: HTTPS 加密了传输内容，但一个常见的安全错误依然存在——是什么？
q_en: What common security mistake still exists even when HTTPS encrypts traffic in transit?
options: 忘记续期证书
用了太旧的 TLS 版本
把密码明文写在 URL 里
信任请求体内容，如直接用 user ID 查库
why:
加密保护「传输中」不被偷看，但不保证内容是你的客户端生成的。API 永远不要信任未经校验的请求体，也别索要你无法验证的东西。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Encryption does not make request contents trustworthy, so never use an unvalidated user id from the request body or an attacker can read arbitrary data.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

Using an outdated TLS version.
Putting a password in plaintext in the URL.
Trusting the request body's contents, like using a raw user id to query the database.

q: 同一个 {id, name} 对象，JSON 与 protobuf 的编码大小对比约是？
q_en: For the same {id, name} object, roughly how do JSON and protobuf sizes compare?
options: JSON 15 字节，protobuf 40 字节
两者一样大

why:
带内嵌字段名的 JSON 40 字节，protobuf 二进制 15 字节：空间更小、解析 CPU 更省。这是 gRPC 高吞吐的底层原因。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
The same object takes about forty bytes as JSON but fifteen as protobuf, and benchmarks show up to ten times the throughput of JSON over HTTP.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 补全 WebRTC 的三大基础设施角色：
q_en: Fill in the three infrastructure roles behind WebRTC.
text: {{信令服务器}}记录哪些 peer 可用及其连接信息；{{STUN}} 用「打洞」等技术帮 peer 获得公网可路由的地址和端口；{{TURN}} 是中继兜底——直连失败时把流量经中央服务器转发。
why: 多数客户端在 NAT 之后、不接受入站连接，直连没那么容易：信令服务器牵线，STUN 打洞，实在不行 TURN 中继。
why_en: A signaling server tracks available peers, STUN performs NAT hole punching to obtain routable addresses, and TURN relays traffic when direct connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直连失败时用中央服务器中继流量的兜底方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TURN is the fallback that relays traffic through a central server when a direct peer-to-peer connection fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台内网设备共享一个公网 IP 的机制，也让它们默认不接受入站连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NAT lets many devices on a private network share one public IP, which is also why they cannot normally accept inbound connections.

q: 垂直扩展 vs 水平扩展，以及面试中的现实是？
q_en: How should you compare vertical and horizontal scaling in interviews?
options: 垂直=加机器，水平=换大机器
垂直换大机器，水平加机器；面试常见水平扩展
两者完全一样
水平扩展不需要负载均衡
why:
现代硬件强到「几台大机器顶过去几千台小机器」，但面试的常规剧本还是水平扩展。往白板上加机器前，得先回答「客户端跟谁说话」——即负载均衡。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Vertical scaling means bigger servers and horizontal means more servers, and while modern hardware favors vertical, interviews almost always end up horizontal with load balancing.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: Vertical means adding more machines, horizontal means switching to a bigger machine.
Vertical means a bigger machine, horizontal means more machines; interviews mostly land on horizontal.
The two are completely identical.
Horizontal scaling never needs a load balancer.
tradeoff: 垂直扩展简单但有上限 vs 水平扩展无上限但要做负载均衡

q_en: How does Redis Cluster demonstrate client-side load balancing?
options: 哈希 key 直连，错了收到 MOVED

q: 负载均衡器靠什么实现自动故障转移（高可用的关键）？

重启所有服务器
把流量全部缓存
why: LB 不只分流量，还持续监控后端健康：服务器崩溃或断电就停止向它路由，恢复了再加回来。检测并绕开故障、无需人工干预——这是 LB 之于高可用的价值。
why_en: Load balancers run health checks, like TCP connection tests or HTTP checks expecting a 200, and automatically route around servers that fail until they recover.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    LB["LB"] -->|健康检查| A["Server A OK"]
    LB -->|健康检查失败| B["Server B"]
    B -.摘除.-> X["不接流量"]
    A --> U["用户请求"]
options_en: A human manually flips traffic over.
Health checks: a TCP or L7 probe for liveness.
Restart every server.
Cache all the traffic.

GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: backend-3

HTTP/1.1 200 OK   # 健康，继续接流量

q: 补全常见负载均衡算法：
q_en: Fill in the common load-balancing algorithms.
text: {{Round Robin}}：按顺序轮流分发；Random：随机分发；{{Least Connections}}：发给活跃连接最少的服务器；Least Response Time：发给响应最快的；{{IP Hash}}：按客户端 IP 决定服务器，可用于会话保持。

q: 负载均衡算法该选？
q_en: Which load-balancing algorithm should you choose for many persistent connections?
options: 永远用轮询
IP Hash
最少连接
随机
why: 长连接不像短请求会自然消散：轮询下先起的服务器会一直背着旧连接。按活跃连接数分发能防止单机被长连接慢慢压满。

IP hash.
Least connections.
Random.
tradeoff: Least Connections 防止长连接堆积 vs Round Robin 简单够用

q: 光速给纽约-伦敦的往返延迟定了什么物理下限？
q_en: What round-trip latency lower bound does the speed of light impose between New York and London?
options: 约 1ms
往返理论最低约 56ms
约 500ms
没有物理下限，取决于带宽
why:
还没算任何处理时间，物理就先收走 56ms。这条硬约束是低延迟应用必须做地理分布的根本原因——你无法优化光速。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Light in fiber travels at about two thirds of light speed, so a New York to London round trip has a theoretical floor of roughly fifty-six milliseconds.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

tradeoff: 粗粒度区域路由 vs 细粒度空间索引
why:
先按城市或区域把请求路由到本地分片，再在本地分片里做附近搜索。geohash 没错，但它通常是第二层：用于在迈阿密分片内找附近司机。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
First route the request to the city or regional shard, then run proximity search inside that local shard. Geohash is useful, but usually as the second layer.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 若数据必须全球共享（社交关系图、全球排行榜），不能只查本地分片；需要复制、缓存或跨区查询来处理全局视图。

q: 「数据局部性（data locality）」原则的内容是？
q_en: What does the data locality principle mean?
options: 数据必须存在本地磁盘
整个计算领域通用：数据离计算越近越快
每个国家一份数据副本
数据只能有一份
why: LA↔NY 约 4,000km，光纤约 200,000km/s，单程物理下限约 20ms、RTT 至少约 40ms；真实路径还会更高。数据局部性就是让一次查询需要的数据彼此靠近，并尽量靠近用户。
why_en: Data locality means keeping query data close together and near the user; LA to New York already has roughly a 40ms round-trip lower bound before routing and queueing.
options_en: Data must live on local disk.
A principle across computing: the closer data is to the computation, the faster it runs.
Every country needs its own data replica.
There can only ever be one copy of the data.

q: 分布式系统「最危险的假设」是哪条？正确的心态是什么？
q_en: What is the most dangerous assumption in distributed systems, and what mindset should replace it?

「时钟是同步的」
「用户是理性的」

why: 服务器会崩、比特会被宇宙射线翻转、光缆会被挖断。健壮的设计不是假设失败不发生，而是把失败当作常态来规划。

scenario: 下游服务偶发瞬时故障（临时变慢、偶尔超时），面试官问你怎么处理。
scenario_en: A downstream service has transient failures such as temporary slowness or occasional timeouts, and the interviewer asks how you handle them.
q: 面试官在等的「魔法短语」是？
q_en: What magic phrase is the interviewer looking for when downstream calls fail transiently?
options: 重启服务
换一个下游服务
指数退避重试
把超时设成无限大
why: 超时+重试是处理瞬时失败的基本卫生。指数退避给系统喘息、避免重试风暴；这个短语面试官明确在等，senior 级别要能展开讲 jitter。
why_en: Interviewers are often looking for the magic phrase retry with exponential backoff, and senior candidates should be ready to elaborate on adding jitter.
whenOtherWins: 被重试的 API 若非幂等（如扣款），先解决幂等性（幂等键），否则重试会造成重复副作用。

flowchart LR
    A["第 1 次"] -->|失败| B["等 100ms"]
    B --> C["第 2 次"]
    C -->|失败| D["等 200ms"]
    D --> E["第 3 次"]
    E -->|失败| F["等更久"]
options_en: Restart the service.
Switch to a different downstream service.
Retry with exponential backoff.
Set the timeout to infinity.
tradeoff: 立即重试快但可能雪上加霜 vs 退避慢一点但给系统喘息

q: 重试为什么是「双刃剑」？
q_en: Why are retries a double-edged sword?
options: 大量重试会反复冲击注定失败的请求，加剧问题

why: 对一个已经趴下的服务疯狂重试等于持续补刀。退避把重试的压力摊薄到时间上，把「雪上加霜」变成「给它时间恢复」。
why_en: Aggressive retries can hammer an already failing service and make things worse, which is why backoff waits progressively longer between attempts.
options_en: A flood of retries keeps hammering a request that's doomed to fail, making things worse.
Retries cause encryption to fail.
Retries only work on single-machine systems.
Retries make a single request faster.

q: 退避策略里为什么必须掺入随机性（jitter）？
q_en: Why must a backoff strategy include jitter?
options: 为了让日志更好看
防止所有客户端同一时刻同步重试
为了绕过限流
随机性能提升单个请求成功率
why: 没有 jitter，指数退避会让所有客户端的重试波峰完美对齐、一次次齐射。加随机把波峰摊平，才真正给系统留出恢复窗口。
why_en: Jitter adds randomness so clients do not synchronize their retries into repeated simultaneous bursts hammering the service like a jackhammer.
options_en: To make the logs look nicer.
It stops every client from synchronizing their retries at the same instant.
To bypass rate limiting.
Randomness improves a single request's odds of success.

q: 支付接口 charge $10 遇到重试，怎么防止把用户扣成 $20 甚至 $2,000？
q_en: How do you prevent a retried $10 charge from becoming $20 or $2,000?
options: 禁止一切重试
每次重试前人工确认
引入幂等键：请求的唯一标识，服务端靠它去重
扣款后立刻退款
why: 读天然幂等（GET），写要自己构造幂等：幂等键让服务器识别重复请求。友好的实现会等首个请求完成后把结果发给所有等待者，不友好的直接报「请求已存在」——但都不会重复扣款。
why_en: An idempotency key uniquely identifies the request so the server processes it only once, preventing retries from double charging the user.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: pay(key=K)
    S-->>C: timeout
    C->>S: retry pay(key=K)
    S-->>C: 返回同一结果
    Note over S: K 已处理，不重复扣款
options_en: Forbid all retries.
Require manual confirmation before every retry.
Introduce an idempotency key that uniquely identifies the request so the server can dedupe.
Immediately refund the charge after it succeeds.
codeSample:
POST /payments HTTP/1.1
Idempotency-Key: user_42_2026-07-02

# 服务端记录该 key 的处理结果；同一个 key 重试直接返回首次结果，不再扣款

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一次请求的唯一键，服务端靠它识别并拒绝重复执行同一请求。

失败超过阈值，熔断器「跳闸」进入 open 状态
超时之后，电路转入 half-open 半开状态
why: 监控 → 跳闸 → 快速失败 → 半开 → 试探定夺。灵感来自电气熔断器：防止级联故障蔓延，并给故障服务恢复时间。
why_en: A circuit breaker monitors failures, trips open past a threshold, fails fast while open, moves to half-open after a timeout, and a test request decides whether to close.
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Closed: 正常调用
    Closed --> Open: 失败超过阈值，跳闸
    Open --> HalfOpen: 超时后半开
    HalfOpen --> Closed: 试探成功
    HalfOpen --> Open: 试探失败

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控对某依赖的失败率，超阈值后让请求快速失败而不再真的调用，给依赖恢复时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker monitors failures against a dependency and, past a threshold, fails requests fast instead of calling it, giving the dependency time to recover.

q: 熔断器带来哪些好处？（多选）
q_en: What benefits does a circuit breaker provide?
options: 快速失败：立刻拒绝而不是干等超时，UI 有快速兜底而非挂死
减负：不再向已经挣扎的服务倾泻更多请求
自愈：不放全量流量的情况下自动试探恢复；隔离故障、防止蔓延到整个系统
提升下游服务的最大吞吐量
why: 熔断器的价值：fail fast、给故障服务减压、半开态自动试探、把一处故障圈起来不扩散。它不会让下游更快——只是不再补刀。
why_en: Circuit breakers fail fast, reduce load on struggling services, self-heal by testing recovery, and keep one failure from cascading through the system.
options_en: Fail fast: reject immediately instead of waiting out a timeout, so the UI gets a quick fallback instead of hanging.
Reduce load: stop pouring more requests onto an already struggling service.
Self-heal by automatically probing recovery without full traffic, and isolate the failure so it doesn't cascade through the whole system.
Increase the downstream service's maximum throughput.

scenario: 数据库冷宕机后需要逐实例重启，但重试洪峰和愤怒用户的流量把第一个实例反复压趴（thundering herd）——第一台永远起不来，整库无法恢复。
scenario_en: After a database cold outage, instances must restart one by one, but retry floods and user traffic keep crushing the first instance before recovery can progress.
q: 预防这类级联故障的关键模式是？
q_en: What pattern prevents this cascading failure during database recovery?
options: 增加更多重试
调大数据库连接池
换更快的数据库
熔断器：超阈值后停止真实调用、快速失败
why: 「一个故障制造出新的故障」是级联故障的标志——识别这些模式并给出缓解，是面试脱颖而出的好方法（也是 3am oncall 的血泪结晶）。
why_en: A circuit breaker stops the retry firehose so the recovering database gets breathing room, preventing the thundering herd from pinning it down forever.
whenOtherWins: 偶发的瞬时失败用「重试+指数退避」就够；熔断器针对的是持续性故障与级联风险。
options_en: Add even more retries.
Enlarge the database connection pool.
Switch to a faster database.
A circuit breaker that stops real calls and fails fast past a failure threshold.
tradeoff: 持续重试雪上加霜 vs 熔断给恢复窗口
optionMeanings: 增加更多重试：会加剧 thundering herd。
调大连接池：治标不治本，冲击照样压向第一台实例。
换更快的数据库：没有解决「重试洪峰持续冲击」这个根因。
熔断器：超阈值后停止真实调用，给恢复窗口。
optionDirectness: 方向反了：更多重试正是制造 thundering herd 的原因，不是解法。
资源代价错了：连接池再大，愤怒重试流量还是会把第一个刚起来的实例打死。
方向错了：这是在优化性能而不是控制请求量，无法阻止级联故障。
抓住了关键差异：熔断器直接切断了「故障→更多请求→更严重故障」的反馈环。

q: 熔断器适合安插在哪些位置？（多选）
q_en: Where should circuit breakers be placed?
options: 对第三方外部 API 的调用
数据库连接与查询
微服务之间的服务间调用；以及任何可能失败或变慢的网络调用/重操作
进程内的纯内存函数调用
why: 原则：凡是跨网络、可能失败或变慢的依赖调用都值得熔断保护。进程内纯内存计算没有网络故障模式，不需要熔断器。
why_en: Place circuit breakers around third-party API calls, database queries, service-to-service communication, and any network call that could fail or slow down.
options_en: Calls to third-party external APIs.
Database connections and queries.
Service-to-service calls between microservices, and any network call or heavy operation that could fail or slow down.
Pure in-process, in-memory function calls.
tradeoff: 跨网络易失败的调用要熔断 vs 进程内内存调用不需要

scenario: 一个直播评论系统写入量约 5k WPS；调优良好的单机 Postgres 简单写入参考值是 20k+ WPS。
scenario_en: A live-comments system writes about 5k WPS; a well-tuned single Postgres can handle 20k+ simple WPS.
q: 这组数字最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision do these numbers support?
options: 5k WPS 远低于单机上限，先别急着分库分表
只要用关系型数据库就必须提前分片
写吞吐超过 1k 就该换 NoSQL
写吞吐低就可以不建索引
why:
20k+ WPS 是单机 Postgres 简单写入的参考上限，5k 远在其内；此时分库分片是过度设计，应先看事务复杂度和索引写放大。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A well-tuned single Postgres handles 20k+ simple writes per second, so 5k WPS does not justify sharding yet.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: 5k WPS is well under the single-node ceiling, so don't shard yet.
Any relational database must be pre-sharded.
Switch to NoSQL once writes pass 1k per second.
Skip indexes because write volume is low.

scenario: 系统写入约 5k WPS，候选人立刻想加消息队列来「缓冲这么高的写吞吐」。
scenario_en: The system writes about 5k WPS, and a candidate immediately wants a queue to buffer that write rate.
q: 这个判断的问题在于？
q_en: What is wrong with that judgment?
options: 对，5k WPS 必须马上加队列缓冲
错，单机 20k+ WPS 能扛，加队列过度设计
错，应直接分库分表而非加队列
错，应直接换成 NoSQL 存储
why:
5k WPS 远在单机 Postgres 20k+ 的能力之内，加队列是过度设计。先考虑批量写、优化索引/schema、连接池、异步提交等更简单手段。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
At 5k writes per second a message queue is over-engineering, since a single Postgres handles 20k+; simpler tuning suffices.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 当需要可靠投递（下游故障不丢）、事件溯源、写尖峰超过单机能力（>20k WPS），或要解耦生产者/消费者时，队列才真正值得。

No, a single node handles 20k+ WPS; adding a queue is over-engineering.
No, you should shard the database directly.
No, you should switch to NoSQL instead.

scenario: 一个订单详情页用主键查询 Postgres；同样的行有时命中缓存，有时要走磁盘。
scenario_en: An order-detail page reads Postgres by primary key; the row may be cached or may require disk access.
q: 这组延迟量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision do these latency numbers support?
options: 数据库读取一定比网络调用慢
磁盘查询几乎和缓存一样快，无需区分
带索引的简单行查询已够快，不必单独加缓存层
只有加了缓存才能做到毫秒级读取
why:
缓存命中约 1-5ms，磁盘读约 5-30ms，带索引的简单行查询本身已是毫秒级；为它单独加缓存层往往是多余复杂度。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Indexed lookups are already 1-5ms cached or 5-30ms from disk, so adding a cache just for simple row reads is often unnecessary.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: A database read is always slower than a network call.
Disk reads are basically as fast as cache hits.
Indexed simple lookups are already fast enough without a dedicated cache.
Only a cache can achieve millisecond-level reads.

scenario: 一个电商订单服务预计稳定在 8k TPS 读写；候选人在判断要不要一开始就上多主分布式数据库。
scenario_en: An e-commerce order service expects a steady 8k TPS of reads and writes, and the candidate is considering multi-primary distribution upfront.
q: 这组吞吐量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision do these throughput numbers support?
options: 8k TPS 已经远超单机数据库能力
TPS 越高越说明必须换 NoSQL
读写吞吐和实例规格无关
单机 Aurora/RDS 吞吐够用，不必上分布式
why:
单机 Aurora/RDS 读最高约 50k TPS、写约 10-20k TPS；8k TPS 在这之内，先调优单机比一开始上分布式更直接。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A single Aurora or RDS node reaches up to 50k read TPS and 10-20k write TPS, so 8k TPS fits comfortably without going distributed.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: 8k TPS already exceeds a single database's capacity.
Higher TPS always means you must switch to NoSQL.
Read/write throughput has nothing to do with instance size.
Single-node Aurora or RDS throughput is enough; skip distributed.

why_en:
Most engines handle up to 64 TiB per instance, and Aurora up to 256 TiB, so 8TB is nowhere near the limit that would force sharding.

A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

A single database instance tops out around 100GB, so it's overdue.
Cloud databases have no real storage ceiling at all.
More storage always means slower reads.

scenario: 要判断一个关系型数据库是否该分片（sharding）。
scenario_en: You are deciding whether a relational database has reached the point where sharding is justified.
q: 下面哪个才是真正该考虑分片的信号？
q_en: Which signal truly justifies considering sharding?
options: 数据量约 500GB，还远没到瓶颈
数据量近 50TiB 或写吞吐超 10k TPS
用户规模刚到 100 万出头
系统开始出现了 JOIN 查询
why:
分片信号是硬指标：数据量近 50TiB、写持续 >10k TPS、跨地域或备份窗口过长。仅几百 GB 或百万用户远不够格。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Consider sharding when data nears 50 TiB or write throughput exceeds 10k TPS, not merely at a few hundred gigabytes or a million users.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 在这些硬指标出现前，先用只读副本、索引优化、缓存等手段——它们比分片简单得多。
tradeoff: 硬扩展指标（数据量/吞吐/合规） vs 表面信号（用户数/GB 数/查询语法）
options_en: About 500GB of data, still nowhere near a limit.
Data nears 50TiB, or write throughput exceeds 10k TPS.
The product just reached one million users.
The team started using JOIN queries.

scenario: 面试者一上来就说要给主键查询加缓存层，理由是数据库延迟太高。
scenario_en: A candidate proposes caching primary-key lookups immediately because they assume database reads are too slow.

q_en: Where is this reasoning wrong?
options: SSD 查询要几百毫秒，必须加缓存
所有查询都该无脑加缓存
数据库根本做不了主键查询
索引主键查询已是毫秒级，无需单独加缓存
why:
带索引的简单行查询是亚毫秒到几毫秒，已经很快；为它单独加缓存层是多余复杂度。复杂 join/聚合查询仍值得缓存。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Indexed row lookups are sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds, so adding a cache just for them is unnecessary infrastructure.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 如果是跨多表 join、聚合的昂贵查询，那仍然值得缓存——快的只是「带索引的简单行查询」。

why_en:

q_en: What design decision do these network latency numbers support?
options: 跨大洲和同 AZ 延迟基本没区别
只要同区，延迟就一定 <1ms
网络延迟和可用区划分无关
同区跨 AZ 延迟仍在 1-2ms，是可靠的默认架构
why:
同 AZ 内 <1ms，同区跨 AZ 1-2ms，跨区域 50-150ms；这组数字支撑了同区多 AZ 部署这种可靠架构。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Latency is under a millisecond within an AZ, 1-2ms across AZs in a region, and 50-150ms cross-region, which supports multi-AZ deployment as a reliable default.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: Cross-continent and same-AZ latency are basically the same.
As long as it's the same region, latency is always under 1ms.
Network latency has nothing to do with AZ layout.
Cross-AZ latency within a region stays at 1-2ms, a reliable default architecture.

scenario: 评估要不要在现有系统里引入消息队列。
scenario_en: You are evaluating whether the current system truly needs a message queue.
q: 消息队列在什么情况下才「真正值得」引入？（多选）
q_en: When is a message queue truly worth introducing? (Select all that apply.)
options: 需要可靠投递：下游故障时消息不丢
事件溯源 / 数据集成等模式
写尖峰超过单机数据库能力（如 >20k WPS）或要解耦生产者与消费者
稳定 5k WPS 的简单插入
why:
队列值得用在：可靠投递、事件溯源、超过单机能力的写尖峰、生产/消费解耦。稳定 5k WPS 的简单写单机就够，不该为它加队列。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Queues are justified by guaranteed delivery, event sourcing, write spikes beyond a single database, or decoupling, not by a steady 5k WPS.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
tradeoff: 真正值得引入队列的硬需求 vs 尚在单机能力内的写量

Event-sourcing or data-integration patterns.

A steady 5k WPS of simple inserts.

q: 把「决定要不要分片」的正确思考顺序排好：
q_en: Put the decision steps for whether to shard in the right order:
steps: 先给出数据模型和规模（条数、每条大小、TPS）
做算术：估出总数据量与读写吞吐的量级
对照单机能力（约 50 TiB、10k+ WPS、50k 读 TPS）
只有超出单机能力时才分片，否则保持单机 + 副本
why:
反过来做（先讲怎么分片）是最常见的错误。正确顺序：给规模 → 做算术 → 对照单机上限 → 真超了才分片。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Decide sharding by stating the scale, doing the math, comparing to single-node limits, and only then sharding if exceeded.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Inputs["records x size x QPS"] --> Math["order math"]
    Math --> Limit["compare limits"]
    Limit --> Decision["simple vs shard"]
tradeoff: 先算术验证单机上限 vs 直接假设需要分片

scenario: 一个团队只用一台数据库主实例，没有分片，正在讨论这是不是单点故障。
scenario_en: A team uses one primary database instance without sharding and is debating whether that automatically means a single point of failure.
q: 「单实例数据库」是否就等于单点故障（SPOF）？
q_en: Does a single database instance automatically mean a SPOF?
options: 是，单实例必然是单点故障
只有分片才能避免单点
不是，主库+只读副本能做高可用
副本反而会降低可用性
why:
「不分片」不等于「单点」：主库 + 只读副本（如 Aurora 多 AZ 故障转移）就能做高可用；HA 复制与 scale 分片是两回事。

scenario: 缓存估算给定锚点：命中延迟约 1ms、单实例约 100k+ ops/s、内存可达约 1TB。
scenario_en: Cache-estimation anchors are about 1ms hit latency, roughly 100k+ ops/s per instance, and up to about 1TB of memory.
q: 这些缓存数字约束哪个扩容判断？
q_en: What scaling judgment do these cache numbers constrain?
text: 这些数字说明：数据集接近 1TB 前先别按内存分片；真正要盯的是 {{ops/s 或网络带宽}}，延迟目标低到亚毫秒时才考虑 {{加节点或分片}}。
why:
1ms、100k+ ops/s、1TB 是缓存容量估算的锚点，不是要背的孤立数字。它们的下游用途是判断单实例是否够用，以及扩容先看吞吐/带宽还是内存。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
These cache numbers are sizing inputs: they tell you whether one instance is enough and whether throughput, bandwidth, or memory is the real bottleneck.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: Operations per second，缓存每秒处理的读写操作次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ops per second counts the read and write operations a cache handles each second.

scenario: 数据库估算给定锚点：单实例读约 50k TPS、写约 10-20k TPS、缓存命中读 <5ms、存储 64TiB+。
scenario_en: Database-estimation anchors are about 50k read TPS, 10-20k write TPS, sub-5ms cached reads, and 64TiB+ storage per instance.
q: 这些数据库数字约束哪个分片判断？
q_en: What sharding judgment do these database numbers constrain?
text: 这组锚点的用途是判断单机边界：8k TPS 或 8TB 这类规模先 {{保留单实例加副本}}；只有持续逼近写入、读吞吐或存储上限时才 {{分片}}。
why:
读 50k TPS、写 10-20k TPS、存储 64TiB+ 是容量规划输入，不是孤立速记。它们帮你先排除过早分片，再把注意力放到真正逼近的上限。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
These database numbers are planning inputs: they help you avoid premature sharding and focus on the limit you are actually approaching.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: Transactions per second，数据库每秒处理的事务数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS is the number of transactions a database completes each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二进制计量的存储单位，1 TiB 约等于 1.1 TB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB is a binary storage unit, about 1.1 times a decimal terabyte.

scenario: 一个后台任务系统给数据库直接开了 3k 个短连接，没用连接池；候选人在判断这样是否安全。
scenario_en: A background-job system opens 3k short database connections directly without pooling, and the candidate is judging whether that is safe.
q: 这组并发连接量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision does this concurrent-connection number support?
options: 单实例能扛 5k-20k 连接，3k 安全但该上连接池
数据库最多只能扛约 100 个连接，3k 早就超了
并发连接数没有上限，不用管理
连接数和数据库实例类型无关
why:
单实例数据库约支持 5k-20k 并发连接，3k 在安全范围内；连接数常成为运维约束，这也是用连接池的原因。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A single database instance supports roughly 5,000 to 20,000 concurrent connections, so 3k is safe but still worth pooling.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

A database can only handle about 100 connections; 3k is already way over.
Concurrent connections have no ceiling, so no need to manage them.
Connection capacity has nothing to do with instance type.

scenario_en: An order-event system has messages around 5KB and must retain three months of history for replay and audit.
q: 这组消息大小与保留量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision do these message size and retention numbers support?
options: 消息队列只能处理 <1KB 的小消息
队列能高效处理 1KB-10MB 消息，保留数月完全可行
队列重启后数据就会丢，存不了 3 个月
消息大小和保留时长互相无关，随便设
why:
队列可高效处理 1KB-10MB 消息，单 broker 存储达 50TB，保留数周至数月；5KB、3 个月都在能力内。

why_en:
Modern queues efficiently handle 1KB-10MB messages and retain data for weeks to months, so a 5KB message kept for three months fits easily.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

Queues efficiently handle 1KB-10MB messages, so months of retention is fine.
Data is lost on restart, so three months of retention is impossible.
Message size and retention length are unrelated, so set them arbitrarily.

steps: 先量化实际写吞吐与写模式（简单插入还是复杂事务）
对照单机能力：简单写单机 Postgres 约 20k+ WPS
若在能力内，先做批量写/索引优化/连接池等简单手段
只有真正超出单机能力或需要可靠投递/解耦时，才引入队列
why:
顺序：量化写模式 → 对照 20k+ WPS 单机上限 → 先上简单优化 → 真超了或有可靠投递/解耦需求才加队列。避免为 5k WPS 过度设计。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Quantify the write pattern, compare to the 20k+ WPS single-node limit, try simple tuning first, and only add a queue if truly exceeded.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Measure["Measure writes"] --> Compare["Compare 20k+ WPS"]
    Compare --> Simple["Optimize first"]
    Simple --> Queue["Queue only if needed"]
tradeoff: 先算术验证单机上限 vs 直接假设需要队列

termDefinitions.meaning: Writes per second，数据库每秒成功处理的写入次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WPS is the number of write operations a database completes each second.

q: Sharding 的核心定义是什么？
q_en: What is the core definition of sharding?
options: 把一个表拆成多个逻辑分区，但仍放在同一台数据库机器上
把数据水平拆分到多台独立数据库机器上，每个 shard 持有一部分数据
只把冷数据迁移到对象存储
给单个数据库实例加更多 CPU 和内存
options_en: Split one table into logical partitions but keep it on the same database machine.
Horizontally split data across multiple independent database machines, where each shard holds part of the data.
Just move cold data off to object storage.
Add more CPU and memory to a single database instance.
why:
Sharding 是跨多台机器的水平分片，每个 shard 都有自己的 CPU、内存、存储和连接池。它用多机分摊存储容量和读写吞吐。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Sharding horizontally splits data across multiple database machines so storage and throughput scale with the number of shards.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
optionExplanations: 把数据放在单机而不是多台机器上，这是 partitioning 的定义而非 sharding。
这正是 sharding 的核心定义，把数据跨多台机器分散。
这是数据归档而不是分片，不涉及跨机器分布。
这只是垂直扩展，无法扩展到多台机器的吞吐和存储。
optionExplanations_en: Putting data on one machine in partitions is partitioning, not sharding.
This is the core definition of sharding: distributing data across multiple independent machines.
Cold data archival is data management, not distribution across machines.
Vertical scaling with more CPU or memory cannot distribute throughput and storage.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding horizontally splits data across multiple independent database machines, each holding a subset of the data.

q: Partitioning 和 Sharding 在最关键维度上的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between partitioning and sharding?
options: Partitioning 一定跨机器，Sharding 一定在单机内
Partitioning 通常是在单个数据库实例内拆数据；Sharding 是把数据拆到多台机器
Partitioning 只能拆列，Sharding 只能拆索引
两者没有任何语义差异，永远完全等价
options_en: Partitioning always spans machines and sharding always stays inside one machine.
Partitioning usually splits data inside a single database instance; sharding splits data across multiple machines.
Partitioning can only split columns and sharding can only split indexes.
The two terms have no semantic difference and are always exactly equivalent.
why:
工程实践里两词常被混用，但技术上 partitioning 更常指单实例内分区，sharding 强调跨机器分布。面试里要说明数据到底在一台机器还是多台机器。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Partitioning usually means splitting data inside one database instance, while sharding means splitting it across multiple machines.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
tradeoff: partitioning（单机内组织数据，不加机器）vs sharding（跨机器分布数据，换来更多容量和吞吐）
optionExplanations: 说反了：这描述的是单机内切分，不是 sharding。
判断标准很简单：只要数据跨过不止一台服务器，就该叫 sharding。
拆列和拆索引是两回事，单机切分既能按行也能按列。
口语上常混用，但面试官仍期待你说清楚数据落在几台机器上。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards — that description is splitting inside one machine, not sharding.
Simple test: if the data spans more than one server, call it sharding.
Splitting columns and splitting indexes are different things; single-machine splitting can go either way.
The words get used loosely in practice, but interviewers still expect you to name how many machines the data spans.

q: 关于单机内 partitioning，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about single-machine partitioning are correct? (Select all that apply.)
options: Horizontal partitioning 按行拆，例如按年份拆 orders
Vertical partitioning 按列拆，例如把大字段或冷字段拆到另一张表
Partitioning 本身不会增加数据库机器数量
Partitioning 一定能把写吞吐扩展到多台机器
options_en: Horizontal partitioning splits rows, for example partitioning orders by year.
Vertical partitioning splits columns, for example moving large or cold columns into another table.
Partitioning by itself does not add more database machines.
Partitioning always scales write throughput across multiple machines.
why:
Partitioning 改善单实例内的数据组织和维护成本，但不等于多机扩展。它可以少扫分区、减小索引和维护范围，但机器资源仍然是同一台。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Partitioning can split rows or columns inside one instance, but it does not add more database machines.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
optionExplanations: 正确，水平分片就是按行分组，按条件（如年份）拆表。
正确，垂直分片就是把不同列拆到不同表或存储。
正确，单实例 partitioning 只改善数据组织，不增加机器数。
错误，单机分区不能把写吞吐扩展到多机器，那需要 sharding。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; horizontal partitioning splits rows by condition, for example by year.
Correct; vertical partitioning splits columns into separate tables or storage.
Correct; partitioning within one instance does not add database machines.
Incorrect; partitioning alone cannot scale write throughput to multiple machines; that requires sharding.

scenario: 一个 orders 表有 500M 行、2TB 数据，查询上月订单经常扫描大量历史数据，但单机 CPU/存储/写入还没有到上限。
scenario_en: An orders table has 500M rows and 2TB of data. Last-month queries scan a lot of history, but single-node CPU, storage, and write capacity are not yet maxed out.
q: 这个阶段优先考虑什么？
q_en: What should you prioritize at this stage?
options: 跳过分区，直接引入 64 个 shard 做水平扩展
先在单机内按时间做 partitioning，让查询只扫相关分区
删掉表上的所有索引来提升扫描速度
把全部历史订单迁移进 Redis 当主存储
options_en: Skip partitioning and jump straight to 64 shards for horizontal scaling.
First partition by time inside the single instance so queries only scan the relevant slice.
Delete every index on the table to speed up scans.
Move all historical orders into Redis as the primary store.
why:
如果瓶颈主要是大表扫描和维护范围，单机 partitioning 可能足够。Sharding 是单机容量或吞吐撑不住时的更重方案。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
If the issue is large-table scans inside one still-capable machine, partitioning can help before introducing sharding.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 当单机存储、写吞吐或读吞吐已经接近上限，即使分区也不够时，才应进入 sharding 讨论。
tradeoff: partitioning（轻量，先解决扫描范围问题）vs sharding（更重，只有单机容量/吞吐真撑不住才值得）
optionExplanations: 64 台机器太重：瓶颈只是扫描范围，不是单机容量或吞吐。
对：按时间分区能让查询只扫相关时间段，先减轻单机扫描压力。
删索引只会让大表扫描更慢，方向反了。
Redis 是缓存，不是能顶替持久化订单历史的主存储。
optionExplanations_en: Sixty-four shards is overkill when the bottleneck is scan scope, not machine capacity.
Correct; time-based partitioning lets queries skip irrelevant periods, easing the single-machine scan load first.
Dropping indexes would make large-table scans slower, the wrong direction entirely.
Redis is a cache, not a durable primary store for the full order history.

q: 按正确顺序排列面试里引入 sharding 的决策链：
q_en: Put the decision chain for introducing sharding in an interview in the right order.
steps: 解释为什么单库或只加 read replicas 已经不够
识别具体瓶颈：存储、写吞吐或读吞吐
提出 sharding，并说明 shard key 和分布策略
先避免过早 sharding，做容量估算
why:
不要一上来就 shard。先做容量估算并证明单库不够，再提出分片方案，面试官更容易接受你的复杂度选择。

why_en:
A good interview answer estimates capacity first, proves one database is insufficient, and only then proposes sharding.

A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

flowchart TD

  B --> C["Pick shard key"]

q: 一个好的 shard key 通常需要满足哪些性质？（多选）
q_en: What properties does a good shard key usually need? (Select all that apply.)
options: 高基数，有很多不同取值
数据和流量分布尽量均匀
和主要查询模式对齐，使常见查询命中单个 shard
值越少越好，最好只有 true/false
options_en: High cardinality, with many distinct values
Data and traffic distribute evenly across shards
It matches primary query patterns, so common queries hit a single shard
The fewer values the better — ideally just true and false
why:
Shard key 决定数据如何被分组。高基数、均匀分布、贴合查询模式能减少热点和跨 shard 查询。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A good shard key has high cardinality, balanced distribution, and matches the dominant query patterns.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
optionExplanations: 正确，高基数意味着 key 有很多可能值，能打散数据。
正确，均匀分布能避免热点 shard 和数据倾斜。
正确，贴合查询模式的 shard key 能减少跨 shard 操作。
错误，基数太低反而会导致严重倾斜和热点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; high cardinality means many distinct values, distributing data better.
Correct; balanced traffic distribution avoids hotspot shards and data skew.
Correct; a shard key aligned with query patterns reduces cross-shard operations.
Incorrect; low cardinality keys cause severe imbalance and hot spots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条记录被分到哪个 shard 的字段，例如 user_id。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key is the field, such as user_id, that determines which shard a record is routed to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个字段可能取值的唯一数量；越高越能把数据打散到更多 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of distinct values a field can take; higher cardinality spreads data across more shards.

q: 为什么用 boolean 字段 `is_premium` 做 shard key 很差？
q_en: Why is a boolean field like `is_premium` a poor shard key?
options: boolean 不能被数据库存储
只有两个取值，最多天然分成两个大组，且很容易严重倾斜
boolean 会让所有查询变成跨 shard
boolean 字段无法建立索引
options_en: Booleans can't be stored in a database.
It only has two values, so at most it splits into two groups, and one easily ends up far larger than the other.
A boolean shard key forces every query to become cross-shard.
Boolean fields can't be indexed.
why:
`is_premium` 基数太低，只能把数据分成 premium 和 free 两堆；如果大多数用户是 free，一个 shard 会远大于另一个。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A boolean shard key has extremely low cardinality and tends to create only two imbalanced shards.

A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
optionExplanations: 错误，boolean 可以被存储，问题出在它作为 shard key 的特性。
正确，boolean 基数只有 2，容易导致数据严重不平衡。
不准确，boolean shard key 会导致倾斜和热点，但不一定所有查询都跨 shard。
错误，boolean 字段完全可以建立索引。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; databases can store booleans; the issue is their low cardinality as shard keys.
Correct; a boolean has only two values, creating at most two imbalanced groups.
Not quite; a boolean key causes skew and imbalance, but not all queries necessarily fan out.
Incorrect; boolean fields can be indexed like any other column.

q: 按 country 分片时，如果 90% 用户都在美国，直接后果是什么？
q_en: If you shard by country and 90% of users are in the US, what is the direct consequence?
options: 所有 shard 一定完全均匀
美国 shard 变热点，其他相对空闲
查询会自动变成 O(1)
数据库不再需要索引
options_en: All shards will necessarily stay perfectly balanced.
The US shard becomes a hotspot while the others sit relatively idle.
Queries automatically become O(1).
The database no longer needs indexes.
why:
Shard key 的取值频率如果高度倾斜，会把数据量和请求量压到少数 shard。分片数量多也救不了一个倾斜的 key。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A skewed shard key like country can overload the dominant value's shard while others remain underused.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
optionExplanations: 错：country 高度倾斜时，均匀性直接被打破。
对：90% 用户集中在美国，等于把绝大部分数据和请求压到一个 shard 上。
错：倾斜的 key 只会让延迟变差，不会把查询降到常数时间。

Boolean shard key
全表扫描
只写单库

codeSample:
ring = sorted(hash(node) for node in nodes)

termDefinitions.meaning: 取模运算，用除法余数决定映射到哪个桶；shard 数一变，几乎所有余数都会变。

q: Directory-based sharding 的核心机制是什么？

why:
Directory sharding 不用公式，而是查一张映射表来定位某个 key 当前在哪个 shard；最大优点是灵活，可以单独搬迁任意一条记录。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。

Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table or service to map each key to its shard.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. q: Cross-shard operation 是什么？

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。

A global top-ten query is expensive because candidates are spread across shards and must be merged.

q: 降低常见跨 shard 查询成本的办法有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are ways to reduce the cost of common cross-shard queries? (Select all that apply.)
options: 缓存结果，例如 trending/top 10 缓存 5 分钟
预计算或用后台任务维护聚合结果
反范式化，把常一起读的数据放在同一 shard
每个用户请求都实时查询所有 shard
options_en: Cache the results, e.g. cache trending/top-10 for five minutes
Precompute results or maintain aggregates with a background job
Denormalize by keeping frequently co-read data on the same shard
Query all shards live for every single user request
why:
常见跨 shard 查询应尽量缓存、预计算或重塑数据模型。频繁 fan-out 到所有 shard 通常是设计需要重想的信号。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Common cross-shard queries should be cached, precomputed, or avoided through denormalization.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
optionExplanations: 对：像 trending 这种能接受几分钟延迟的结果，缓存能挡掉后面几千次重复的全 shard 查询。
对：后台任务提前算好聚合结果，用户请求时直接读，不用现场 fan-out。
对：把常一起读的数据复制到同一个 shard，一次查询就能拿全，代价是多存一份、更新更复杂。
错：每个用户请求都现查所有 shard，正是要避免的高成本模式。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; for results like trending that tolerate a few minutes of staleness, caching blocks thousands of repeat all-shard queries.
Correct; a background job precomputes the aggregate ahead of time, so requests just read it instead of fanning out live.
Correct; copying frequently co-read data onto one shard makes it a single query, at the cost of extra storage and harder updates.
Incorrect; querying all shards live on every request is exactly the expensive pattern to avoid.

Query all 64 shards live on every request.

optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; deleting the feature is avoidance, not a design solution.

q: 为什么 sharding 会让原本简单的数据库事务变复杂？
q_en: Why does sharding make formerly simple database transactions more complex?
options: 索引在分片后完全无法用于事务
分片后数据库彻底不再支持任何写入操作
相关数据分落不同 shard，单库事务盖不住
分片后所有查询都被迫变成只读模式
options_en: Indexes can never be used in transactions after sharding.
The database completely stops supporting any writes after sharding.
Related data may live on different shards, so a single-database transaction can't cover all of them.
Every query is forced to become read-only after sharding.
why:
单库事务只覆盖一个数据库实例。如果用户账户在 shard 1、交易记录在 shard 2，就需要跨独立数据库协调一致性。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Sharding complicates transactions because related writes may live on different independent databases.
