A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

错误，分片后仍然支持写入，只是写入可能跨多个 shard。
正确，sharding 后相关数据可能在不同数据库，需要跨 shard 协调。
错误，分片后查询仍可读写，只是可能需要跨 shard 协调。

Incorrect; sharded databases still support writes, though they may span multiple shards.
Correct; sharding puts related data on independent databases, breaking single-database transactions.
Incorrect; sharding does not make queries read-only.

q: Two-phase commit 在跨 shard 事务中的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of two-phase commit for cross-shard transactions?
options: 不需要协调者
极快且没有故障模式
只能用于缓存，不能用于数据库
强一致但慢，协调者/shard 故障会卡住
options_en: It requires no coordinator.
Extremely fast with no failure modes at all.
It only works for caches, never for databases.
Strong consistency, but slow and fragile — a coordinator or shard failure can stall the whole process.
why: 2PC 能提供强一致提交语义，但用性能和可用性换一致性。多数生产系统会尽量避免把它放在高频路径上。
why_en: Two-phase commit gives stronger consistency but is slow and fragile under coordinator or participant failures.
tradeoff: 2PC（强一致提交，但慢、协调者/参与者故障会卡住）vs 避免跨 shard 事务或用 saga（更快更有弹性，只拿 eventual consistency）
codeSample:
Coordinator -> ShardA: PREPARE
Coordinator -> ShardB: PREPARE
ShardA -> Coordinator: READY
ShardB -> Coordinator: READY
Coordinator -> ShardA: COMMIT
Coordinator -> ShardB: COMMIT
# if ShardB times out after READY, the whole transaction can block
optionExplanations: 错，2PC 需要一个协调者来管理准备/提交流程。
错，2PC 本身不快，而且有明确的故障模式。
错，2PC 主要用于跨数据库的分布式事务，不是缓存。
对：2PC 提供强一致性，但有性能和可用性开销，故障会让流程卡住。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; two-phase commit requires a coordinator to run the prepare/commit flow.
Incorrect; two-phase commit is neither fast nor failure-free.
Incorrect; two-phase commit is for distributed database transactions, not caches.
Correct; two-phase commit provides strong consistency but has real performance and availability costs, and failures can stall it.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort together.

q: 最好的事务设计方向是什么？

故意把每个字段放到不同 shard
所有操作都用 2PC
同用户数据聚合到一个 shard

Deliberately spread every field across different shards.
Use two-phase commit for every operation.

why: 避免跨 shard 事务是首选。把同一聚合边界的数据放在同一 shard，可以继续用普通单库事务，简单且可靠。
why_en: The best design keeps related user data on one shard so normal single-shard transactions still work.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务天然跨用户或跨 tenant，例如转账，就需要 saga、异步补偿或接受更复杂的一致性方案。
tradeoff: 同一用户数据聚合在一个 shard（保持普通单库事务，简单可靠）vs 拆到不同 shard（灵活分布，但事务要靠 2PC/saga）
optionExplanations: 错误，缓存不能替代数据库作为持久化。
错误，分散数据会导致强制需要跨 shard 事务。
错误，不是所有操作都需要 2PC，只有必要时才用。
正确，把用户相关数据聚合在同一 shard，可以用普通单库事务。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; caches cannot replace the database for durability.
Incorrect; scattering data forces unnecessary cross-shard transactions.
Incorrect; not all operations need two-phase commit; use it only when necessary.
Correct; keeping related user data on one shard lets you use normal single-shard transactions.

q: 按正确顺序排列跨 shard 转账的 saga 补偿流程：
q_en: Put the saga compensation flow for a cross-shard transfer in the right order.
steps: 如果给 User B 加钱失败，执行补偿动作
从 User A 所在 shard 扣钱
把钱加到 User B 所在 shard
补偿动作把 User A 的扣款退回
why: Saga 把跨 shard 操作拆成独立步骤，并为已完成步骤准备补偿。它提供 eventual consistency，而不是 2PC 那种原子提交。
why_en: A saga coordinates cross-shard work through independent steps plus compensating actions on failure.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Debit shard"] --> B["Credit shard"]
  B --> C{"Failed?"}
  C -->|"no"| D["Commit outcome"]
  C -->|"yes"| E["Compensate debit"]

scenario: 用户 follower_count 被反范式化到多个 shard 以加速 profile 读取，短时间内不同 shard 显示的计数可能不一致。
scenario_en: A user's `follower_count` is denormalized across several shards to speed up profile reads, so counts may disagree briefly across shards.
q: 这类场景通常可以接受什么一致性模型？
q_en: What consistency model is usually acceptable for this kind of scenario?
options: 所有读都锁住全站
每次读都必须 2PC
禁止缓存和反范式化
最终一致，异步收敛
options_en: Lock the entire site for every read
Every read must go through two-phase commit
Ban caching and denormalization entirely
Eventually consistent, converging asynchronously
why: 计数类展示通常允许几秒延迟，最终收敛即可。为了这类低风险数据强行做分布式事务，复杂度不值得。
why_en: Denormalized counters often tolerate eventual consistency because brief inconsistencies are acceptable.
whenOtherWins: 库存扣减、资金转账这类强正确性场景不能轻易接受短暂错误，需要更强事务或补偿设计。
tradeoff: eventual consistency（快、简单，短暂不一致）vs 强一致/2PC（每次读写都准确，但要跨 shard 协调，慢且脆弱）
optionExplanations: 错：全站锁会把所有并发读写都串行化，代价极大。
错：给每次读加 2PC，性能代价远超这类展示型数据值得的程度。
错：反范式化和缓存正是为了减少昂贵的跨 shard 查询，不该禁止。
对：几秒内不同 shard 数字略有出入没关系，后台任务最终会把它们收敛成同一个值。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; a site-wide lock serializes all concurrent reads and writes at a huge cost.
Incorrect; adding two-phase commit to every read costs far more than this display-only data is worth.
Incorrect; denormalization and caching exist precisely to cut expensive cross-shard queries, not to be banned.
Correct; a few seconds of disagreement between shards is fine, since a background job eventually converges them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短时间内不同副本/shard 数据不一致，但保证最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows replicas or shards to briefly disagree, as long as they are guaranteed to converge to the same value over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了减少跨 shard 查询，把常一起读的数据复制一份放到同一个 shard 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization copies frequently co-read data onto the same shard so a query no longer needs to cross shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PC（Two-Phase Commit，两阶段提交）：协调者先让所有参与者准备好，再统一提交或回滚的分布式事务协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort together.

q: 现代数据库通常如何帮你处理 sharding？（多选）
q_en: How do modern databases usually help you handle sharding? (Select all that apply.)
options: 让你指定 partition key 或 shard key
自动处理路由、分裂/迁移或再平衡中的一部分
完全消除 shard key 选择带来的所有后果
在不同产品中使用完全相同的内部机制
options_en: Let you specify a partition key or shard key
Automatically handle part of the routing, splitting/migration, or rebalancing
Completely eliminate every consequence of your shard key choice
Use exactly the same internal mechanism across different products
why: Cassandra、DynamoDB、MongoDB、Vitess/Citus 等会帮你处理很多路由和再平衡细节，但 shard key 选择仍会决定热点和查询形状。
why_en: Modern databases automate routing and balancing work, but they do not remove the need to choose a good key.
optionExplanations: 正确，现代数据库通常要求你指定 partition/shard key。
正确，现代数据库自动处理很多分片细节，减少手动工作。
错误，即使自动处理，shard key 选择仍会影响热点和查询形状。
错误，不同数据库用不同内部机制，虽然对用户来说大致相似。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; modern databases let you specify a partition or shard key.
Correct; they automate routing, splitting, migration, and rebalancing work.
Incorrect; automation does not eliminate the impact of shard key choice.
Incorrect; different databases use different internal mechanisms under the hood.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条记录被分到哪个 shard 的字段，例如 user_id。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key is the field, such as user_id, that determines which shard a record is routed to.

scenario: 你的 orders 表已经涨到 200TiB，还在以每年翻倍的速度增长；Amazon Aurora 单集群存储上限大约在 256TiB 量级。
scenario_en: Your orders table has grown to 200TiB and doubles every year. Amazon Aurora single-cluster storage is roughly capped around 256TiB.
q: 这个上限对你的容量规划意味着什么？
q_en: What does this ceiling mean for your capacity plan?
options: 既然还没到 256TiB，可以完全不用考虑分片，永远用单集群
单集群有天花板，约 1 年后逼近，需提前规划分片
只要升级到更贵的实例类型，存储上限就会消失
把索引全部删掉就能突破这个上限
options_en: Since we haven't hit 256TiB yet, we never need to consider sharding on a single cluster.
A single cluster has a ceiling; at this rate we'll approach it in about a year, so plan sharding now.
Upgrading to a pricier instance type makes the storage ceiling disappear.
Deleting all the indexes would break through this limit.
why:
单个数据库集群的存储不是无限的，Aurora 这类顶级云数据库也有量级上限（约 256TiB）。按当前翻倍速度推算多久会撞到天花板，才能判断现在还是一年后该开始做 sharding。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Even top-tier managed databases like Aurora have a storage ceiling, so projecting your growth rate against that ceiling tells you when sharding actually becomes necessary.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 补全面试里提 sharding 的三步公式：
q_en: Complete the three-step interview formula for introducing sharding.
text: 先识别{{瓶颈}}，再解释为什么{{单数据库}}无法扩展，最后提出{{sharding}}并说明 key 与策略。
why:
这能避免过早 sharding 的常见错误，也能把复杂度选择建立在容量推导上。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
The interview formula is to identify the bottleneck, prove one database is insufficient, and then propose sharding.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 按正确顺序排列一个社交应用里的 sharding 面试回答：
q_en: Put a sharding interview answer for a social app in the right order.
steps: 说明全局 trending 查询会变贵，可用缓存/后台预计算处理

好的表达不是列名词，而是先用访问模式选 key，再选分布策略，然后主动讲 tradeoff 和扩容计划。

A strong answer chooses the key from access patterns, selects a distribution strategy, then explains tradeoffs and growth.

A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 系统设计面试里过早提出 sharding 的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the risk of proposing sharding too early in a system design interview?
options: 过早 sharding 不会改变系统复杂度
面试官一定希望所有系统一开始就分 100 个 shard
sharding 会自动让所有设计更简单
你引入了热点、跨 shard 查询、重平衡和一致性等复杂度，却没有证明这些成本必要
options_en: Premature sharding doesn't change the system's complexity at all.
The interviewer definitely wants every system to start with 100 shards.
Sharding automatically makes every design simpler.
You introduce hotspots, cross-shard queries, rebalancing, and consistency complexity without proving those costs are necessary.
why:
Sharding 是解决单库规模瓶颈的重武器，不是默认起点。先做 math，证明单库或复制不够，再引入它。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Premature sharding adds real operational and consistency complexity before proving the scale requires it.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

错误，好的面试官不会希望过早 sharding，而是看容量估算。
错误，sharding 反而增加复杂度。
正确，过早 sharding 会引入大量复杂度，但没有基于容量推导来证明必要。

Incorrect; good interviewers expect capacity math, not immediate sharding.

q: 补全三种 sharding 策略的关键词：

text: {{Range}} sharding 简单且支持范围扫描；{{Hash}} sharding 默认更均匀；{{Directory}} sharding 最灵活但每次请求多一次 lookup。
why: 三种策略没有绝对赢家：range 强在范围，hash 强在均匀，directory 强在动态控制。
why_en: Range, hash, and directory sharding trade off range scans, balance, and routing flexibility.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 shard key 的连续值区间分配给不同 shard，例如 user_id 1–1M 到 shard 1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns continuous ranges of the shard key's values to different shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 做 hash 后再取模，把结果映射到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and maps the result to a shard, typically via modulo.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一张查找表或目录服务记录每个 key 当前在哪个 shard 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table or service that records which shard each key currently lives on.

q: 你应该回答哪两个？
q_en: Which two design decisions should you answer with?
options: 选择是否用 dark mode，以及字体大小
选择 logo 颜色，以及 README 标题
选择前端框架，以及按钮圆角

options_en: Choosing dark mode, and the font size
Choosing the logo color, and the README title
Choosing the frontend framework, and the button corner radius
Choosing the shard key, and choosing the strategy for how data is distributed to shards
why:
Sharding 设计最核心的是“按什么字段分组”和“用什么规则把这些组分布到机器”。这两个决定会影响热点、查询和扩容。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
The two core sharding decisions are the shard key and the distribution strategy.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统还没证明单库瓶颈，最重要的决策不是怎么 shard，而是先做容量估算和单库/复制方案评估。
tradeoff: shard key 选择（数据怎么分组）vs 分布策略选择（这些组怎么摊到机器上）——两个独立但相关的决策

Gateway 通常无状态，因此可以横向扩容：前置 LB 把请求分发到多个 Gateway 实例即可。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A stateless gateway scales horizontally by adding instances behind a load balancer.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 如果 Gateway 持有本地会话或连接状态，就要先解决状态迁移或粘性会话，再谈扩容。

q: 传统的 hash(value) % num_nodes 分配方案有哪些问题？（多选）
options: 节点数量变化时，大量值会被重新映射到新节点，数据要在节点间大规模搬迁
哈希不走运时，很多值会集中到同一节点，负载不均
无法计算出哈希值
读请求永远比写请求慢
options_en: When the node count changes, most values get remapped to new nodes and a huge amount of data has to move between nodes
If the hash distribution is unlucky, many values land on the same node, creating uneven load
The hash value cannot be computed at all
Read requests are always slower than write requests
why:
取模哈希的两大痛点：一是加减节点会让几乎所有 key 换家，引发海量数据迁移；二是分布可能不均导致热点节点。一致性哈希正是为了解决这两点。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Modulo hashing forces massive data remapping whenever the node count changes and can also produce uneven load across nodes.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 一致性哈希如何决定一个值存到哪个节点？
options: 对值取模节点数
随机选择一个节点

Always store it on the first node that started up

一致性哈希把哈希空间视为一个环：值哈希成 token 后顺时针找到第一个节点。这样节点增减只影响环上相邻的一段，而不是全部数据。

why_en:
Consistent hashing maps a value to an integer on a ring and walks clockwise to the first node, which stores the value.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

options: 在应用层做内存 JOIN
把两个查询合并成一个
加更多节点

options_en: Do an in-memory join at the application layer
Merge the two queries into one
Add more nodes
Build one table per query and denormalize

q: Discord 最初的 messages 表主键设计是？
options: PRIMARY KEY (channel_id, message_id) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (message_id DESC)
PRIMARY KEY (message_id) 全局唯一，无法按频道单分区查询，需要跨节点 scatter-gather
PRIMARY KEY (author_id, channel_id)，按作者分区，无法服务频道时间线查询
PRIMARY KEY ((channel_id, author_id), message_id)，复合分区键打散了同频道消息
options_en: PRIMARY KEY (channel_id, message_id) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (message_id DESC)
PRIMARY KEY (message_id), globally unique, but a channel query needs a cross-node scatter-gather
PRIMARY KEY (author_id, channel_id), partitioned by author, can't serve a channel timeline
PRIMARY KEY ((channel_id, author_id), message_id) scatters one channel's messages across partitions
why: channel_id 作分区键让一个频道的消息都在同一分区（避免 scatter-gather），message_id DESC 聚簇让最新消息排前面，正好匹配「看最近消息」的访问模式。
why_en: Partitioning by channel with messages clustered by descending message id serves recent-message queries from a single partition.
tradeoff: channel 单分区服务查询 vs 全局/复合分区导致 scatter-gather
whenOtherWins: 频道消息量极大、分区会无限增长时，这个设计会产生大分区问题——那就要在分区键里加时间 bucket。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Discord bounds each channel's partition by bucketing messages into fixed ten-day windows anchored to its own epoch, so partitions stop growing without any manual migration.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

why:
分区大小要看最坏情况：section 数量天然有上界（通常 <100），所以 event_id 单分区没有大分区风险——和座位表形成对比。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Events rarely have more than about a hundred sections, so a single partition per event easily serves the venue overview query.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

steps: 代价：默认偏最终一致，没有 JOIN / 通用多行事务 / ad-hoc 聚合
缓解：关键路径用 QUORUM 读写 + 查询驱动建模、按访问模式反规范化
需求：写入吞吐极高、必须水平扩展、可用性优先
决定性属性：LSM 写优化存储 + 一致性哈希分区 + 无主多副本复制
选型：Cassandra
why: 标准链路：需求（高写、可扩、高可用）→ 决定性属性（LSM + 一致性哈希 + 无主复制）→ 选 Cassandra → 代价（默认偏最终一致、查询和事务受限）→ 缓解（QUORUM + 查询驱动建模）。
why_en: High write throughput and availability needs point to Cassandra's LSM and leaderless replication, whose consistency, transaction, and query costs are mitigated by quorum operations and query-driven modeling.
tradeoff: 高写吞吐可扩可用 vs 一致性/事务/查询能力受限

q: 布隆过滤器在抽象上最接近哪种数据结构的概率版?
q_en: Conceptually, a Bloom filter is a probabilistic version of which data structure?
options: 队列(插入和弹出)
图(节点和边)
有序列表(排序遍历)
集合(插入元素、查询成员是否存在)
options_en: A queue (push and pop).
A graph (nodes and edges).
A sorted list (ordered traversal).
A set (insert elements, check membership).
why: 布隆过滤器是集合(set)的概率类比:支持插入和成员查询,但用概率答案换取远小于哈希表的内存。
why_en: A bloom filter is a probabilistic analog of a set, supporting inserts and membership checks with far less memory than a hash table.
optionExplanations: 队列关心顺序进出,不支持“是否存在”这种成员查询语义
图建模的是节点间的关系,不是元素的成员关系
有序列表关心顺序遍历,不是概率化的成员测试
正确:集合语义(插入+成员查询)正是布隆过滤器概率化的对象
optionExplanations_en: A queue is about ordered push/pop, not an is-it-present query.
A graph models relationships between nodes, not set membership.
An ordered list is about traversal order, not probabilistic membership testing.
Correct: set semantics — insert plus membership check — is exactly what a Bloom filter makes probabilistic.

q: 要跟踪数万亿个元素 ID 的成员关系,为什么直接用哈希表实现集合不可行?
q_en: Why is a hash-table-backed set infeasible for membership over trillions of element IDs?
options: 每个元素都要占内存,超大集合下扛不住
哈希表的插入是 O(n)
哈希表不支持成员查询
哈希表必须存在磁盘上
options_en: Every element needs memory, unaffordable at huge scale.
A hash table's insert is O(n).
A hash table does not support membership queries.
A hash table must live on disk.
why: 哈希表插入和查询都是 O(1),但每个元素都要占内存,万亿级元素时内存不可行——这正是布隆过滤器做妥协的出发点。
why_en: A hash table gives O(1) inserts and lookups but needs memory for every element, which becomes infeasible at trillions of items.
optionExplanations: 正确:哈希表按元素数线性占内存,万亿级时不可行
哈希表插入是均摊 O(1),不是 O(n)
哈希表恰恰支持成员查询,这不是它的短板
哈希表可以完全放在内存里,不要求必须落盘
optionExplanations_en: Correct: a hash table's memory grows linearly with element count, infeasible at trillions of items.
Hash table inserts are amortized O(1), not O(n).
Membership queries are exactly what a hash table supports well; that is not its weakness.
A hash table can live entirely in memory; it is not required to be on disk.

q: 布隆过滤器能可靠给出哪些回答?(多选)
q_en: Which answers can a Bloom filter give reliably? (multi-select)
options: 元素“可能”在集合中(概率可配置)
元素“一定不”在集合中
元素“一定”在集合中
元素出现了多少次
options_en: The element is probably in the set (configurable probability).
The element is definitely not in the set.
The element is definitely in the set.
How many times the element occurred.
why: 布隆过滤器只有两种回答:可能在(有可配置的假阳性率)和一定不在。它永远无法证明元素一定在,也不提供计数。
why_en: A bloom filter can only say an element is probably in the set or definitely not in it, never that it is certainly present.
optionExplanations: 正确:能给出配置好的假阳性率下的“可能在”
正确:位缺失时的“一定不在”是绝对可靠的结论
布隆过滤器永远无法证明“一定在”,这正是它的代价
结构里没有计数信息,回答不了出现次数
optionExplanations_en: Correct: it can say an element is probably present at a configurable false-positive rate.
Correct: a missing bit gives an absolutely reliable definitely-not-present answer.
A Bloom filter can never prove definite presence; that certainty is exactly what it gives up.
The structure carries no count information, so it cannot answer how many times.

q: 补全布隆过滤器的读写机制:
q_en: Fill in the Bloom filter read/write mechanism:
text: 插入元素时,用 {{k}} 个不同的哈希函数各哈希一次,把对应比特位都置为 {{1}}(相当于按位 OR 盖章);查询时若任意一位是 {{0}},该元素一定不在集合中。
why: k 个哈希函数生成元素的“印章”位图;插入是置位,查询是检查所有对应位。任何一位缺失就能斩钉截铁地说“不在”。
why_en: Each element is hashed k times to set k bits, and on lookup any unset bit proves the element was never inserted.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["item"] --> B["hash1 hash2 hash3"]
  B --> C["set bits"]
  D["query item"] --> E["check bits"]
  E --> F["no or maybe"]

q: 查询布隆过滤器时,发现元素对应的所有位都是 1,正确的结论是?
q_en: If all Bloom filter bits for an element are 1, what conclusion is correct?
options: 元素一定在集合中
元素一定不在集合中
元素可能在集合中(可能被其他元素的位覆盖)
无法得出任何结论
options_en: The element is definitely in the set.
The element is definitely not in the set.
The element is possibly in the set (bits may overlap with other elements).
No conclusion can be drawn at all.
why: 所有位为 1 只能说“可能在”:这些位可能是其他元素叠加置上的(就像别人的印章恰好覆盖了你的形状),这就是假阳性的来源。
why_en: If all bits are set the element is only probably present, because other elements' hashes may have set those same bits.
optionExplanations: 所有位为 1 只是“可能”,不能断言一定在集合中
位全为 1 时恰恰无法说“一定不在”,那是位缺失时才有的结论
正确:位可能被其他元素的哈希叠加置上,这就是假阳性的来源
至少能得出“可能在”这个概率结论,并非毫无信息
optionExplanations_en: All bits being set only means probably present, never a guarantee of presence.
When all bits are set you specifically cannot conclude definitely-absent; that needs a missing bit.
Correct: those bits may have been set by other elements' hashes overlapping, the source of false positives.
There is at least a probabilistic probably-in conclusion; it is not zero information.

q: 随着插入越来越多、越来越多的位被置为 1,布隆过滤器会发生什么?
q_en: What happens as more inserts set more bits to 1 in a Bloom filter?
options: 单次查询延迟变慢
假阳性率持续升高,最终彻底失效
触发自动扩容机制
开始漏报真正存在的元素
options_en: Each query gets slower.
The false-positive rate keeps climbing until it fails entirely.
It triggers automatic resizing.
It starts failing to report elements that are actually present.
why: 位图越饱和,任意元素的位都全为 1 的概率越高,过滤器越没信息量;全部置 1 就像被墨水浸透的印章纸,什么都说明不了。
why_en: As more bits get set the filter saturates and its false-positive rate climbs, until a fully-set filter can say nothing at all.
optionExplanations: 查询始终是固定 k 次位检查,不会因位图变满而变慢
正确:位越满,任意查询命中全 1 的概率越高,假阳性率随之升高
布隆过滤器容量固定,不支持自动扩容
它只会误报“在”,不会漏报真正存在的元素(不存在假阴性)
optionExplanations_en: Lookup stays O(k), a fixed number of hash checks, regardless of how full the bit array gets.
Correct: as more bits fill, any query is more likely to see all-ones by chance, so false positives climb.
The filter's capacity is fixed; it has no auto-resizing.
It can only over-report presence; it never under-reports an element that is actually there.

q: 既然位越多越不容易饱和,为什么不能无脑加大布隆过滤器的位数组?
q_en: If more bits reduce saturation, why not make the Bloom filter bit array huge by default?
options: 位数组太大会导致哈希冲突增加
加位会让查询变成 O(n)
位太多会产生假阴性
加位就加体积,省内存正是用它的全部意义,必须精确调参
options_en: A bigger bit array causes more hash collisions.
Adding bits turns lookup into O(n).
Too many bits causes false negatives.
More bits means more memory, and saving memory is the whole point, so sizing must be deliberate.
why: 布隆过滤器必须按元素规模和目标假阳性率仔细选位数 m 和哈希数 k;盲目加位就丧失了省空间这个使用它的初衷。
why_en: You must size the bit array and hash count carefully, because adding bits grows the filter and saving space is the whole reason to use it.
optionExplanations: 位数组大小和哈希冲突率无关,冲突由哈希函数质量决定
查询固定是 k 次位检查,和位数组大小无关,不会退化成 O(n)
多加位只会让假阳性更少,不会产生假阴性
正确:加位就是加内存,省空间才是用它的理由,必须按需精确调参
optionExplanations_en: Bit-array size is unrelated to collision rate, which depends on hash-function quality.
Lookup is always k bit checks regardless of array size; it never degrades to O(n).
More bits only reduces false positives; it cannot cause false negatives.
Correct: more bits means more memory, and saving memory is the whole point, so size must be tuned deliberately.

q: 这组量级对布隆过滤器的部署方式意味着什么?
q_en: What does this scale imply for deploying a Bloom filter?
options: 1GB 已是不小的常驻内存,应作为独立组件做容量规划,不能想当然地每实例各存一份
可以完全忽略它的内存占用,像日志文件一样对待
既然比哈希表省了 80%,就不用再监控它的内存增长
1GB 还不够小,应该继续加哈希函数数量把它压到几 MB
options_en: One gigabyte is already substantial memory and needs real capacity planning, not casual per-instance copies.
Its memory footprint can be ignored entirely, treated like a log file.
Since it saves eighty percent over a hash table, its memory growth no longer needs monitoring.
One gigabyte is still not small enough; keep adding hash functions to shrink it to a few megabytes.
why:
10 亿元素、1% 假阳性率的布隆过滤器约 1GB——比很多人想象的大得多,必须像其他大内存组件一样规划部署和监控,而不是随手在每个实例里复制。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A billion-element Bloom filter at a one percent false-positive rate takes about a gigabyte, large enough that it needs real capacity planning rather than casual per-instance duplication.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

The Bloom filter can under-report definitely-absent (a false negative).

flowchart LR

布隆过滤器更精确
两者都只给概率答案
options_en: Both give exact answers.
A hash table is exact, a Bloom filter is probabilistic.
A Bloom filter is more precise.
Both only give probabilistic answers.
why: 哈希表是精确集合;布隆过滤器把“一定在”弱化成“可能在”,换取约 80% 的内存节省——这是它存在的全部理由。
why_en: A hash table answers membership exactly, while a bloom filter trades that certainty for memory by answering probably-in or definitely-not.
tradeoff: 精确成员判定 vs 内存节省(约 80%)

q: Count-Min Sketch 回答的核心问题是什么?

集合里有多少个不同元素
某个元素在数据流中出现次数的上界估计
数据的分位数分布
options_en: Whether an element is in the set.
How many distinct elements are in the set.
An upper-bound estimate of how many times an element appeared in a stream.
The quantile distribution of the data.
why: CMS 是布隆过滤器的自然延伸:不是回答“在不在”,而是估计某元素在流中出现了多少次——严格说是给出出现次数的上界。
why_en: Count-Min Sketch estimates how many times an item has appeared in a stream, more precisely an upper bound on that count.

分位数分布由直方图/桶算法处理,不是 CMS 的职责

Counting distinct items is HyperLogLog's job; Count-Min Sketch does not deduplicate.
Correct: Count-Min Sketch estimates an upper bound on how many times a known item has appeared.
Quantile distributions are handled by histogram/bucket algorithms, not Count-Min Sketch.

q: 在 Count-Min Sketch 里查询某元素的计数时,取的是什么值?
q_en: When querying an item in Count-Min Sketch, which value do you return?
options: 该元素对应的所有计数器中的最小值
所有计数器的平均值
对应计数器中的最大值
对应计数器之和
options_en: The minimum across the element's counters.
The average of all counters.
The maximum across the element's counters.
The sum of the element's counters.
why: 取最小值(“count-min”名字的由来):任何一个对应计数器都 ≥ 真实次数(可能被碰撞抬高),所以最小的那个就是最紧的上界。
why_en: You take the minimum across the item's counters, because every counter is inflated by collisions and the smallest gives the tightest upper bound.
optionExplanations: 正确:取最小值给出最紧的上界,这正是“count-min”名字的由来
平均值会被碰撞抬高的计数器拖累,不是紧的上界
取最大值只会得到更松的上界,没有意义
求和会重复叠加碰撞误差,偏差比取最小值大得多
optionExplanations_en: Correct: taking the minimum gives the tightest upper bound, exactly why it is called count-min.
An average is dragged up by collision-inflated counters and is not a tight bound.
Taking the maximum only gives a looser upper bound, which is not useful.
Summing compounds collision error across counters, worse than taking the minimum.

一棵平衡树
一个跳表
二维计数器阵列+多哈希
options_en: A bitmap plus a single hash function.
A balanced tree.
A skip list.
A 2D counter array with multiple hashes.

why_en: A Count-Min Sketch is a two-dimensional array of counters with one hash function per row, incrementing on insert and taking the row-wise minimum on query.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["event key"] --> B["d hash rows"]
  B --> C["increment counters"]
  C --> D["estimate = min row counts"]

平衡树维护的是有序结构,和固定大小的计数阵列无关

正确:二维计数器数组,每行配一个哈希函数,插入递增、查询取行最小值
optionExplanations_en: A bitmap plus one hash function describes a Bloom filter, not Count-Min Sketch.
A balanced tree maintains order; it is unrelated to a fixed-size counter array.
A skip list is also an ordered structure, not the backing structure of Count-Min Sketch.
Correct: a two-dimensional counter array with one hash function per row, incrementing on insert and taking the row minimum on query.

q: 两个极端:只用 1 个计数器,或给 N 个元素配 N 个专属计数器,分别会怎样?

options: 都能得到有用的近似
1 个坑毫无信息,N 个坑精确却不省空间
1 个计数器最省也最准;N 个计数器最浪费
两种都会导致假阴性
options_en: Both give a useful approximation.
One bucket gives no information, N buckets are exact but save nothing.
One counter is both cheapest and most accurate; N counters are the most wasteful.
Both extremes cause false negatives.
why: 1 个坑=所有人共享一个总数,上界毫无区分度;每人一个坑=精确计数但空间没省。CMS 的价值区间在中间:计数器数远小于唯一元素数仍能给有效上界。
why_en: One shared counter gives a useless bound and one counter per item is exact but saves nothing, so the sketch lives in between with far fewer counters than unique items.
optionExplanations: 1 个计数器时人人共享同一个数,给不出任何区分度
正确:1 个坑=毫无信息的共享上界;N 个坑=精确但不省空间
1 个计数器最省空间但完全没有区分度,谈不上“最准”
两种极端都不产生假阴性问题,CMS 本身也不会漏报

Correct: one bucket gives an uninformative shared bound; N buckets are exact but save nothing.
One counter saves the most space but has zero discrimination, so it is not 'most accurate'.
Neither extreme causes a false-negative issue; Count-Min Sketch itself never under-reports.

q: 补全二进制前缀的出现概率:
q_en: Fill in the occurrence probabilities for binary prefixes:
text: 一个均匀随机的二进制数以 1 开头的概率是 {{50%}},以 01 开头是 {{25%}},以 001 开头是 {{12.5%}}——前导零越多越罕见。
why:
每多一个前导零概率减半,所以“见过 k 个前导零”大致意味着见过约 2^k 个不同的值,这是 HLL 估计的数学根基。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Each extra leading zero halves the probability, so observing k leading zeros suggests roughly two to the k distinct values were seen.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: HyperLogLog 为什么要把哈希值分进多个桶(bucket)?

正确:哈希前 b 位选桶,靠多桶取平均降低单个罕见哈希带来的偏差
optionExplanations_en: Bucketing is unrelated to deletion; HyperLogLog does not support deletion at all.
Bucketing is not for parallelism; it is to reduce the variance of the estimate.
A bucket stores the max leading-zero count, not a storage-compression trick.

存完整哈希会让内存随元素数增长,违背了 HLL 省内存的目标

optionExplanations_en: Exact per-bucket counts are unrelated to how a HyperLogLog register actually stores data.
Correct: the register stores only the largest leading-zero count seen so far in that bucket, updated only on a new record.

q: HyperLogLog 的最终估计值是怎么从各桶寄存器算出来的?
q_en: How does HyperLogLog compute the final estimate from bucket registers?
options: 取调和平均,修正极端范围
取所有寄存器的最大值
取所有寄存器之和
取中位数寄存器
options_en: The harmonic mean, corrected at the extremes.
The maximum of all registers.
The sum of all registers.
The median register.
why: 调和平均对离群大值不敏感,配合对极端范围(很小或很大基数)的修正项,得到稳定的基数估计。
why_en: The estimate is the harmonic mean of all registers with corrections applied at the very small and very large ends.
optionExplanations: 正确:调和平均压低离群大值影响,再对极端范围做修正,给出稳定估计
取最大值会被单个偶然的大寄存器带偏,不稳定
求和没有意义,寄存器不是可加总的计数
中位数忽略了大部分寄存器携带的信息
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the harmonic mean dampens outlying large values, and corrections handle extreme ranges for a stable estimate.
Taking the max would be skewed by a single lucky large register — unstable.
Summing makes no sense; registers are not additive counts.
A median throws away information carried by most of the registers.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The harmonic mean averages the reciprocals of a set of numbers, which dampens the influence of outlying large values.

scenario: 面试官给出 HyperLogLog 的量级参考:约 1.5KB 内存 ≈ 2% 误差,3KB ≈ 1.6%,6KB ≈ 1.2%(误差与寄存器数 m 的平方根成反比)。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives HLL scale anchors: about 1.5 KB memory gives around 2% error, 3 KB gives around 1.6%, and 6 KB gives around 1.2%; error is inversely proportional to the square root of register count m.
q: 这组数字对“要不要为了更高精度加内存”的决定意味着什么?
q_en: What do these numbers imply about adding memory for more HLL accuracy?
options: 内存翻倍只把误差压到约 1/√2,收益递减——2% 已够用就不必再堆内存
内存翻倍误差也减半,应该不断加内存直到误差趋近于 0
这组数字说明 HLL 不适合十亿级数据,应换用精确 HashSet
只要给够内存,HyperLogLog 最终能做到零误差
options_en: Doubling memory only cuts error to about one over root two — diminishing returns, so stop once two percent is good enough.
Doubling memory halves the error too, so keep adding memory until error approaches zero.
These numbers mean HyperLogLog does not fit billion-scale data, so switch to an exact HashSet.
Given enough memory, HyperLogLog can eventually reach zero error.
why:
HLL 误差 ∝ 1/√m,内存翻倍只把误差除以约 1.4——收益递减很快,与其无脑加内存,不如先确认业务能接受的误差下限。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Because HyperLogLog error scales as one over the square root of the register count, doubling memory only cuts error by about thirty percent, so it pays off to size for the error your business actually needs rather than over-provisioning.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: HyperLogLog 是好选择的前提条件有哪些?(多选)

可用内存有限
能容忍小幅估计误差
需要能列出所有唯一元素
options_en: You need to count unique elements in a huge dataset.
Available memory is limited.
Small estimation error is tolerable.
You need to list every unique element.
why: HLL 的铁三角:去重计数 + 内存有限 + 容忍小误差。它只给数字,永远列不出具体有哪些元素。
why_en: HyperLogLog fits when you count unique items in huge data with limited memory and can tolerate small estimation errors.
optionExplanations: 正确:去重计数正是 HLL 存在的理由
正确:内存受限是选择近似结构而非精确 HashSet 的前提
正确:HLL 的估计天生带误差,必须能接受小幅偏差
HLL 只给数字,永远列不出具体是哪些元素
optionExplanations_en: Correct: counting unique items is exactly why HyperLogLog exists.
Correct: limited memory is the precondition for choosing an approximate structure over an exact HashSet.
Correct: HyperLogLog's estimate inherently carries error, so small deviations must be acceptable.
HyperLogLog only returns a number; it can never list which elements were seen.

q: HyperLogLog 的两个主要反模式是什么?
q_en: What are the two main HyperLogLog anti-patterns?
options: 数据是字符串;数据是数字
数据有序;数据无序
需要精确计数,或基数本来就很小
内存太大;内存太小
options_en: The data is strings; the data is numbers.
The data is ordered; the data is unordered.
You need exact counts, or the cardinality is naturally tiny.
Memory is too large; memory is too small.
why: 要精确就别用 HLL;基数很小也别用——几千个元素的 hash set 又准又便宜,套 HLL 只添误差和复杂度。
why_en: Avoid HyperLogLog when you need exact counts or when the unique set is small enough that a plain hash set is cheaper and exact.
optionExplanations: 数据类型不是 HLL 的反模式,它对字符串和数字都能哈希处理
有序无序也不是反模式,HLL 只关心哈希后的分布
正确:需要精确计数,或基数本来就很小,都不该用 HLL
内存大小本身不是反模式,是权衡的输入而非错误用法
optionExplanations_en: Data type is not the anti-pattern; HyperLogLog hashes strings and numbers alike.
Ordering is not the anti-pattern either; HyperLogLog only cares about the hashed distribution.
Correct: needing exact counts, or having a naturally tiny cardinality, are both poor fits for HyperLogLog.
Memory size itself is not the anti-pattern; it is an input to the tradeoff, not a misuse.

Correct: distinct search terms and unique IPs are both 'how many distinct X' questions.

只抽样 1% 的请求
用 Count-Min Sketch

q: 桶算法估计分位数时,误差上界由什么决定?

桶的宽度
哈希函数的质量
读取的并发度
options_en: The total data volume.
The bucket width.
The quality of the hash function.
The concurrency of reads.
why:
桶内的具体分布是未知的,只知道值落在桶范围内,所以误差上界就是桶宽——这也是桶边界设计如此重要的原因。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Quantile error is bounded by bucket width, so a ten-millisecond bucket means the estimate can be off by up to ten milliseconds.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 现代 DynamoDB 的分区定位机制与 2007 年 Dynamo 论文的区别是？
q_en: How does modern DynamoDB's partition-location mechanism differ from the 2007 Dynamo paper?
options: 现代 DynamoDB 用点对点哈希环，和论文一致
论文用中心化服务，现代版反而改用 gossip 协议
两者的分区定位机制完全相同，没有演进
现代版用中心化的分区映射服务定位节点；论文描述的是点对点哈希环
why:
概念上仍类似一致性哈希，但实现从 P2P 环换成了中心化的 partition map + placement service；该元数据服务还负责分区的自动拆分与合并。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Modern DynamoDB uses a centralized partition map and placement service consulted by request routers, unlike the peer-to-peer hash ring in the original Dynamo paper.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 把 DynamoDB 分区写入的底层流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the underlying steps of a DynamoDB partition write in the correct order:
steps: 写请求路由到该分区的 leader 节点
quorum（3 个中的 2 个）持久化日志记录后，写入即确认成功
leader 生成 WAL（写前日志）条目
leader 把日志条目发送给复制组的 peer 节点
why: 每个分区是一个基于 Multi-Paxos 的 3 节点 leader 复制组：leader 写 WAL → 发给 peers → 2/3 quorum 持久化即 ack。这解释了强一致读为什么找 leader。
why_en: The partition leader writes a WAL entry, sends it to its peers, and acknowledges the write once a quorum of two out of three persists it.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant L as Leader
    participant F1 as Follower1
    participant F2 as Follower2
    C->>L: 写请求
    L->>L: 生成 WAL 条目
    L->>F1: 发送日志
    L->>F2: 发送日志
    F1-->>L: 已持久化
    Note over L: quorum 2/3 达成
    L-->>C: 确认写入

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：写入先落日志再应用，保证持久性和可恢复性。

termDefinitions.meaning: 达成确认所需的最小副本数，这里是 3 副本中的 2 个。

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持连续多轮决议的 Paxos 共识协议变体，靠稳定 leader 做日志复制。

why:
这笔账的意义在于「gut check」：超高写入量在 DynamoDB 上成本可能高到不现实，这正是「成本效率」成为不选它的理由之一。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Ten million writes per second costs roughly one hundred fifty six thousand dollars a day on provisioned capacity, a sanity check on feasibility.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

About $1,500 per day.
About $156,000 a day -- a startling cost magnitude.
Within the free tier.

q: 把多数读设为最终一致读，在读容量（RCU）成本上有什么好处？
q_en: What read-capacity (RCU) cost benefit comes from making most reads eventually consistent?
options: 最终一致读省一半读容量。
两种读消耗完全相同，这个选择不影响成本
最终一致读免费，完全不计入读容量
只有强一致读会消耗读容量，最终一致读不计费
why:
最终一致读 0.5 RCU/4KB、强一致读 1 RCU/4KB；把大部分只读流量放在最终一致路径上，能直接把这部分读成本砍半。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Eventually consistent reads cost half the RCUs of strongly consistent reads, so routing most read-only traffic through the eventual path directly halves that read cost.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: 一个读多写少的服务把 90% 的读请求设为最终一致，只有下单确认页强制走强一致读。
scenario_en: A read-heavy service sets 90% of reads to eventual consistency, forcing strong consistency only on the order-confirmation page.

Strong and eventual reads consume exactly the same amount, so this choice does not affect cost.
Eventually consistent reads are free and never count against read capacity.
Only strongly consistent reads consume read capacity; eventual reads are not billed at all.

q: 补全 DynamoDB 的复制与读取路径：
q_en: Fill in DynamoDB's replication and read path:
text: 每个分区 {{3}} 个副本（1 个 {{leader}} + 2 个 follower），分布在 3 个{{可用区}}；写入经 leader 生成 {{WAL}} 并在 quorum（2/3）持久化后确认；强一致读走 leader，最终一致读任意副本可服务。
why: 一张卡记全复制拓扑：3 副本 3 AZ、leader 写入、quorum 确认、读路径按一致性分流。
why_en: Each partition keeps three replicas across availability zones, with the leader acknowledging writes at quorum and serving every strongly consistent read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：写入先落日志再应用，保证持久性和可恢复性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records a write before it is applied, guaranteeing durability and recoverability.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 数据中心的独立故障域；DynamoDB 默认跨 3 个 AZ 复制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Availability Zone is an independent failure domain in AWS, and DynamoDB replicates across three of them by default.

termDefinitions.meaning: 达成确认所需的最小副本数，这里是 3 副本中的 2 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas -- here two out of three -- that must acknowledge a write.

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Beyond roughly ten thousand results, from-size pagination becomes prohibitively expensive because all preceding documents must be fetched and sorted, which is the point to switch to a cursor like search_after.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

With one primary shard and Y replica shards, there are Y+1 shard copies that can serve reads, so read throughput scales to roughly X times Y plus one.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: keyBy 算子做了什么？
q_en: What does the keyBy operator do?
options: 把流里的数据写到对应的 Kafka 分区里
按键分流成 KeyedStream，状态按 key 独立

options_en: Write the stream's data out to the matching Kafka partition.
Partition the stream by key into a keyed stream, state kept independent per key.

Broadcast the stream as-is to every node in the cluster.
optionMeanings: 写 Kafka 分区
按 key 分区成 KeyedStream
全局排序
广播到所有节点
optionMeanings_en: Write the stream's data out to the matching Kafka partition.
Partition the stream by key into a keyed stream, state kept independent per key.
Perform a single global sort over the elements in the stream.
Broadcast the stream as-is to every node in the cluster.
why:
keyBy 是并行化和按键状态的基础：同 key 的事件路由到同一处理实例，窗口/状态对每个 key 各自独立。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
KeyBy partitions the stream by a key into a keyed stream, so state and windows are maintained independently per key.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

    K --> P2["partition B"]

      .withTimestampAssigner((event, ts) -> event.getTimestamp()));

q: 补全 Flink 的四种窗口类型：

text: {{Tumbling}}（滚动）窗口：固定大小、互不重叠；{{Sliding}}（滑动）窗口：固定大小、相互重叠；{{Session}}（会话）窗口：按活动动态定大小；{{Global}}（全局）窗口：自定义窗口逻辑。

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定大小、互不重叠的窗口，例如「每 5 分钟一个桶」。

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定大小但相互重叠、按滑动步长推进的窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sliding window is fixed-size but overlapping, advancing by a slide interval.

why: CEP（复杂事件处理）专门表达「事件序列 + 时间约束」的模式；filter 只能看单条事件，表达不了先后顺序。
why_en: Complex event processing expresses sequential patterns with time constraints, like a small test transaction followed within five minutes by a large one.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则只看单笔交易的属性（如金额超阈值），普通 filter/process 就够，不必上 CEP。
tradeoff: CEP 表达序列模式的能力 vs 普通 filter 的简单低成本
codeSample:
Pattern<EnrichedTransaction, ?> fraudPattern = Pattern.<EnrichedTransaction>begin("small-tx")
    .where(tx -> tx.getAmount() < 10.0)
    .next("large-tx")
    .where(tx -> tx.getAmount() > 1000.0)
    .within(Time.minutes(5));

DataStream<PatternAlert> alerts = CEP.pattern(
    enrichedTransactions.keyBy(t -> t.getCardId()), fraudPattern)
    .select(new PatternAlertSelector());

q: checkpoint barrier（屏障）是怎么工作的？

q: 把 Flink 的故障恢复流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put Flink failure recovery in the correct order:
steps: 整个作业暂停：所有任务（含健康节点上的）都停下
JobManager 发现某 TaskManager 心跳消失，标记其失败
作业从 checkpoint 恢复处理，保证 exactly-once
取回最近的 checkpoint，把失败节点的任务重新分配到健康节点
各任务恢复状态，source 回退到 checkpoint 时的位点（如 Kafka offset）
why: 检测 → 全作业暂停 → 取 checkpoint + 重分配 → 恢复状态 + 回退 source → 继续处理。代价是恢复期间全作业不可用，但换来一致的状态边界。
why_en: Flink detects the failure, pauses the whole job, restores from one checkpoint, rewinds sources, and pays downtime to keep state consistent.

    P --> R["取最近 checkpoint\n重分配任务"]
    R --> S["恢复状态 + source 回退"]
    S --> G["恢复处理 (exactly-once)"]

q_en: What goes wrong if match events are randomly spread across queue servers?
options: 事件乱序：进球出现在开赛之前、球员为还没发生的犯规吃牌

why:
队列各自独立消费，跨队列没有全局顺序：随机打散后同一场比赛的事件先后不可控——这正是要按实体分区的原因。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Randomly spreading events across queues destroys ordering, so a goal could appear before kickoff, which is exactly why related events must share one partition.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q_en: For interview purposes, how small should one Kafka message stay to avoid hurting memory and network use?
options: 偏小：10KB，超过就必须拆分，会强制把结构化事件拆得过碎
推荐上限：1MB，技术上无硬限制（可调 message.max.bytes），但建议压在这以下
偏大：100MB，接近视频文件也能塞，已经逼近建议上限的十倍以上
过大：1GB，可以直接放小视频，等同于把整段小视频直接塞进消息
why:
没有硬限制但建议压在 1MB 以下：这不是随口的推荐值，而是约束——超过它就该像视频这类大文件一样改存 S3、Kafka 只放指针，否则内存压力和网络利用率会明显变差。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
There is no hard limit, but keeping messages under roughly one megabyte is the recommendation, because anything bigger should move to S3 with only a pointer left in Kafka.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: Too small: 10KB, and anything larger must be split, forcing structured events to be chopped up unnecessarily.
Recommended ceiling: 1MB, with no hard limit technically (message.max.bytes is tunable), but recommended as the ceiling.
Too large: 100MB, large enough to fit even a small video, already an order of magnitude past the recommended ceiling.
Way too large: 1GB, enough to hold a short video directly, equivalent to stuffing an entire short video into one message.

q: 经验数量级：一台好硬件的 Kafka broker 大约能承载多少？
q_en: As a rough order of magnitude, what can one strong Kafka broker handle?
options: 存 ~1TB 数据、处理高达 ~100 万条消息/秒
存 ~10GB、处理 ~1 千条/秒
存 ~1PB、处理 ~10 亿条/秒
存 ~1MB、处理 ~100 条/秒
why:
粗略锚点：单 broker ~1TB 存储、~1M 消息/秒（取决于消息大小和硬件）。你的估算量级如果远低于这个数，扩展性就不是这轮面试要深入的重点。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A single broker on good hardware stores roughly a terabyte and handles up to about a million messages per second, a hand-wavy but useful anchor for deciding whether scaling deserves deep discussion.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

scenario_en: The cluster added new brokers for scale, but nobody changed the partition count of the existing topic.
q: 往集群里加了新 broker，但 topic 的分区数没跟上，会怎样？
q_en: What happens if you add brokers but do not increase the topic's partition count?
options: 新 broker 会自动切分现有分区，Kafka 并不会主动帮你重新切分

why:

If a topic is under-partitioned, newly added brokers cannot take on any load, so more partitions must accompany more brokers.

q: 在这个前提下，最简单的热分区解法是？

scenario: 还想保留一定的 key 结构，但要把爆款广告的流量摊到多个分区，能接受消费端聚合变复杂。
scenario_en: You still want a key structure, but you can accept more complex consumer aggregation to spread a viral ad across partitions.
q: 这种把热 key 拆开分摊的手法叫什么？
q_en: What is this technique for splitting a hot key across partitions called?
options: 背压（back pressure），只调发送速度，不改变 key 到分区的映射
增加副本因子（replication factor），影响的是容错，跟单 key 流量分布无关
干脆不设 key 分发，会连同一广告内部的关联信息也一起丢掉
随机加盐（salting）：ad id 拼上随机数或时间戳做分区 key
why:
加盐把一个热 key 拆成多个分区 key，负载摊开；代价是同一广告的数据散在多个分区，消费端聚合逻辑变复杂。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Salting appends a random number to the hot key to spread it across partitions, at the cost of more complex consumer-side aggregation.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 若存在天然的第二维度（地域、用户段），复合 key 比随机盐更可控、聚合也更自然。
tradeoff: 加盐换来负载分摊 vs 复合 key 换来更可控的聚合

q: 「背压（back pressure）」方案具体是怎么做的？
q_en: How does the back-pressure approach work here?
options: 直接丢弃超出容量的消息，意味着数据永久丢失，不符合可靠性要求
把热分区手动迁到更大的机器，同一个 key 依旧还是那个热 key

why:
背压 = 让生产者感知下游压力并降速，简单直接；代价是数据进入系统变慢。

Back pressure has the producer watch partition lag and slow down when it grows too high, a simple fix if you can tolerate the delay.

API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 把「热分区应对」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the hot-partition response chain in the right order:
steps: 缓解：无 key / 随机加盐 / 复合 key / 背压，按顺序要求选择
现象：爆款广告使单个分区流量激增
代价：失去顺序保证，或消费端聚合逻辑变复杂
原因：partition = hash(key) % N，同一个热 key 永远打进同一分区

现象→原因→缓解→代价：先解释哈希分区为什么造成热点，再给出方案并说清新引入的成本。

q: 补全常见的复制配置：
q_en: Fill in the common replication setup:
text: 复制因子（replication factor）为 {{3}} 是常见配置：每个分区共 3 个副本 = {{1}} 个 leader + {{2}} 个 follower；一台 broker 挂掉，数据仍在另外两台上。
why: RF=3 是耐用性和成本的常见平衡点：单 broker 故障后仍有两份数据，可以立刻提升一个 follower 顶上。
why_en: A replication factor of three means one leader plus two followers, so data survives a single broker failure and a follower can be promoted right away.

scenario: 你设计的系统只需要支持「最近 3 天内」补处理失败的消费者重放，没人告诉你要改过默认配置。
scenario_en: Your system only needs to replay failed consumer work from the last three days, and nobody changed the default retention config.
q: 面试要点：不特意配置的话，Kafka 会把消息留存多长时间，这对你的重放窗口设计意味着什么？
q_en: By default, how long does Kafka retain messages, and what does that mean for your replay window?
options: 偏短：1 小时，比你需要的重放窗口短得多，必须显式调大
仍偏短：24 小时，同样短于 3 天的需求，仍需调整 retention.ms
默认恰好够用：7 天，已经覆盖你 3 天的重放需求，不用改配置
误判成永久：以为默认不清理，其实并非无限，需要主动设上限控制存储成本
why:
这是一个默认配置值，不是算出来的：默认保留 7 天，已经盖住了 3 天的重放需求；如果需求变成 30 天，才需要显式调大 retention.ms 并承担更高的存储成本。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
This is a default setting, not a computed number: the default seven-day retention already covers a three-day replay need, and only a longer requirement would force you to raise retention.ms at extra storage cost.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

Default is just enough: 7 days, already covers your 3-day replay need, no config change required.

q: 下面哪种 send 写法能满足「同一用户事件按序处理」这个要求？
q_en: Which kafkajs send call preserves per-user event order?
options: messages: [{ value: JSON.stringify(order) }]（不带 key）

tradeoff: 按 userId 分区换来同用户内顺序 vs 无 key/随机 key 换来更均匀的分布

why:
这些是粗略估算锚点，不是精确 SLA：join/聚合越复杂，该留的吞吐预算越低；全表扫描快不快，关键在数据是否装得进内存。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
These are rough interview anchors, not SLAs: heavier joins need a lower throughput budget, and full-scan speed depends on whether data fits in memory.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 低冲突竞价可用哪种应用层并发控制？
options: 无条件 UPDATE：不查 version，直接覆盖当前行
关闭事务：让读写不再受原子提交保护
OCC：按数据库 version 条件更新，失败后重读重试
Cookie version：把客户端版本当唯一裁判
options_en: Unconditional UPDATE: do not check version; overwrite the current row.
Disable transactions: remove atomic commit protection from reads and writes.
OCC: update by database version, then reload and retry if it fails.
Cookie version: treat the client-side version as the only judge.
tradeoff: 提前加锁避免冲突 vs 写入时检测冲突
why: OCC 的 version 在数据库行里。客户端只带回刚读到的旧值；UPDATE 用 WHERE version = 5 判断这行是否被改过。
why_en: In OCC, the version is stored on the database row. The client only sends back the version it read, and the UPDATE succeeds only if the row still has that version.
whenOtherWins: 如果同一拍卖行冲突频繁，SELECT FOR UPDATE 这类 row-level locking 更直接，能减少反复失败和重试。

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant DB as Postgres
  C->>DB: SELECT maxBid, version
  DB-->>C: maxBid=90, version=5
  C->>DB: UPDATE ... WHERE id=123 AND version=5
  alt row still version 5
    DB-->>C: 1 row updated, version becomes 6
  else row already changed
    DB-->>C: 0 rows updated, reload and retry
  end

API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 补全邻近搜索的根本问题:
q_en: Complete the root problem in proximity search:
text: 根本问题是{{一维}}的排序顺序无法保留{{二维}}的邻近性——把地图压平到一条排序轴上,地面上相邻的点可能在索引里离得{{很远}}。

q: 在四叉树里做邻近搜索,候选集由什么组成?

q: 四叉树在规模上的第一个麻烦——"深度问题"是什么?

q: 四叉树在规模上的第二个麻烦——"磁盘问题"是什么?

q: 候选粗筛和门牌级定位分别该用几位 geohash 前缀?
q_en: How many geohash prefix characters should coarse candidate filtering and door-level precision use?
options: 两步统一用 9 位前缀,精度越高越保险,门牌级也能覆盖粗筛
粗筛用约 5 位前缀圈公里范围,门牌定位再用更长前缀——按用途选精度
两步统一用 5 位前缀,反正后面还有精确距离过滤兜底
geohash 长度和覆盖范围其实无关,固定用 6 位就够
why:
5 位前缀能圈出公里级候选;如果粗筛就上 9 位,格子太小、边界效应更频繁,反而会漏掉刚好跨格子的候选。精度要按这一步的用途选,不是越长越好。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Pick the geohash prefix length by purpose: a short prefix casts a wide candidate net, a long one is only for final house-number precision.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: 打车软件先用 geohash 前缀圈出一批候选司机做粗筛,后续还要给用户展示最终选中门店的精确门牌定位。已知 geohash 每加一个字符,覆盖范围就按约 32 倍收缩面积:5 位约 5 公里(街区级),9 位约 5 米(门牌级)。
scenario_en: A ride-hailing app first uses a geohash prefix to collect candidate drivers, then later displays an exact storefront or door-level point. Each added geohash character shrinks area by about 32x: 5 chars is about 5 km, 9 chars is about 5 m.
options_en: Use a 9-character prefix for both steps — more precision is always safer, even for coarse filtering.
Use a roughly 5-character prefix to cast a kilometer-wide candidate net, then a longer prefix for house-number precision — pick the length by purpose.
Use a 5-character prefix for both steps since exact distance filtering happens later anyway.
Geohash length has nothing to do with coverage area; just always use 6 characters.

q: 哪条 SQL 能直接利用现有索引完成粗筛?
q_en: Which SQL can use an existing index for coarse filtering?
options: SELECT * FROM places WHERE geohash = 'dr5ru'
SELECT * FROM places WHERE geohash LIKE '%dr5ru'
SELECT * FROM places WHERE distance(lat, lng, ?, ?) < 5000
SELECT * FROM places WHERE geohash LIKE 'dr5ru%'
why: LIKE 'dr5ru%' 是普通的 B-tree 前缀扫描——和任何文本列上的前缀查询一模一样,这正是 geohash 的威力:邻近查询跑在任意数据库的普通索引上。
why_en: A LIKE prefix scan on the geohash column is an ordinary B-tree range scan, which is exactly how geohash makes proximity queries run on any database.
whenOtherWins: 查询点贴着格子边界时,单前缀会漏掉隔壁格子里更近的对象——必须升级为 3x3 九宫格查询加精确距离后过滤。

SELECT id, geohash FROM places
WHERE geohash LIKE 'dr5ru%';
-- 之后仍需对候选做精确距离后过滤

text: 形状用{{空间树}},移动点用{{编码 cell}},并且永远、永远{{后过滤}}。

q: 把"为位置功能做索引选型"的决策链排成正确顺序:
q_en: Put the decision chain for choosing a location index in order:
steps: 对候选集做精确距离/几何计算,得到最终答案
判断数据的形状:是多边形/道路等几何体,还是高频移动的点
选路线:几何体 → 空间树(PostGIS/ES);移动点 → 编码键(geohash/S2/H3)
用索引把"查每一行"缩小成一小撮候选(前缀扫描 / IN 查询 / 矩形下钻)

why_en: Decide by data shape, pick tree or encoded key accordingly, generate a small candidate set, and finish with exact math.

q: 这个量级最支持下面哪条设计判断?
q_en: Which design judgment does this scale fact support?
options: 全球尺度该换 S2/H3 球面网格,而非平面 geohash
只要把 geohash 的精度多加几位字符就够
高纬度地区可以直接跳过索引,全表扫描兜底
这个数字只影响地图渲染效果,不影响索引选型
why:
111 公里到 0 的收缩说明同一级 geohash 格子在赤道是胖方块、在高纬是细长条,面积不一致会让候选集在不同纬度表现完全不同。要在全球尺度保持一致,必须换成 S2/H3 这类尊重球面的编码。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Longitude spans about 111km at the equator but shrinks toward zero at the poles, so flat geohash cells get uneven — that pushes global-scale indexes toward S2 or H3.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: 地图服务要在伦敦、新加坡、雷克雅未克等不同纬度的城市统一做同城 5 公里邻近召回;已知一度经度的地面距离在赤道约 111 公里,向两极收缩趋近于 0。
scenario_en: A map service must do uniform 5 km in-city recall across London, Singapore, and Reykjavik. One degree of longitude is about 111 km at the equator and shrinks toward 0 near the poles.

q: 关于各方案的 ID 位数,哪组数字正确?
q_en: Which set of ID bit widths is correct?
options: geohash 每字符是 8 bit,S2 与 H3 都用 32 位 ID
geohash 每字符只有 4 bit,S2 与 H3 用 128 位 ID
geohash 每字符 5 bit,Redis 存 52 位,S2/H3 都是 64 位
三者其实都采用不定长的 ID 编码方式
why:
32 个格子恰是 5 bit,Redis geo 用 52 位整数存 sorted set score,S2/H3 都是 64 位层级 ID。建表该选 bigint(64 位),三种编码都装得下。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Each geohash character is five bits, Redis stores a 52-bit geohash integer, and S2 and H3 both use 64-bit cell IDs, so a 64-bit bigint column fits any of them.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. q: 这个 fsync 频率的量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 关键写入要么接受约 1 秒的丢失窗口，要么改成每写 fsync 或换真正持久化的实现
默认配置和关系型数据库一样是提交即落盘
丢失窗口只取决于网络延迟，与 fsync 频率无关
只要打开了 AOF 就等于零丢失，不需要额外设计
why:
每秒 fsync 划出一个约 1 秒的丢失窗口：能接受就用默认配置换速度，不能接受就改每写 fsync 或换 MemoryDB 这类真正持久化的实现。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
The once-per-second fsync policy leaves a roughly one-second loss window, so critical writes need per-write fsync or a truly durable store instead of the defaults.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: AOF 默认策略是每秒 fsync 一次；你要为「已确认写入」写一份诚实的持久性说明给业务方。

why_en: MemoryDB is a Redis-compatible durable primary database, but Redis or ElastiCache is usually better when the data is only a rebuildable cache.
whenOtherWins: 若只是可重建缓存，Redis/ElastiCache/Memcached 更轻；AWS 新项目还要评估带持久性的 ElastiCache。
options_en: Stock Redis defaults: fastest, but acknowledged writes may still have a loss window.
Redis RDB plus AOF: safer, but still depends on the fsync policy.
AWS MemoryDB: Redis-compatible, confirms writes after the Multi-AZ log.
Memcached: pure cache; data is lost on restart or node failure.
tradeoff: 持久主数据库 vs 纯缓存/弱持久 Redis

MemoryDB 用 Redis 接口，但把自己当持久主库。

q: 这个「槽数量在集群运行期间固定」的设计，最支持哪个判断？
options: 扩缩容 = 重新分配槽归属哪个节点，而不是重新对所有 key 哈希
每加一个节点，哈希函数本身都要跟着重新调整算法
槽的总数必须精确等于集群里的节点数量
槽总数会随着集群规模自动增加或减少
why:
槽数固定意味着扩缩容只是把一部分槽（连同其中的 key）挪给新节点，客户端和哈希函数完全不用变。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Because the slot count is fixed, scaling only reassigns which node owns a share of the slots, leaving the hash function and clients untouched.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 这个耗时量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 命令本身很少是瓶颈，优化重点应放在减少网络往返（pipeline/MGET）
命令执行本身是主要瓶颈，要用 Lua 脚本替换所有命令
微秒级执行意味着可以放心做同步跨机房调用
既然命令很快，热点 key 就不需要任何缓解手段
why:
命令本身只花微秒，真正决定观感延迟的是网络往返次数，这正是 pipeline/MGET 划算的原因。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Since a command itself costs only microseconds, the number of network round trips dominates perceived latency, which is why pipelining and MGET pay off.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
scenario: 一条 Redis 命令在服务器上的执行只有微秒级开销，网络往返才是你看到的亚毫秒延迟的主因。

Command execution is the main bottleneck, so replace every command with a Lua script
Microsecond execution means synchronous cross-region calls are safe
Since commands are fast, hot keys need no mitigation at all
q_en: Which design conclusion does this latency order of magnitude best support?

scenario: Ticketmaster 式抢座：多台应用服务器并发处理同一张票，同一时刻只允许一个进程操作，且锁要能在持有者崩溃后自动释放。
q: 获取锁的正确命令是？
options: SETNX lock:concert:343 1（不带过期时间）
SET lock:concert:343 my-token NX EX 30
先 GET 判断不存在再 SET
INCR lock:concert:343
why: NX 保证只有 key 不存在时才写入成功（即抢到锁），EX 30 让崩溃的持有者最多占 30 秒，随机 token 是稍后安全释放的凭证。
why_en: SET with NX and EX atomically creates the lock only if absent and adds an expiry so a crashed holder cannot keep it forever.
whenOtherWins: 若被保护的数据就在数据库里，SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 行锁或条件 UPDATE 往往能直接取代分布式锁，更简单也更安全。
codeSample:
SET lock:concert:343 my-token NX EX 30
# OK  -> 抢到锁
# nil -> 已被占用，等待后重试

SET lock:concert:343 my-token NX EX 30
GET to check absence, then SET separately
INCR lock:concert:343
tradeoff: 原子获取 + 自动过期 vs 无过期时间的锁永远占用风险

scenario: 对每个 API key 做固定窗口限流：窗口内最多 N 次请求，超出返回 429 并带 Retry-After 头。

why: INCR 原子地自增并返回新值，一条命令完成「计数 + 读数」；配合窗口过期就是固定窗口限流器。

whenOtherWins: 固定窗口在窗口边界可能被打出双倍突刺；要平滑限速就改用有序集合做滑动窗口。

INCR the current window's counter key and reject once it exceeds N

q: 补全 Stream 工作队列的命令分工：
text: 生产者用 {{XADD}} 追加条目；工作者通过消费组用 {{XREADGROUP}} 领取条目；超时未确认的条目可被其他工作者用 {{XCLAIM}}（或 XAUTOCLAIM）抢过来重做。
why: 工作队列链路是：XADD 入流，XREADGROUP 分给 worker，成功后 XACK；没 XACK 会留在 PEL，超时后用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管。
why_en: The queue loop is XADD to append, XREADGROUP to deliver, XACK to finish, and XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM to recover idle pending entries.
codeSample:
XGROUP CREATE jobs workers $ MKSTREAM
XADD jobs * kind email user 42
XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 1 STREAMS jobs >
# worker-1 dies before XACK; entry stays in PEL
XCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 {entry-id}
XAUTOCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 0-0 COUNT 10
XACK jobs workers {entry-id}

termDefinitions.meaning: XADD：向 Stream 追加一条新记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XADD appends a new entry to a stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: XREADGROUP：消费组里的 worker 用它领取 Stream 里的新条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XREADGROUP is how a worker in a consumer group reads new entries from a stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把一个超时未确认的条目转交给另一个 worker 重新处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a stalled, unacknowledged stream entry to another worker to reprocess.

q: Redis Streams 工作队列里，worker 取到任务后崩溃，未确认任务如何恢复？
scenario: 生产者用 XADD 写入任务，worker 用 XREADGROUP 领取任务；只有处理成功并 XACK 后，这条任务才算完成。
options: 未 XACK 的任务永久丢失，不再恢复
Redis 自动重启崩溃 worker，再继续原任务
idle 超时后，用 XCLAIM 转给其他 worker 重做
主节点重新广播任务，让所有 worker 抢处理
why: 未 XACK 的条目会留在 PEL，记录 owner 和 idle。idle 超阈值后，其他 worker 用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管并重做。
why_en: Unacknowledged stream entries stay in the PEL, so another worker can claim an idle entry with XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM and retry it.
tradeoff: 故障恢复与至少一次处理 vs 重复执行风险
whenOtherWins: 若任务不能重复执行，业务层要加去重键或状态机；Redis 重新交付，但不保证只执行一次。

flowchart LR

    G --> W1[worker1 XREADGROUP]
    W1 --> PEL[PEL: delivered, not XACKed]
    W1 -. crashes .-> PEL
    PEL -- idle exceeds threshold --> W2[worker2 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM]
    W2 --> R[redo work]
    R --> A[XACK removes from PEL]

q: 100 节点的 Redis 缓存集群，某个商品突然爆红、流量占到全站一半，会发生什么？
options: 集群检测到热点后会自动触发一次槽再均衡
这份流量会被所有 100 台节点平均分摊
Redis 检测到热点后自动把这个 key 复制到多个节点
拥有这个 key 的那台节点负载暴涨、开始失败，其余 99 台闲着
why:
key 哈希决定归属：一个 key 只住一台节点，节点再多也分不走单 key 的流量——这就是 hot key 问题（Memcached、DynamoDB 同样有）。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A single hot key lives on one node, so that node melts while the other ninety-nine idle, a problem Memcached and DynamoDB share.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
diagram:
flowchart TD

  B --> C["Replicas or key copies"]
  C --> D["Fan out reads"]

Redis detects the hot spot and automatically replicates this key across nodes

q: 最合适的缓解是？
options: 应用服务器进程内缓存这几个最热 key（配短 TTL）
单纯加大拥有热 key 的那台 Redis 节点的内存
把持久化模式从 RDB 换成 AOF

q: 「key 副本」方案怎么做？
options: 只是把 key 的名字改得更短一点，指望能减少内存占用
同一份数据存成 product:123:1..10 多个 key 散到不同槽，读者随机挑后缀读
用 hash tag 反而把这些数据副本全部绑到同一个槽上
打开集群自带的代理转发模式，指望它来分摊流量
why: 带不同后缀的 key 哈希到不同节点，读流量被随机打散；代价是每次写要扇出到所有副本，读者还得知道哪些 key 被复制过。
why_en: Storing copies under suffixed keys spreads them across nodes and readers pick a random suffix, while every write must fan out to all copies.
whenOtherWins: 写频繁的 key 不适合（写扇出放大）；那种情况优先在数据模型上拆分，或用副本读扛读热。

Store the data under suffixed keys like product:123:1 through 10 spread across slots, readers pick a random suffix
Use a hash tag to pin all of these data copies onto that very same slot instead
Turn on the cluster's built-in proxy forwarding mode, hoping it spreads the traffic
tradeoff: 读流量摊到多节点 vs 每次写扇出到全部副本的额外成本

why_en: Replicas only absorb load if clients are configured for replica reads, and they do nothing for a write-hot key since writes still hit the one primary.

Replica nodes simply cannot be deployed to a different region or availability zone
Cluster clients still read the primary by default (replica reads must be explicit), and replicas do nothing for write-hot keys
The mere existence of multiple replicas directly causes cluster split-brain

q: 什么时候该选择时间序列数据库（TSDB）？
q_en: When should you choose a time-series database (TSDB)?
options: 只要数据里有 timestamp 字段就必须用 TSDB
当业务需要强事务和复杂外键约束时
当通用数据库在高写入、时间范围查询、保留策略和压缩上出现真实瓶颈时
当核心需求是跨全部 series 做 Top-K 排序时
why: 决定性约束是通用数据库先撑不住高写入、时间范围查询或保留/压缩需求；仅有 timestamp 字段不构成理由。先用 Postgres/DynamoDB 顶，顶不住再上专用系统。
why_en: A time-series database is worth adopting once a general-purpose database genuinely bottlenecks on write volume, time-range queries, or retention, not just because the data happens to have a timestamp.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询核心是跨海量 series 的全局排序或强事务/复杂 join，Postgres/DynamoDB 等通用方案通常更直接。
tradeoff: 专用 TSDB 的写入/压缩优化 vs 通用数据库的事务与关系能力
options_en: Any time your data has a timestamp field, you must use a TSDB.
When the business needs strong transactions and complex foreign keys.
When a general-purpose database hits real bottlenecks on high write volume, time-range queries, retention, and compression.
When the core need is Top-K ranking across all series.

q: 在磁盘 I/O 模式上，append-only 写入相比传统原地更新的优势是什么？
q_en: For disk I/O, what advantage does append-only writing have over traditional in-place updates?
options: 它让每次写入都必须先随机寻址到旧 block 再修改

它保证所有查询都不必再使用任何索引

why: 原地更新要先定位旧位置再读改写，产生随机 I/O；append-only 只在文件尾追加，把随机变顺序，代价是空间需要靠后台整理回收。
why_en: In-place updates need to locate, read, modify, and rewrite old data, causing random I/O, while append-only writes sequentially at the end and reclaims space later via background compaction.
tradeoff: 顺序追加换取写入吞吐 vs 原地更新换取即时空间复用

memtable 满后顺序刷盘成不可变的有序 SSTable

flowchart LR

SSTable --> Compaction[Background compaction]
Compaction --> Larger[Large sorted files]
Query[Query] --> Memtable
Query --> SSTable

q: LSM（Log-Structured Merge Tree）的 memtable 为什么通常保持有序？
q_en: Why is the memtable in an LSM tree usually kept sorted?
options: 为了让所有写入都必须等待磁盘完成排序后才算成功
为了强制所有查询必须全表扫描，不能走索引
为了把每个 key 随机分散写到不同文件，避免热点
为了刷盘后直接生成有序 SSTable，方便二分查找、范围扫描和后续合并
why: 内存里排序成本低，刷盘时直接顺序写出有序文件；有序文件支持二分查找、范围扫描，也让后台 merge-sort compaction 更高效。
why_en: A sorted memtable flushes into a sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, efficient ranges, and merge-based compaction.
options_en: So that every write must wait for the disk to finish sorting before it's considered successful.
So that every query is forced to do a full scan instead of using an index.
So that each key is randomly scattered across different files to avoid hotspots.
So that flushing produces an already-sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, range scans, and later merge-based compaction.

误以为有序结构会禁止索引查询。
误以为有序是为了打散 key 分布。
有序 memtable 刷盘后直接是有序 SSTable。
