options: 牺牲所有写入能力，换取只读性能
牺牲部分读性能和写放大，换取高写入吞吐
牺牲压缩能力，换取更高空间占用
完全没有任何后台开销，因此性能只受磁盘限制
why: 读可能要查多个 SSTable，compaction 会重写数据产生写放大。它适合高写入场景，而不是所有 workload 的默认答案。
why_en: LSM trees trade some read cost and write amplification for much higher write throughput.
tradeoff: 高写入吞吐 vs 读放大与写放大
options_en: It gives up all write capability in exchange for read-only performance.
It trades some read performance and write amplification for much higher write throughput.
It gives up compression capability in exchange for higher space usage.
It has zero background overhead, so performance is limited only by disk.

q: 补全 delta encoding 的思想：
q_en: Complete the idea behind delta encoding:
text: Delta encoding 不反复存完整值，而是存相邻值之间的 {{difference}}；时间序列相邻点通常变化小，所以这些 delta 更容易被 {{compressed}}。
why: CPU、内存、流量等指标通常连续且变化平滑，delta 值比原始值小。配合可变长编码能显著降低存储。
why_en: Delta encoding stores differences between adjacent values, which compress well when time-series data changes gradually.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["t1 t2 t3"] --> B["deltas"]
  B --> C["delta of delta"]
  C --> D["compressed block"]
codeSample:
Raw values:     45.2  45.3  45.1  45.4
Delta encoded:  45.2  +0.1  -0.2  +0.3
# 只存差值，差值比原值小很多，更容易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 存相邻值之间的差而不是完整值的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores the difference between adjacent values instead of the full value each time.

q: varint（variable-length encoding，变长整数编码）在 TSDB 压缩中解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does varint, or variable-length encoding, solve in TSDB compression?
options: 让所有字符串自动转换成图片格式存储
强制每条记录都补齐到固定 1MB 大小
让数值小的整数只占 1-2 字节，而不是固定 4/8 字节
让浮点数从此无法用任何方式存储
why: delta 往往是小数值，varint 能让小值占用 1-2 个字节。它放大了 delta encoding 的空间收益。
why_en: Variable-length encoding stores small deltas in fewer bytes instead of always using a fixed-width integer.
options_en: It automatically converts all strings into image format for storage.
It forces every record to pad out to a fixed 1MB size.
It lets small integers take only 1-2 bytes instead of a fixed 4 or 8 bytes.
It makes floating-point numbers impossible to store at all.

varint(1)        = 0x01            (1 byte)
varint(300)      = 0xAC 0x02       (2 bytes)
varint(1000000)  = 0xC0 0x84 0x3D  (3 bytes)
# 值越小，占用字节越少；delta 编码后大多是小数值

q: 时间戳 delta-of-delta（二阶差分）编码为什么对固定采样间隔特别有效？
q_en: Why is timestamp delta-of-delta encoding especially effective for fixed sampling intervals?
options: 因为 timestamp 不能被排序
因为相邻 timestamp 的间隔经常相同，二阶差分大量为 0
因为它会丢弃真实采样时间，只保留序号
因为所有 timestamp 都必须先转成字符串再比较
why: 如果每 10 秒采样一次，timestamp 的 delta 基本恒定，delta-of-delta 接近 0。大量 0 非常容易压缩。
why_en: Delta-of-delta compression works well because regular sampling intervals make second-order timestamp deltas mostly zero.
options_en: Because timestamps cannot be sorted.
Because the interval between adjacent timestamps is often constant, so second-order deltas are mostly zero.
Because it discards the real sample time and keeps only a sequence number.
Because every timestamp must first be converted to a string before comparison.
codeSample:
Raw timestamps:   1000  1010  1020  1030  1040
Deltas:              10    10    10    10
Delta-of-delta:            0     0     0
# 间隔恒定 → 二阶差分几乎全 0 → 极易压缩

q: TSDB 对浮点值常用 XOR 压缩的直觉是什么？
q_en: What is the intuition behind XOR compression for floating-point values in a TSDB?
options: 浮点数在时间序列里完全无法做任何压缩处理
XOR 运算会把所有数值变成同一个常数输出
XOR 压缩只对文本字符串生效，对浮点数无效
相邻浮点值接近时，XOR 后多数 bit 是 0，只需存差异部分
why: 相邻指标值通常很接近，二进制表示也有大量相同位。XOR 后只保留有意义的差异位，能显著减少空间。
why_en: XOR compression exploits similar adjacent floating-point values because their XOR contains many zero bits.
options_en: Floating-point values in time series can't be compressed at all.
XOR turns all values into the same constant output.
XOR compression only works on text strings, not floats.
When adjacent float values are close, XORing them leaves mostly zero bits, so only the differing part needs to be stored.

q: Time-based partitioning 在 TSDB 中的含义是什么？
q_en: What does time-based partitioning mean in a TSDB?
options: 按用户名哈希把数据随机拆分成数量不受控的表
把所有历史数据永远放进一个不可删除的大文件
按时间窗口把数据切成不同 partition/chunk，比如按天或按周划分
只根据 metric 的数值大小做分区，不看时间
why:
时间序列查询天然带时间范围，按时间窗口组织能让写入、读取和保留策略都更简单。不同 partition 可以在同机或多机上。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Time-based partitioning groups points into time-windowed chunks such as daily or weekly partitions.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: Time-based partitioning 带来哪些收益？
q_en: What benefits does time-based partitioning provide?
options: 所有高基数标签都会自动变低基数
新写入集中到当前时间 partition
保留策略可直接 drop 旧 partition
时间范围查询可以跳过不相关 partition
why:
按时间组织同时优化写入局部性、查询裁剪和数据过期。它不能解决 tag cardinality 爆炸。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Time partitions localize writes, prune reads by time range, and make retention as simple as dropping old partitions.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: All high-cardinality tags automatically become low-cardinality.
New writes concentrate on the current time partition.
Retention can simply drop entire old partitions.
Time-range queries can skip irrelevant partitions.

q: Bloom filter（布隆过滤器）在 LSM/TSDB 读取路径中的作用是什么？
q_en: What role does a Bloom filter play in the LSM/TSDB read path?
options: 保证所有聚合查询完全不需要读取任何磁盘数据

q: Bloom filter 的 false positive / false negative 特性是什么？

options: 它有时会漏掉真实存在的 key，即产生 false negative
它保证零误差，既没有 false positive 也没有 false negative
它可能误报“也许有”但实际没有；绝不会漏报“没有”但实际有
它只能用于对 key 做精确计数，不能做成员判断
why: Bloom filter 的核心保证是 no false negatives。false positive 只会导致多读一次文件，不会漏结果。
why_en: Bloom filters can have false positives but no false negatives, so they may cause extra reads but do not miss existing keys.
tradeoff: 多读几次文件（false positive）vs 绝不漏掉真实数据（no false negative）
options_en: It sometimes misses keys that really exist, producing a false negative.
It guarantees zero error, with neither false positives nor false negatives.
It may falsely say maybe-present when absent, but never falsely says absent when the key is actually present.
It can only be used for exact key counting, not membership checks.

q: Downsampling / rollup 在 TSDB 中解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem do downsampling and rollups solve in a TSDB?
options: 让所有原始数据永远保持最高分辨率并无限复制
把时间戳删除，使数据无法按时间查询
把老数据降到更粗粒度，减少历史查询需要扫描的数据量
只用于加密用户密码
why: 近期数据常需要高分辨率，历史数据通常只看趋势。rollup 用更粗的时间桶保存预聚合结果，换取更快历史查询和更低存储。
why_en: Downsampling stores lower-resolution rollups for older data so historical queries scan far fewer points.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Raw points"] --> B["1m buckets"]
  B --> C["5m rollup"]
  C --> D["Long range query"]

Delete timestamps so data can no longer be queried by time.
Reduce older data to coarser granularity so historical queries scan far less data.
It is only used to encrypt user passwords.

scenario: Dashboard 把一天历史数据用 5 分钟粒度的 rollup 展示，而不是原始 10 秒采样点。
scenario_en: A dashboard shows one day of history using 5-minute rollups instead of raw 10-second samples.
q: 相比直接扫描原始 10 秒采样点，用 5 分钟 rollup 回答“过去一天趋势”的查询，设计上带来了什么？
q_en: Compared with scanning raw 10-second samples, what does a 5-minute rollup change for a past-day trend query?
options: 扫描的数据点数量完全不变，只是换了一种展示方式
查询需要扫描的数据点数量级下降，历史大范围查询明显更快，但会牺牲一部分时间精度
rollup 会让查询变慢，因为要先做聚合计算
rollup 只影响存储成本，不影响查询要扫描多少数据
why:
原始 10 秒采样一天有 8,640 点，5 分钟 rollup 只有 288 个桶，两个数量级的差距直接决定长范围查询要扫多少数据。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Raw 10-second sampling produces 8,640 points a day while 5-minute rollups produce only 288 buckets, and that order-of-magnitude gap is what makes long-range queries fast.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: The number of points scanned stays exactly the same; only the display changes.
The number of points to scan drops by orders of magnitude, making large historical queries much faster at the cost of some time resolution.
Rollups make queries slower because they require upfront aggregation.
Rollups only affect storage cost, not how much data a query scans.

tags 和 fields 在存储和查询上完全没有区别，可以互换使用

q: 把典型 TSDB 写入/存储引擎步骤按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the typical TSDB write/storage engine steps in order:
steps: buffer 达到阈值后刷盘成不可变压缩文件
数据写入 WAL 以便崩溃恢复
后台 compaction 合并小文件、减少查询要检查的文件数
数据进入按 measurement/tag 组织的内存 buffer
why: WAL 负责 durability，buffer 负责吸收新写入，flush 生成压缩文件，compaction 再优化读取路径。这个组合就是很多 TSDB 的核心写路径。
why_en: A TSDB often writes to the WAL, buffers points in memory, flushes compressed immutable files, and compacts them in the background.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Point[Metric point] --> WAL[WAL]
Point --> Buffer[In-memory buffer]
Buffer --> File[Compressed immutable file]
File --> Compact[Background compaction]
Compact --> QueryFiles[Query-optimized files]

q_en: Complete the key TSDB data assumptions:
text: TSDB 的高性能依赖一些假设：tags 的 cardinality 较 {{low}}，采样时间较 {{regular}}，相邻数据点的 delta 较 {{small}}。

why_en: Time-series databases perform best when tags are low cardinality, samples are regular, and adjacent values have small deltas.

scenario_en: The interviewer asks roughly how much faster a TSDB can be than a general-purpose database after stacking write-path, time-partitioning, compression, and indexing optimizations.
q: 对目标 workload 而言，TSDB 相比通用数据库的性能收益大致是什么量级？
q_en: For the target workload, what order of performance gain can a TSDB have over a general-purpose database?
options: 永远只快 1%，几乎感觉不到差别
永远慢 100x，专用系统反而更差
通常能比通用数据库快一到两个数量级，比如 10-100x
只影响 UI 展示，不影响存储或查询本身
why:
这个收益来自多种设计叠加：append-only、LSM、压缩、时间分区、Bloom filter、rollup 和 block pruning。前提是 workload 符合 TSDB 假设。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
For the right workload, time-series databases can deliver order-of-magnitude improvements such as 10 to 100 times better performance.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 这个维度量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this embedding dimensionality range support?
options: 维度越高，索引内存和查询计算通常也越高，需要按需求取舍
维度数字只是背景八卦，不影响任何架构决策

why:
128-1536（部分模型上千维）不是要背下来，而是提醒你：维度越高，索引占用内存和单次相似度计算量通常也越大。选维度要结合 recall 目标和内存预算一起权衡。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Typical embedding dimensionality of 128 to 1536 matters because higher dimensions usually raise index memory and per-query compute cost.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

The dimension number is just trivia that doesn't affect architecture.
As long as dimensions stay under 1,000,000, memory planning can be ignored.
Dimension choice depends only on the database vendor, not the model.

q: 1M 个 1536 维向量做一次 naive exact KNN，大致为什么很贵？
q_en: Why is naive exact KNN expensive over 1M 1536-dimensional vectors?
options: 需要对 100 万个向量逐个计算高维相似度，浮点运算量达十亿级
只需要比较两个整数主键，几乎零计算
数据库会直接缓存答案，不需要现场计算
维度越高，需要比较的数字反而越少更简单
why:
1M * 1536 维已经是十亿级乘加/距离计算，再加排序或 heap 维护。SIMD/GPU 能优化，但大多数在线应用仍需要 ANN。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Naive exact KNN over a million 1536-dimensional vectors requires billions of floating-point operations per query.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

It only compares two integer primary keys, almost zero computation.
The database already has the answer cached, no live computation needed.
Higher dimensionality means fewer numbers to compare, so it's simpler.

q: 把 HNSW 搜索流程按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the HNSW search flow in order.
steps: 在 Layer 0 做更细的局部搜索，找 K 个候选
从最高的稀疏层和入口点开始
到达当前层局部最接近位置后下降一层
贪心移动到更接近 query vector 的邻居
why: 高层先快速定位大致区域，逐层下降后在底层附近精搜。这个流程解释了 HNSW 为什么能跳过大量向量。
why_en: HNSW starts at a sparse top layer, greedily walks toward the query, descends layers, and does local search at the base layer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Top[Top sparse layer] --> Greedy[Greedy walk toward query]
Greedy --> Down[Drop down a layer]
Down --> Base[Layer 0 local search]
Base --> TopK[Return top K candidates]
tradeoff: 高层快速定位区域 vs 底层局部精搜的准确性

q: HNSW（分层可导航小世界图索引）在生产系统中常被选择的原因是什么？
q_en: Why is HNSW often chosen in production vector search?
options: 它常能以低延迟达到 95%+ recall 级别
它不消耗任何内存
它不需要任何向量输入
它只适合离线 CSV 排序
why:
HNSW 的吸引力是查询性能和 recall 都很好。代价是内存、构建时间和更新复杂度。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
HNSW is popular because it often achieves very high recall, such as 95 percent or more, with low latency.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: IVF / Inverted File Index 的基本思想是什么？
q_en: What is the basic idea behind IVF?
options: 用 k-means 把向量分簇，查询时只搜索最近的几个簇

why_en: IVF clusters vectors around centroids and searches only the closest clusters for a query.
diagram:

    C --> C1["list 1"]
    C --> C2["list 2"]
    C --> C3["list N"]
    Q["Query"] --> NP["probe nearest lists"]
    NP --> C1
    NP --> C2

Put all vectors in a single linked list and scan all of them.
Sort only by vector creation time.
Convert the vector model directly into SQL foreign keys.

# LSH hash bit for cosine similarity
def hash_bit(vector, hyperplane):
    return 1 if dot(vector, hyperplane) > 0 else 0

# 8 random hyperplanes -> 8-bit hash bucket
bucket = "".join(str(hash_bit(v, h)) for h in hyperplanes)

options: filtered vector search，要同时处理相似度和过滤条件

whenOtherWins: 如果查询只是精确查商品 ID，不需要向量库，普通数据库索引更合适。
tradeoff: 相似度排序 vs 结构化过滤条件

Only an exact primary key lookup.

post-filtering 只能用在 SQL 场景，pre-filtering 只能用在图片场景
二者在效果和适用场景上完全一样，没有区别
pre-filtering 永远不需要用到任何索引结构
why: post-filtering 在过滤很严格时可能凑不够 K；pre-filtering 可能无法充分使用 ANN 索引。选择依赖数据分布和过滤选择性。
why_en: Post-filtering searches similar candidates then filters them, while pre-filtering restricts the set before vector search.

    Q["Query + filter"] --> A{"Filter timing"}
    A --> Pre["pre-filter candidates"]
    A --> Post["post-filter results"]
    Pre --> Fast["less vector work"]
    Post --> Recall["risk too few matches"]
tradeoff: 先过滤再搜索 vs 先搜索再过滤
options_en: Post-filtering fetches many similar candidates then filters; pre-filtering restricts the set before vector search.
Post-filtering only works with SQL, pre-filtering only works with images.
The two are completely identical.

q: 更可能适合哪种策略？
q_en: Which filtering strategy is more likely to fit here?
options: pre-filtering，先缩小候选集，brute-force 可能更快
post-filtering，因为它一定能最大程度节省计算量

why_en: Pre-filtering often wins when a restrictive filter reduces the candidate set to a tiny subset.
whenOtherWins: 如果过滤条件不太选择性，或向量库能在 ANN 遍历中高效应用过滤，混合/内置过滤可能更好。
tradeoff: 小候选集直接计算 vs 走全量 ANN 索引
options_en: Pre-filtering, because shrinking to a small set first can make brute-force or light search faster.
Post-filtering, because it always minimizes compute.
Skip filtering entirely.
Return all results in random order.

options: 同时用关键词/全文搜索和向量相似度，再合并结果
同时给两份数据各写一份事务日志
把图片相似搜索改成只查询主键 ID
只依赖缓存层，完全不使用任何索引

flowchart LR

    Q --> V["vector search"]
    L --> M["merge candidates"]
    V --> M
    M --> R["rerank"]
    R --> K["top results"]

q_en: At what vector-count scale should you seriously consider a purpose-built vector database?
options: 超过 100 万个字符

why:
这不是硬规则，但能帮助面试里把“先简单”与“何时升级”说清楚。上亿向量往往意味着内存、分片、过滤和运维压力都更大。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A rough rule is to consider a purpose-built vector database when you are dealing with more than about 100 million vectors.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

scenario: 1536 维 float32 embedding，单个原始向量约占 6KB（1536 × 4 bytes）。
scenario_en: A 1536-dimensional float32 embedding uses about 6 KB of raw storage per vector: 1536 times 4 bytes.
q: 这个单条向量大小最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this single-vector size support?
options: 百万级向量的原始存储很容易到 GB 级，要提前做内存预算
向量大小与内存规划无关，只要磁盘够大就行
6KB 已经大到必须单独分库分表
更换向量模型不会改变内存占用
why:
1536×4 bytes ≈ 6KB 只是起点；乘以百万级数据量会迅速逼近 GB 级，这决定了要不要在设计里显式提内存预算。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A single 1536-dimensional float32 vector is about 6 KB, and at million-vector scale that adds up to gigabytes you must budget for.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
options_en: Raw storage for millions of vectors easily reaches gigabytes, so budget memory ahead of time.
Vector size is irrelevant to memory planning as long as disk is big enough.
6KB is already large enough to require sharding into separate databases.
Changing the embedding model never changes memory usage.

q: 个性化向量推荐里的 cold start 问题是什么？

options: 新用户缺乏行为历史，user embedding 不可靠
新用户的向量维度一定会被强制设为 0

options_en: New users lack behavior history, making it hard to generate a reliable user embedding.

q: 把“是否引入 vector DB”的决策链按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the decision chain for whether to introduce a vector database in order.
steps: 先从 pgvector/Elasticsearch/Redis 等已有系统扩展开始，除非规模或功能要求更高
确认问题是语义相似、推荐、RAG、近重复或异常检测，而不是精确查找
明确 staleness、embedding 生成、过滤策略和 update/rebuild 方案
如果超过约 100M 向量或需要复杂 filtered ANN，再考虑 Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus/Qdrant 等专用系统
选择 ANN 索引时用真实数据评估 recall、latency、memory
why: 先确认 vector search 真能解决问题，再从简单方案开始并量化索引取舍。专用向量库应由规模、过滤或运维需求驱动，而不是默认引入。
why_en: The decision should start with a real similarity problem, choose the simplest viable vector capability, benchmark index tradeoffs, and only then move to dedicated vector infrastructure.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Need["Need similarity search"] --> Size{"small enough?"}
    Size -->|yes| Pg["pgvector or existing store"]
    Size -->|no| VDB["purpose built vector DB"]
    VDB --> Tune["benchmark recall latency cost"]
tradeoff: 先复用现有系统 vs 规模/过滤驱动才上专用向量库

q: 补全三种 ZNode 类型：
q_en: Fill in the three ZNode types.
text: {{Persistent}}（持久）节点：显式删除前一直存在；{{Ephemeral}}（临时）节点：创建它的会话结束（断连或超时）就自动删除；{{Sequential}}（顺序）节点：名字自动追加单调递增计数器。
why: 三种节点是所有 ZK 配方的原料：配置用持久、活性跟踪用临时、排序/锁/选举用顺序（常与临时组合）。
why_en: Persistent nodes live until deleted, ephemeral nodes vanish when their session ends, and sequential nodes get an auto-incrementing counter in their name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久节点：显式删除前会一直存在，不受客户端会话影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A persistent znode stays until explicitly deleted, regardless of client sessions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 临时节点：创建它的客户端会话一结束（断连或超时）就自动被删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral znode is automatically deleted when the client session that created it ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序节点：ZooKeeper 自动在节点名后追加单调递增的计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential znode gets a monotonically increasing counter automatically appended to its name by ZooKeeper.

scenario: 要在 ZK 里存聊天应用的配置：最大消息长度、限速参数——改了才变，不随会话消失。
scenario_en: You need to store chat-app configuration in ZooKeeper, such as max message size and rate limits. It changes only when edited and must not disappear with a client session.
q: 该用哪种 ZNode？
q_en: Which ZNode type should you use?
options: Ephemeral（临时）节点——但它会随客户端会话结束而消失
Sequential ephemeral（顺序临时）节点——既顺序编号又跟会话绑定
不用 ZNode，把配置塞进外部消息队列里发布
Persistent（持久）节点——不随会话变化，显式删除前一直存在
options_en: Ephemeral — but it disappears the moment the client session ends.
Sequential ephemeral — numbered in order and still tied to a session.
Skip znodes entirely and push the config through an external message queue.
Persistent — stays until explicitly deleted, unaffected by session changes.
why: 配置数据要求「直到显式删除/修改前一直存在」，持久节点正合适；临时节点会随会话断开而消失。
why_en: Configuration like max message size belongs in persistent nodes that survive until explicitly changed.
whenOtherWins: 跟踪「谁活着」（服务器/用户在线状态）时要用临时节点，让崩溃自动清理。
tradeoff: 持久节点「一直存在」的可靠配置 vs 临时节点「随会话消失」的活性跟踪

# 存最大消息长度等配置（默认就是 Persistent）
create /chat-app/config/max_message_size "1024"
create /chat-app/config/rate_limit "100/sec"
# 不带 -e / -s 标志

q: 更可扩展的做法是？
q_en: What is the more scalable routing design?
options: 照原计划做，ZooKeeper 的写入能力足够扛住百万级节点
只让服务器注册进 ZK，用户按 ID 用一致性哈希映射到服务器，ZK 只跟踪服务器

Register only servers in ZooKeeper and map users to servers by consistent hashing on user ID.
Stuff the entire list of online users into one big znode.
Create five znodes per user for redundancy.
why: ZK 管协调元数据不管海量条目：跟踪几十台服务器（临时节点，故障秒级发现）+ 哈希函数定位用户，量级立刻可控。
why_en: Register only servers in ZooKeeper and map millions of users to servers with consistent hashing, keeping fast failure detection without per-user znodes.
whenOtherWins: 用户量小（几千）时按用户建节点也行，简单直接。

scenario: 聊天平台要求即便同时有服务器故障，路由用的 ZooKeeper ensemble 依然能继续处理读写；团队把 ensemble 定为 5 台。
scenario_en: The chat platform needs its ZooKeeper ensemble to keep serving routing reads and writes even when some servers fail. The team chooses a 5-node ensemble.
q: 5 台服务器的 ZooKeeper ensemble 最多能容忍几台故障仍正常工作？
q_en: In a 5-node ZooKeeper ensemble, how many node failures can it tolerate?
options: 1 台，因为多一台都会丢失多数派
2 台，因为剩下的 3 台仍是多数派（quorum）
3 台，只要还剩 2 台在线就能工作
4 台，只要还有 1 台在线就能工作
options_en: One, because losing a second server would break the majority.
Two, because the remaining three servers still form a quorum majority.
Three, as long as two servers stay online.
Four, as long as one server stays online.
why:
容忍故障数 = ⌈N/2⌉-1；5 台的多数派门槛是 3 台，所以最多能失去 2 台。这个门槛也是选 3/5/7 奇数 ensemble 的原因。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A five-server ensemble tolerates two failures because three remaining servers still form a majority, or quorum.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum（多数派）：ensemble 里过半数服务器，是继续接受写请求的最低存活门槛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the majority of ensemble servers that must stay alive for the cluster to keep accepting writes.

q: 客户端连接 ZooKeeper 时的连接串长什么样？为什么？
q_en: What does a ZooKeeper client connection string look like, and why?
options: 只填当前 leader 那一台服务器的地址，其余 follower 地址客户端完全不需要知道
填一个统一的负载均衡器地址，把连哪台 ZooKeeper 的决定权完全交给负载均衡器
填整个 ensemble 的地址列表（如 zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181）+ 会话超时 + watcher 回调
只填一个 DNS 泛域名地址，具体解析到哪台机器完全交给 DNS 服务去决定
options_en: Only the current leader's address; client does not need to know the followers at all.
A unified load balancer address, leaving which ZooKeeper server to route to entirely up to it.
The full ensemble address list plus a session timeout and a watcher callback.
Just a wildcard DNS name, leaving which machine gets resolved entirely up to DNS.
why: 客户端知道全部节点，某台挂了可以换一台重连并恢复会话；构造参数里还有会话超时和 watch 回调。
why_en: Clients connect with the full ensemble address list plus a session timeout and watcher callback, so any live server can serve them.
codeSample:
// Chat Server 1 连接 ZooKeeper
ZooKeeper zk = new ZooKeeper(
  "zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181", // 全部 ensemble 地址
  3000,     // 会话超时（毫秒）
  watcher); // 变更通知回调

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：客户端连接串里列出的一组 ZooKeeper 服务器地址，任一台存活即可接入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ensemble is the set of ZooKeeper server addresses in the connection string; any live one can serve the client.

q: 正确的做法是？

每隔 100ms 就用一个本地轮询定时器主动查询一次 /chat-app/users 整个目录

Have every server continuously exchange heartbeat probes with each other, piggybacking user location on them.

scenario: 要给整个聊天平台上线一个新功能开关，希望所有服务器实时生效、不用重启。
scenario_en: You need to launch a new feature flag across the chat platform, and every server should see it in real time without a restart.
q: 用 ZooKeeper 怎么做？
q_en: How would you implement this with ZooKeeper?
options: SSH 逐台登录到每一台服务器机器，手动修改本地配置文件后再滚动重启服务进程
更新一个 ZNode（如 enable_reactions 设为 true），watch 该节点的服务器收到通知后即时改变行为
给运维和研发团队群发一封全员邮件，逐个通知大家自行手动修改本地配置
把开关值直接硬编码进代码常量里面，走一次完整的重新打包和发布上线流程
options_en: SSH into every single server machine, manually edit the local config file, then roll a restart process by process.
Update one znode (say, enable_reactions to true) and every watching server reacts instantly.
Send an all-hands email to ops and engineering, telling everyone to manually change their local config one by one.
Hard-code the flag as a constant right in the code and go through a full rebuild-and-redeploy cycle.
why: 集中配置 + watch 通知 = 实时传播、版本化、原子更新；这是 ZK 配置管理的招牌场景。
why_en: Update one znode and every watching server gets notified and changes behavior without restarting.
whenOtherWins: 只在部署时才变的静态配置放文件或环境变量更合适；云上可用 AWS Parameter Store / Azure App Configuration 等托管方案。
tradeoff: 集中 ZNode + watch 推送（秒级生效、免重启）vs 改文件重启（简单但要停机滚动）
codeSample:
# 更新配置节点

steps: 序号最小的服务器成为 leader
每台服务器在指定路径下创建顺序+临时节点
leader 故障 → 它的节点消失，下一个序号的服务器收到通知接任

why_en: Each server creates a sequential ephemeral node, the lowest number leads, everyone watches the next lower node, and when the leader dies the next in line takes over.
diagram:
flowchart LR

    B -.被 watch.- C["node-0003"]

Git also uses it to decide which branch's commit history should be kept as priority during a merge.

scenario_en: Multiple payment workers want to process the same payment, but only one worker may enter the critical section at a time. Workers can crash, so the lock must release automatically.
q: ZooKeeper 分布式锁的配方是？
q_en: What is the ZooKeeper distributed-lock recipe?
options: 所有客户端抢写同一个固定节点，成功者持锁
每个客户端建临时顺序节点，最小号持锁
由 ensemble leader 手动挑一个客户端发锁
按客户端本地时间戳排序，最早者持锁
options_en: All clients race to write the same fixed node; whoever succeeds holds the lock.
Each client creates an ephemeral sequential node; the lowest number holds the lock.
The ensemble leader manually chooses one client and grants the lock.
Sort by each client's local timestamp; the earliest one holds the lock.
why: 把锁想成排队拿号：每个客户端拿一个会自动递增、会话结束会消失的节点号。号最小的人持锁；其他人只 watch 自己前一个号，前一个消失后再检查是否轮到自己。
why_en: Think of the lock as taking a queue ticket: each client creates an ephemeral sequential node, the lowest ticket holds the lock, and everyone else watches only the previous ticket.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是同一进程内互斥，用本地 mutex；如果是高频短锁，Redis 或数据库条件写通常更轻。
tradeoff: 公平排队+崩溃自动释放 vs 每次加解锁都走 ZooKeeper 写路径

q: ZooKeeper 锁不适合什么场景？该用什么替代？
q_en: When is a ZooKeeper lock a poor fit, and what should replace it?
options: 只要持锁时间超过几分钟，就应该换成本地内存锁替代
任何生产场景都不该用 ZooKeeper 锁，风险太高

跨机房场景不适合，应该改成每个机房各自独立加锁

ZooKeeper locks should never be used in any production scenario at all.

why: 每次加解锁都是走共识的写操作，高频场景撑不住；高频轻量锁交给 Redis 或数据库。
why_en: ZooKeeper locks are not built for hundreds of acquisitions per second, where Redis locks or database transactions fit better.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock is a lightweight distributed lock built with commands like SETNX and TTL, offering high throughput but relying on timeout management.

q: 选 ZooKeeper 锁还是 Redis 锁？

Redis locks — higher throughput and lower latency, which looks like a fit for this long-hold scenario.

q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的一致性保证：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's consistency guarantees.
text: 五大保证：{{顺序一致性}}（同一客户端的更新按发送顺序生效）、{{原子性}}（更新要么全成要么全败）、{{单一系统映像}}（连哪台服务器看到的视图一致）、{{持久性}}（确认过的更新不会丢）、及时性（客户端视图在有界时间内更新）。
why: 这五条是 ZK 可以被信任为「协调真相源」的原因；实现上全靠写走 leader 的全序 + quorum 持久化。
why_en: ZooKeeper guarantees sequential consistency, atomicity, a single system image, durability, and timeliness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序一致性：同一客户端发出的多个更新，所有服务器都按发送顺序应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential consistency means updates from one client are applied by every server in the order that client sent them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一系统映像：无论客户端连到 ensemble 里哪台服务器，同步后看到的数据视图都一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single system image means a client sees the same data view regardless of which ensemble server it connects to, once synced.

q: 从 follower 读数据可能读到旧值。需要最强一致的读时怎么办？
q_en: Follower reads can be stale. What should you do when you need the strongest read consistency?
options: 把所有读请求都强制改发给 leader 一台机器处理
读前先调用 sync 操作，确保该服务器已与 leader 同步再读
同一份数据读三次，取出现次数最多的那个结果
这个问题无解，只能接受可能读到旧数据
options_en: Force every read request to go only to the leader.
Call sync before reading, ensuring the server has caught up with the leader first.
Read the same value three times and take the majority result.
There is no fix — you just accept that reads may be stale.
why: follower 平时不为每次读询问 leader，所以可能滞后；sync 强制先追平再读，换来最新数据。

q: 网络分区导致任何一组服务器都凑不齐多数派时，ZooKeeper 会怎样？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper do when no network partition can form a majority?
options: 分区两边的服务器各自继续独立处理写请求，等分区恢复后再合并数据
自动在云上现拉起几台新的服务器节点来补足所需的多数派
由系统随机挑其中一边的服务器组，继续处理这一边的写请求
停止处理写请求直到分区恢复——宁可不可用也要避免 split-brain（脑裂）
options_en: Both sides of the partition keep processing writes independently and merge the data after it heals.
It automatically spins up a few new servers in the cloud to restore a majority.
The system randomly picks one side of the partition to keep processing its writes.
It stops processing writes until the partition heals, choosing unavailability over split-brain.
why:
没有多数派就不写，防止系统两半各持一套「真相」；这是 CP 系统的典型选择。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Without a majority ZooKeeper refuses writes until the partition heals, preventing split-brain disagreement.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: split-brain（脑裂）：网络分区后系统两半各自独立接受写入，产生两份互相矛盾的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Split-brain is when a network partition lets both halves of a system independently accept writes, producing two conflicting copies of the data.

q: 把「聊天服务器崩溃后 ZooKeeper 的自动处理」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put ZooKeeper's automatic handling of a crashed chat server in the right order.
steps: 其它 watch 这些节点的服务器收到通知，更新路由表、把用户标记下线
Server 2 崩溃
它创建的所有临时节点被自动删除（服务器注册节点 + 名下用户节点）
Server 2 的 ZK 会话超时（典型 10-30 秒后）
why: 崩溃 → 会话超时 → 临时节点消失 → watcher 收通知并响应。全程无需人工干预——这是 ZK 最强大的特性之一。
why_en: After a crash the session times out, its ephemeral nodes are deleted, and watching servers get notified and update their routing automatically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Server 2 崩溃"] --> T["会话超时"]
    T --> D["临时节点自动删除"]
    D --> N["watcher 收到通知\n更新路由/标记下线"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话超时：客户端超过约定时间没有发送心跳，ZooKeeper 判定其会话失效并清理其临时节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session timeout is when a client misses heartbeats for the agreed window, so ZooKeeper marks its session expired and cleans up its ephemeral nodes.

q: ZooKeeper 的主要局限有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are ZooKeeper's main limitations? (Select all that apply.)
options: 写昂贵：必须经 leader 传播到多数派
内存存储模型限制容量：ZNode 要 <1MB、数据集须装进内存
运维复杂：JVM 参数、磁盘布局、超时与连接监控——「用起来简单，运维起来复杂」
不支持 watch 通知，只能靠轮询感知变化
options_en: Writes are expensive: they must propagate through the leader to a majority.
Capacity is memory-bound: znodes must stay under one megabyte and the dataset must fit in memory.

scenario: 设计 Facebook Live Comments / YouTube Live Chat：百万观众看同一直播，希望同一直播间的 websocket 连接尽量集中到同一台（组）服务器以减少跨服务器通信。
scenario_en: You are designing Facebook Live Comments or YouTube Live Chat. Millions of viewers watch the same stream, and you want connections for one room concentrated on the same server group to reduce cross-server traffic.
q: ZooKeeper 在这里扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role does ZooKeeper play in this live-chat routing design?
options: 让 ZooKeeper 直接充当消息队列，转发全部实时评论的消息本体内容
把每一条历史评论的完整内容都存进 ZooKeeper 里，方便日后回放
作为 API 网关的协调点：维护「哪个房间/直播由哪台服务器负责」的映射；服务器带容量注册，新连接按房间查 ZK 定向
给每一条实时评论单独加一把分布式锁，用来防止重复展示
options_en: Have ZooKeeper act directly as the message queue forwarding every live comment's payload content.
Store the full content of every historical comment inside ZooKeeper for later replay.
Act as the API gateway's coordination point, mapping which server handles which room, with capacity-aware registration and routing.
Put an individual distributed lock on each live comment to prevent it from being shown twice.
why: 这是「智能路由/同房间同服务器（colocation）」的高级用法——Staff+ 或深度分布式面试的加分项。
why_en: ZooKeeper coordinates smart routing by mapping rooms to servers so a gateway can colocate all viewers of a stream on the same server group.
whenOtherWins: 普通规模的聊天用 pub/sub 广播就能绕开大部分协调问题，不必上这套。
tradeoff: ZK 做房间→服务器的协调映射（轻量、可扩展）vs 把评论本体也塞进 ZK（违反小数据原则、写爆）

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Colocation routing means directing all connections for the same room or stream to the same server or server group, minimizing cross-server chatter.

q: 设计「分布式消息队列」时，ZooKeeper 可以作为共识大脑承担哪些职责？（多选）
q_en: In a distributed message queue, which responsibilities can ZooKeeper handle as the consensus brain? (Select all that apply.)
options: broker 注册与发现、topic 元数据（分区数、副本因子）存储
每个分区的 leader 选举（顺序临时节点保证单一 leader）
consumer group 成员关系与分区分配，broker 故障经临时节点触发分区重分配
存储全部消息本体，让 broker 直接从 ZK 读写消息内容
options_en: Broker registration and discovery, plus topic metadata like partition count and replication factor.
Per-partition leader election, using sequential ephemeral nodes to guarantee a single leader.
Consumer group membership and partition assignment, with broker failure triggering reassignment via ephemeral nodes.
Storing the full message payloads so brokers read and write message content directly from ZooKeeper.
why: KRaft 之前的 Kafka 正是这么用 ZK 的；HBase、Hadoop、Solr 也是类似模式。消息本体走 broker 自己的日志存储，绝不放 ZK。
why_en: In a distributed queue design ZooKeeper handles broker registration, topic metadata, partition leader election, consumer membership, and failure detection, never the message payloads.
tradeoff: ZK 管协调元数据（小、强一致）vs broker 自管消息日志（大、高吞吐）——两者不能互换

scenario: 分布式文件系统需要「目录及其文件」的嵌套锁获取，要防死锁，还要能监控整个锁层级的变化。
scenario_en: A distributed file system needs nested locks for directories and files. It must avoid deadlocks and watch changes across the whole lock hierarchy.
q: 为什么这里 ZooKeeper 严格优于 Redis？
q_en: Why is ZooKeeper strictly better than Redis in this case?
options: 因为部署 ZooKeeper 集群的机器成本比部署 Redis 更加便宜
ZK 的层级命名空间天然表达父子锁结构，能同时 watch 多个节点监控整个锁层级；Redis 缺少层级与联动通知
因为 Redis 这个产品根本就没有实现过分布式锁的能力
因为 ZooKeeper 锁的整体写入吞吐量比 Redis 锁要高得多
options_en: Because running a ZooKeeper cluster costs less hardware than running Redis.
ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace naturally expresses parent-child lock structure and can watch multiple nodes across the whole hierarchy; Redis lacks that hierarchy and linked notification.
Because Redis as a product has never implemented any distributed-lock capability.
Because ZooKeeper locks have much higher overall write throughput than Redis locks.
why: 资源有父子关系、锁获取要尊重层级时，ZK 的树形结构 + 多点 watch 是量身定制；Redis 锁是平面的。
why_en: ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace and multi-node watches express nested directory-file locks with deadlock prevention, which flat Redis locks cannot.
whenOtherWins: 普通的单资源短锁（订单、座位）Redis 又快又简单，是默认选择。
tradeoff: ZooKeeper 的层级命名空间+多点 watch（表达父子锁结构）vs Redis 的平面 key 空间（无天然层级）

1MB, matching the guideline: znodes hold only small coordination data and the dataset must fit in memory.
1GB, treating a znode like file storage, which defeats ZooKeeper's whole design premise.
why:
ZNode 定位是小协调数据：保持在 1MB 以下，整个数据集要能装进内存；超过这个量级就该把大对象放对象存储/DB，ZNode 只存一个引用指针。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Keep each znode under one megabyte and ensure the whole dataset fits in memory; anything bigger belongs in object storage with just a reference stored in the znode.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。

A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的三大基础原语：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's three basic primitives.
text: ZooKeeper 靠三个简单原语组合出所有协调能力：{{ZNode}}（层级命名空间中的数据节点）、可靠的服务器 {{ensemble}}（多数派容错）、{{watch}}（变更实时通知）。
why: 数据模型 + 可靠集群 + 通知机制——三件套组合出配置管理、服务发现、选举与锁的全部配方。
why_en: ZooKeeper combines znodes in a hierarchical namespace, a reliable server ensemble, and watches for change notification.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZNode：层级命名空间里的一个数据节点，能存少量数据、能有子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A znode is a node in the hierarchical namespace that can hold a small amount of data and have children.

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：一组协同工作、以多数派（quorum）容错的 ZooKeeper 服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble is the group of ZooKeeper servers working together with majority-based fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: watch：客户端登记在 ZNode 上的一次性变更通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watch is a one-time change notification a client registers on a znode.

q: 纽约到伦敦的请求，仅光纤中的光速就决定了最低延迟约是？
q_en: For a New York to London request, what latency floor does fiber propagation alone create?
options: ~1ms
RTT 约 70-90ms
options_en: About one millisecond.
A practical round trip of about seventy to ninety milliseconds, with a pure physical floor around sixty.
About two seconds.
About one hundredth of a millisecond.
why:
纽约到伦敦纯物理 RTT 下限约 55-60ms，实践中常在 70-90ms；还没开始处理就有这个级别的跨洋成本，所以全球低延迟必须区域化部署、按地理复制或分区数据。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A New York to London round trip has a physical lower bound around 55-60ms and practical network latency often around 70-90ms, which is why regional deployments and CDNs exist.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

options: 把 API 下线
提到限流，点到为止
换一种编程语言
禁止所有匿名访问
options_en: Take the API offline.
Mention rate limiting, but don't go deep unless the interviewer asks.
Switch to a different programming language.
Block all anonymous access.
optionMeanings: 回避问题
点到为止
无关的手段
过度设防
optionDirectness: 只有无法服务或关停产品时才下线；它不是常规架构答案。
接口可能被刷时，提限流能说明你想到了滥用和保护下游。
换语言不改变请求量、配额或滥用风险。
匿名读路径可以保留；用限流比全量登录更精细。
optionDirectness_en: Taking the API down only fits shutdown or inability to serve; it is not normal architecture.
Mentioning rate limits shows you considered abuse and downstream protection.
Changing languages does not change request volume, quotas, or abuse risk.
Anonymous reads can remain; rate limits are more precise than forcing login everywhere.
why: 可能被滥用的系统值得提一句限流；分页/认证/限流这些点都是「提到即可」，深挖等考官发起。
why_en: If the system could get hammered by bots or abuse, mention rate limiting but do not go deep unless asked.
whenOtherWins: 纯内部、流量完全可信的系统就不必主动展开限流，把时间留给核心架构。

scenario: 数据是结构化的、关系清晰（用户账户→订单→商品），需要强一致、事务和复杂查询。
scenario_en: The data is structured with clear relationships, such as users to orders to products, and needs transactions and strong consistency.
q: 最合适的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits structured relational data with transactions?
options: MongoDB
DynamoDB
关系型数据库（如 Postgres）
S3 对象存储
options_en: MongoDB.
DynamoDB.
A relational database like Postgres, with complex SQL queries, transactions, and foreign key constraints.
S3 object storage.
optionMeanings: 文档型 NoSQL
键值/宽列 NoSQL
关系型数据库
对象存储
optionDirectness: 文档库适合半结构化文档，不适合强 join 和事务主路径。
键值/宽列适合按 key 访问，不适合复杂关系查询。
关系型数据库适合结构清楚、关系多、事务要求强的路径。
对象存储适合大文件，不适合订单关系查询。
optionDirectness_en: Document stores fit semi-structured documents, not heavy joins and transaction-heavy paths.
Key-value or wide-column stores fit key access, not complex relational queries.
Relational databases fit clear structure, many relationships, and strong transaction needs.
Object storage fits large files, not order relationship queries.
why: 结构化 + 清晰关系 + 强一致，正是关系型的主场：SQL 表达复杂查询、事务保一致、外键约束护关系。
why_en: Relational databases like Postgres excel with structured data, clear relationships, strong consistency, transactions, and complex SQL queries.
whenOtherWins: schema 频繁变化、或需要不依赖复杂 join 的水平扩展时，NoSQL（DynamoDB/MongoDB）更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，用来存文件/二进制大对象，不是给结构化查询用的。

scenario_en: The data shape changes often, must scale horizontally across machines, and does not rely on complex joins.

q_en: Which storage choice fits flexible schema and horizontal scaling without complex joins?
options: NoSQL（DynamoDB / MongoDB）
单机 Postgres，不做任何扩展准备
强一致的分布式 SQL（如 Spanner），join 成本依旧高
关系型 + 只读副本，schema 变化仍要迁移脚本
options_en: NoSQL, such as DynamoDB or MongoDB.
A single Postgres instance with no scaling plan.
A strongly consistent distributed SQL database like Spanner, where joins still cost the same.
Relational plus read replicas, still needing migration scripts for schema changes.
optionMeanings: 灵活 schema+水平扩展
单机无扩展
分布式但仍强关系
关系型+副本
optionDirectness: 文档型或宽列 NoSQL 适合 schema 变化快、按访问模式横向扩展的系统。

分布式 SQL 适合强关系和事务，不是为了弱化 schema。
读副本扩读不扩写，也不消除 schema 迁移成本。
optionDirectness_en: Document or wide-column NoSQL fits fast schema changes and access-pattern-based horizontal scaling.
A single JSON file fits prototypes, not concurrency or scaling.
Distributed SQL fits strong relationships and transactions, not avoiding schema design.
Read replicas scale reads, not writes, and do not remove schema migration cost.

q: 「规范化（normalization）」的含义与代价是？
q_en: What does normalization mean, and what does it cost?
options: 把所有数据塞进一张宽表，不做任何拆分
拆表避免重复，读取需要 join
给每个字段单独建一张表来省空间
把重复字段做压缩存储，但仍然保留每处的拷贝
options_en: Put all data into one wide table with no splitting.

Split data across tables to avoid duplication, so orders reference a user ID instead of copying user data: updating once updates everywhere, but reading full data needs joins, which get expensive at scale.
Give every single field its own table to save space.
Compress duplicate fields but still keep a copy in every place.
optionMeanings: 反规范化的极端
标准规范化定义
过度拆分的误解
压缩≠规范化
optionDirectness: 把所有字段塞一行会让重复数据和更新不一致变严重。
实体拆表并用引用连接时，更新更一致，但读取常要 join。
每个字段单独成表会过度拆分，查询成本很高。
压缩节省字节，不解决实体关系和重复事实。
optionDirectness_en: Putting every field in one row worsens duplication and inconsistent updates.
Splitting entities into referenced tables improves update consistency but often requires joins.
One table per field is over-splitting and makes queries expensive.
Compression saves bytes; it does not solve entity relationships or duplicate facts.
why: 规范化保一致性（改一次商品名全站生效），代价是读取要 join；表巨大或跨多表 join 时开销显著。
why_en: Normalization splits data across tables to avoid duplication, keeping it consistent but requiring joins that get expensive at scale.

q: 反规范化（denormalization）与规范化在「读写」上的取舍是？

options: 反规范化读写都更慢
规范化读更快
两者读写性能一样
反规范化免 join，读更快写更贵
options_en: Denormalization makes both reads and writes slower.
Normalization makes reads faster.
The two have identical read/write performance.

无差异的错误认知

optionDirectness: 反规范化通常是为了少 join、读更快，不是读写都变慢。
如果数据经常变，反规范化的多处更新成本会很痛。
两者都能存数据，但读路径和更新一致性成本不同。
读多且冗余字段少变时，反规范化用写复杂度换读速度。
optionDirectness_en: Denormalization usually reduces joins for faster reads; it is not meant to make both paths slower.

Both can store the data, but their read path and update-consistency costs differ.
For read-heavy data with rarely changing copies, denormalization trades write complexity for read speed.

q: 把高频读路径迁到缓存命中之后，对数据库扩容的时间点意味着什么？
q_en: After moving a hot read path behind cache hits, what changes about the database scale-up point?
options: 读负载从数据库卸下，扩容时点推迟
缓存命中之后数据库延迟反而变高
缓存和数据库延迟其实一样，迁移没有意义
只影响写请求，读请求延迟不变
options_en: Cache hits bypass the database entirely, offloading that read traffic and pushing back when you need to shard or scale.
Database latency actually goes up once caching is added.
Cache and database latency are actually the same, so the migration is pointless.
It only affects write requests; read latency is unchanged.
why:
缓存命中约 1ms、未命中查库约 20-50ms，是 20-50 倍的差距；命中路径完全跳过数据库，相当于把这部分读流量从数据库卸载，推迟了触发分片/扩容的时间点，这个数字后续直接喂进容量规划。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A cache hit near one millisecond versus twenty to fifty for a database query fully offloads that read traffic, pushing back when you need to shard or scale.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 防止 cache stampede 的手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which techniques prevent a cache stampede? Select all that apply.
options: 加锁：只让一个请求重建条目，其余等待结果
提前重算：条目过期前主动刷新
错开 TTL：避免大量条目同时过期
把 TTL 全部设为 0
options_en: Locking: let only one request rebuild the entry while the rest wait.
Early recomputation: refresh the entry before it expires.
Staggered TTLs: avoid a mass of entries expiring at once.
Set every TTL to zero.
optionScenarioImpacts: 挡住重建请求同时涌向数据库

why: 锁（single flight）、提前刷新、错峰过期是三板斧；TTL 设 0 等于每次都打库，恰恰制造问题。
why_en: Prevent stampedes with locking so one request regenerates, early recomputation before expiry, and staggered TTLs.

q: 什么信号说明你可能真的需要分片？（多选）
q_en: Which signals mean you may actually need sharding? Select all that apply.
options: 存储逼近单实例上限（单个 Postgres 到 TB 量级封顶）
写吞吐到顶（数万写/秒）
读吞吐连读副本都扛不住
用户数刚过一万
options_en: Storage nears a single instance's limit, like a Postgres instance capping out in the terabytes.
Write throughput hits its ceiling, tens of thousands of writes per second.
Read throughput that even read replicas cannot handle.
The user count just crossed ten thousand.
optionScenarioImpacts: 提示要按存储上限规划分片，不是凭感觉
单库写路径成为瓶颈，是最常见的真实触发点
说明加读副本这条路已经走到头，该水平切分了
用户数不是负载指标，跟数据库扛不扛得住无关
why:
分片的三个触发条件：存储、写吞吐、副本也救不了的读吞吐；用户数本身不是理由，要看负载数字。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Shard when you hit storage limits, write throughput limits, or read throughput that even replicas cannot handle.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 分片时最重要的决策是什么？以 Instagram 为例说明取舍。

options: 选数据库品牌
选机房位置
选 shard key
选分片数量
options_en: Choosing the database vendor.
Choosing the data center location.

Choosing the shard key: sharding by user id keeps a user's data on one shard so user-scoped queries are fast, but global queries like trending posts must hit every shard and aggregate, which gets expensive.
Choosing the number of shards.
why:
shard key 决定数据怎么分布、什么查询快什么查询贵，牵动整个设计——这是分片的第一决策。

why_en:
The shard key is the most important decision: sharding Instagram by user id makes user-scoped queries fast but global queries expensive.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 分片引入的新问题有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What new problems does sharding introduce? Select all that apply.
options: 跨分片事务几乎不可能——需要分布式事务或 saga，复杂且慢
热点分片：某个分片流量畸高（Taylor Swift 所在的分片被打爆，其他闲着）
resharding 痛苦：加分片要搬移海量数据
分片后不再需要考虑数据一致性问题
options_en: Cross-shard transactions become nearly impossible, needing distributed transactions or sagas, which are complex and slow.
Hot shards: one shard's traffic spikes far above the rest, like the shard holding Taylor Swift's data getting hammered while others sit idle.
Resharding is painful: adding a shard means moving massive amounts of data.
Sharding means you no longer need to think about data consistency.
optionScenarioImpacts: 跨分片边界的写操作会显著变慢、变复杂，甚至无法原子提交
单个分片被打爆时，扩容其他分片没有用，压力集中在一处
改分片数量意味着一次昂贵的数据重分布，不能说改就改
分片不解决一致性问题，反而让跨片一致性更难保证
why:
分片换来扩展性，同时带来跨片事务、热点、再分片三大痛；设计分片边界时要主动规避跨片操作。

why_en:
Sharding makes cross-shard transactions nearly impossible, creates hot spots, and makes resharding a painful mass data migration.

A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

why:
这组数字就是一致性哈希的价值：动态增删节点不再引发海量数据迁移，这个比例直接决定了扩缩容操作是否安全、可以随时做。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Adding one server to ten means moving about ninety percent of data with modulo hashing but only about ten percent with consistent hashing.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 消息队列的关键量级是？
q_en: What message-queue scale anchors should you remember?
options: 每 broker 每秒 100 条
每秒 1 万条是极限
端到端延迟至少 1 秒
单 broker ~100万条/秒
options_en: One hundred messages per second per broker.
Ten thousand per second is the ceiling.
At least one second of end-to-end latency.

A single broker can reach about a million messages per second with sub-five-millisecond end-to-end latency and storage up to 50TB; scale when nearing eight hundred thousand per second or consumer lag keeps growing.
why:
消息队列吞吐远比直觉高；真正要盯的是接近吞吐上限、分区数（~20 万/集群）和不断增长的 consumer lag。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
A message queue broker handles up to a million messages per second with sub-five-millisecond latency, with growing consumer lag as a key scale trigger.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 补全 Twitter 的非功能需求示例：
text: 系统应高可用，{{可用性}}优先于{{一致性}}；应能扩展到支撑 {{100M}}+ 日活用户；feed 渲染延迟应低于 {{200ms}}。
why:
这三条示范了 NFR 的正确写法：点名 CAP 取舍、给出规模数字、给出量化延迟目标——每条都能在深挖环节被验收。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Twitter's example requirements prioritize availability over consistency, scale past one hundred million daily active users, and render feeds in under two hundred milliseconds.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

scenario: 面试开场刚定完需求，很多备考指南建议此时先做一轮 back-of-the-envelope 容量估算（存储、DAU、QPS）。
q: 本框架推荐的做法是？
options: 必须先算完存储、DAU、QPS 再动手设计
向面试官说明：跳过开场估算，需要时再算
让面试官替你把数字算出来
整场面试完全不做任何计算
options_en: Finish estimating storage, DAU, and QPS before doing anything else.
Tell the interviewer you'll skip upfront estimation and do the math only when needed.
Ask the interviewer to do the numbers for you.
Do no calculations at all during the whole interview.
why:
开场估算常是无用功——大型分布式系统直接假设即可；只有当数字会改变设计决策时才当场做数学。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Tell the interviewer you will skip upfront estimation and do the math during the design only when it directly influences a decision.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
whenOtherWins: 当结果直接决定架构时必须算：比如 TopK 热门话题要估话题总数，才能决定 min-heap 用单实例还是要分片。
tradeoff: 开场就估算『看似严谨但常无信号』 vs 按需估算『省时间，只在改变设计时才算』

scenario: 你在设计一个 TopK 热门话题系统：需要在内存里维护『当前最热的 K 个话题』。
q: 什么时候当场估算才是「必要」的？

options_en: When the topic count decides whether to shard.
At the very start of every interview, no matter the system.
Only as a closing summary at the end.
Whenever the interviewer happens to be in a good mood.
why:
TopK 例子：话题总数决定单个数据结构实例是否装得下，直接改变架构——这类计算才值得当场做。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Estimation matters when it changes the design, like estimating topic counts in a top-k system to decide between a single min-heap and a sharded one.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在候选集合里持续维护排名前 K 的元素的问题模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the problem of continuously tracking the highest-ranked K elements in a set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 堆顶始终是最小值的二叉堆，常用来维护当前的 K 个最大候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A min-heap is a binary heap whose root is always the smallest element, often used to track the current top-K candidates.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试开始时明确的功能性和非功能性需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements are the functional and non-functional constraints you clarify at the start.

q: 先读 Core Concepts / Key Technologies / Patterns 的收益是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of reading Core Concepts, Key Technologies, and Patterns first? (Select all that apply.)
options: 知道系统设计题常见组件和模式的边界
做题时能复用已有概念，而不是每题从零发明
帮助建立学习范围
保证不用再练任何题
options_en: You learn the boundaries of common components and patterns.
You can reuse existing concepts instead of reinventing them each time.
It helps you scope what you need to study.
It guarantees you never have to practice a question.
why: 基础材料不是替代练题，而是给练题提供词汇和取舍框架；没有基础，题解容易变成死记硬背。
why_en: The foundations give you reusable vocabulary and a tradeoff framework, but they do not replace active practice.
optionMeanings: 了解常见组件/模式各自适用的边界。
把学过的概念当工具直接复用。
明确该学到多深、多广。
假设读完基础就不用再练题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 遇到新题能快速判断该用哪类组件。
省去每题重新发明轮子的时间。
避免漫无目的地乱看资料。
会让你误以为可以跳过输出训练。
optionDirectness: 用来知道组件和模式什么时候适用。
用来把已有概念带进新题，减少从零发明。
用来控制学习范围，避免无目的乱看。
只在不考输出时成立；系统设计仍要练题。
optionMeanings_en: You learn where each common component or pattern applies.
You reuse concepts you've already learned as tools.
It clarifies how deep and how broad to study.
It assumes finishing the foundations means skipping practice.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You can quickly judge which component fits a new problem.
It saves you from reinventing the wheel on every question.
It keeps you from wandering aimlessly through material.
It falsely suggests you can skip output training.
optionDirectness_en: Use this to know when components and patterns apply.
Use this to bring known concepts into new problems.
Use this to scope study instead of wandering through material.
Only works if output is not tested; system design still requires practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

scenario: 你已经练过几道题，准备进入 mock 阶段，想让反馈更贴近目标面试。
scenario_en: You have practiced several questions and are ready for mocks, but you want feedback that matches your target interview.
q: peer mock 对象怎么选更好？
q_en: Who is the better person to choose for a peer mock?
options: 只找完全不了解 system design 的人
优先找目标公司或相近风格的工程师
只对着镜子读答案
只用随机题目生成器，不要反馈
options_en: Find someone with no system design background at all.
Prioritize an engineer from the target company or a similar interview style.
Just read the answer out loud to a mirror.
Use a random question generator with no feedback.
why: 目标公司员工更熟悉该公司的面试节奏和评价偏好；反馈越贴近目标环境，练习价值越高。
why_en: A peer from the target company is more likely to give feedback aligned with that company's interview style.
whenOtherWins: 找不到目标公司的人时，找有系统设计面试经验的工程师，重点是拿到真实追问。
tradeoff: 贴近目标公司的真实反馈 vs 容易约到的泛泛反馈
optionMeanings: 找完全没有相关背景的人陪练。
找了解目标评分标准的人给反馈。
自己对自己复述，没有外部反馈。
只刷题，主动放弃反馈环节。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方提不出有价值的技术追问。
追问方式和评分口味更接近真实面试官。
没有人能指出你漏掉的需求或取舍。
没有反馈就发现不了自己的盲点。
optionDirectness: 适合练普通表达；技术追问和评分反馈会很弱。
适合目标公司冲刺；反馈更接近真实面试口味。
适合自我朗读热身；缺少外部追问和纠偏。
适合扩充题量；不能替代有人反馈的 mock。
optionMeanings_en: Pair with someone who has no relevant background at all.
Find someone who knows the target grading style to give feedback.
Recite your own answer to yourself, with no outside feedback.
Only drill questions and deliberately skip the feedback step.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They can't ask technically meaningful follow-up questions.
Follow-up questions and grading feel closer to the real interviewer.
No one can point out the requirement or tradeoff you missed.
Without feedback, your blind spots stay hidden.
optionDirectness_en: Fits general speaking practice; technical follow-up will be weak.
Fits target-company prep because the feedback matches the real style.
Fits a warm-up read-through, but it lacks outside probing.
Fits adding question volume, not replacing a feedback-based mock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

q: “读懂题解”和“面试中讲出设计”的最大区别是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest difference between understanding a write-up and explaining a design in an interview?
options: 讲出设计要在时间压力下自己组织结构和取舍
读懂题解更难，因为不需要表达
两者完全一样
讲出设计不需要任何技术判断
options_en: Explaining a design out loud means organizing structure and tradeoffs yourself, under time pressure.
Reading a write-up is harder because it requires no explanation.
The two are exactly the same skill.
Explaining a design requires no technical judgment at all.
why: 面试是实时沟通：要澄清需求、排序问题、画图、解释取舍并响应追问；阅读只是输入的一部分。
why_en: Speaking a design out loud requires actively organizing structure, tradeoffs, and communication under time pressure.
tradeoff: 主动组织表达 vs 被动接收阅读
optionMeanings: 把讲设计当成主动输出加沟通的任务。
颠倒了阅读和表达的难度关系。
否认输入和输出是两种技能。
错误地剥离了技术判断这一核心。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对应面试官真正在评估的能力。
表达通常比阅读更难，不是更容易。
会让人误以为看懂题解就等于会面试。
面试恰恰全程都在考技术判断。
optionDirectness: 适合描述现场面试能力；它强调自己组织和限时表达。
适合只比较阅读负担；没有覆盖面试输出难点。
适合低风险复习；真实面试和阅读不是同一任务。
适合非技术展示；系统设计仍然围绕技术判断。
optionMeanings_en: Treats explaining a design as active output plus communication.
Reverses the actual difficulty relationship between reading and speaking.
Denies that input and output are different skills.
Incorrectly strips out technical judgment as the core.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It matches what the interviewer is actually evaluating.
Speaking is usually harder than reading, not easier.
It wrongly implies understanding a write-up equals being interview-ready.
Technical judgment is exactly what's being tested throughout.
optionDirectness_en: Fits live interview skill because it stresses organizing under time.
Fits comparing reading load, not the hard part of interview output.
Fits low-risk review; real interviews and reading are different tasks.
Fits nontechnical presentation, but system design centers on judgment.

scenario: 主线 common questions 题单大约有 30 道，分布在 easy（约 4 道）、medium（约 13 道）、hard（约 13 道）三档。
scenario_en: The main common questions list has about 30 problems across easy, medium, and hard tiers: roughly 4 easy, 13 medium, and 13 hard.
q: 这个题量和难度分布，最支持哪条备考策略？
q_en: What prep strategy does this problem count and difficulty split support?
options: 跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard
题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上
只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题
在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档
options_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
why: 约 30 道题在三档间分布均衡，说明常见面试难度本身就是均衡分布的；两周内做不完全部，应按难度分层抽样，而不是只啃一档或反复刷同一批题。
why_en: With about thirty problems split evenly across easy, medium, and hard, the right move in a short window is to sample every tier, not just one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文章正文列出的主线练习题单，带书面 write-up。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common questions are the main practice list in the article, each with a written guide.

optionMeanings: 选项主张：跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard。
选项主张：题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上。
选项主张：只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题。
选项主张：在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档。
optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
适合本题给出的约束。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让系统依赖「跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题」这个前提。
会让方案围绕「在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档」展开。
optionMeanings_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.

This is the core issue in this scenario.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It commits the design to this assumption: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
It commits the design to this assumption: The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
It commits the design to this assumption: Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
It commits the design to this path: Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.

scenario: 你独立完成一题后，对比 answer key 发现自己的高层架构不同。
scenario_en: After completing a problem independently, you compare with the answer key and find that your high-level architecture is different.
q: 最有价值的复盘方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most useful way to review the difference?
options: 直接把自己写的完整答案删除重做一遍
只核对两边用的组件名称是否一致
跳过复盘环节，直接进入下一道练习题
比较背后的 requirements 和 tradeoffs
options_en: Delete your own complete answer and redo it from scratch.
Only check whether the component names on both sides match.
Skip the review step and go straight to the next practice question.
Compare the requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference.
why: 系统设计通常没有唯一图；复盘要找出作者为什么选了某个组件、你漏了哪个约束、哪些取舍没讲清。
why_en: The useful review compares requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference, not the memorization of one architecture diagram.
whenOtherWins: 如果你的方案违反了硬性需求或指标，那不是风格差异，是需要修正的设计错误。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Mine["My design"] --> Gap["Find gaps"]
    Key["Answer key"] --> Gap
    Gap --> Req["Requirements"]
    Gap --> Trade["Tradeoffs"]
    Gap --> Deep["Deep dives"]
tradeoff: 复盘约束和取舍 vs 复盘表面架构图
optionMeanings: 把不同结果当成完全失败处理。
只核对名词，不核对决策依据。
放弃从这道题里学习的机会。
把差异当成理解取舍的线索去追问。
optionScenarioImpacts: 丢掉了本可以对比学习的素材。
组件名一样，决策逻辑可能完全没学到。
同样的缺口会在下一题重复出现。
能定位自己漏掉的约束或没考虑的取舍。
optionDirectness: 适合方案明显错误时重做；这里先要理解差异来源。
适合快速核对表面组件；不能解释为什么选它们。
适合赶进度；会错过这道题给你的反馈。
适合复盘设计判断；差异会指向漏掉的约束。
optionMeanings_en: Treat a different result as total failure.
Only check naming, not the reasoning behind decisions.
Give up the chance to learn from this question.
Treat the difference as a clue to chase down the reasoning.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You throw away material you could have learned from.
Matching names doesn't mean you learned the decision logic.
The same gap will resurface on the next question.
You can pinpoint the missed constraint or unconsidered tradeoff.
optionDirectness_en: Fits clearly broken designs; here you first need the source of the gap.
Fits surface-level component checks, not why those components were chosen.
Fits moving fast, but it throws away the feedback from this question.
Fits reviewing design judgment because differences point to missed constraints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Constraints are the hard limits a design must satisfy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tradeoffs are the balances you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全准备路线的三个基础动作：
q_en: Fill in the three foundation steps in the preparation path:
text: 理解{{system design interview}}是什么，选择{{Delivery Framework}}，再学习{{Core Concepts}}、{{Key Technologies}}和{{Common Patterns}}。
why: 三步构成从面试形态到表达框架、再到知识地图的基础路线；缺一步，后面练习容易失焦。
why_en: The foundation is understanding the interview format, choosing a delivery framework, and then filling in core concepts, technologies, and patterns.
tradeoff: 先搭完整基础 vs 边练边补概念

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Delivery Framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

scenario: 你没有练习伙伴，但想先自己模拟白板设计流程。
scenario_en: You do not have a practice partner yet, but you want to simulate the whiteboard design flow by yourself.
q: 没有练习伙伴时，可行替代是什么？
q_en: What is a workable substitute before you have a mock partner?
options: 什么都不做，干等 mock 机会
只截图收藏别人的答案
用 Guided Practice 或白板自己讲一遍
只写代码，跳过架构图
options_en: Do nothing and just wait for a mock opportunity.
Only screenshot and save other people's answers.
Use Guided Practice or a whiteboard to narrate it yourself.
Only write code, skip the architecture diagram.
why: 没有 peer 时也能用 guided practice 或白板练结构化输出；重点是不要停留在只读的模式。
why_en: Guided practice or a virtual whiteboard lets you practice structured output even before you find a mock partner.
whenOtherWins: 能独立讲完整后，仍应尽快找 mock，因为真实追问很难自我模拟。
tradeoff: 自己动手画讲 vs 被动等待搭子
optionMeanings: 把练习进度完全交给等待。
把收集答案当成练习本身。
自己扮演讲解者，边画边说完整流程。
把练习范围缩小到只剩代码。
optionScenarioImpacts: 找到搭子前的时间完全被浪费。
截图不会训练任何表达或设计能力。
没有搭子也能练到结构化输出这一步。
漏掉了需求、架构和取舍的练习。
optionDirectness: 适合安排未来 mock；等待期间不会产生练习量。
适合收集参考资料；不会训练输出或取舍说明。
适合没有搭子时练流程；你仍然要边画边讲。
适合实现题；系统设计练习还需要架构图和取舍。
optionMeanings_en: Hand all your practice progress over to waiting.
Treat collecting answers as practice itself.
Play the role of the presenter, drawing and narrating the full flow.
Shrink the scope of practice down to just code.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The time before finding a partner is completely wasted.
Screenshots train no explanation or design skill.
You can still practice structured output without a partner.
It skips practicing requirements, architecture, and tradeoffs.
optionDirectness_en: Fits scheduling future mocks; waiting creates no practice volume.
Fits collecting references, not training output or tradeoff explanation.
Fits solo practice because you still draw and narrate the flow.
Fits implementation questions; design practice still needs architecture and tradeoffs.

termDefinitions.meaning: HelloInterview 提供的分步骤引导式练习工具，边做边给反馈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided Practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

scenario: 你在练题时没有固定推进顺序，想到哪讲到哪。
scenario_en: When practicing, you have no fixed answer order and just say whatever comes to mind.
q: 没有清晰 roadmap 的系统设计回答最容易出现什么问题？
q_en: What problem does a system design answer without a clear roadmap most often run into?
options: 所有问题都会自动收敛，不用管
已经不再需要澄清任何需求
即兴发挥必然比用框架更快
scope creep：不断发散、偏离核心需求
options_en: All problems automatically converge on their own, no effort needed.

Improvising is guaranteed to be faster than using a framework.

why_en: Without a roadmap, answers tend to drift into scope creep and lose time needed for the core design.
optionMeanings: 假设无框架也能自动聚焦。
假设可以跳过需求澄清环节。
假设即兴发挥天然更省时间。
讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求。
optionScenarioImpacts: 现实中恰恰相反，没框架更容易发散。
没澄清需求，设计方向可能整体跑偏。
来回摸索方向反而更费时间。
高层设计和深潜的时间被无关话题占用。
optionDirectness: 适合非常熟练的讲解者；新手无框架通常会发散。
适合需求已经写死的练习；真实面试仍要澄清。
适合短暂脑暴；正式回答通常会更费时间。
适合描述缺路线图的风险；发散会吃掉深潜时间。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes discussions self-focus even without a framework.
Assumes you can skip the requirements-clarification step.
Assumes improvising is inherently faster.
The discussion keeps expanding away from the core requirements.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: In reality the opposite happens without a framework.
Without clarifying requirements, the whole design can drift off target.
Wandering back and forth actually costs more time.
Time meant for the high-level design and deep dives gets eaten by tangents.
optionDirectness_en: Fits very experienced presenters; beginners usually drift without a framework.
Fits fully specified exercises; real interviews still need clarification.
Fits brief brainstorming; formal answers usually take longer this way.

termDefinitions.meaning: 讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求的现象。

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试回答时预先规划好的阶段顺序。

scenario_en: You have only two weeks to prepare for system design, your foundation is weak, but you can practice every day.
q: 最合理的时间分配倾向是什么？
q_en: What time-allocation strategy makes the most sense?

两周全部用来看题解，不做输出

optionMeanings: 把有限时间优先分给动手输出。
把所有时间都花在被动阅读上。
跳过基础，直接冲最难题目。
把练习简化成背名词。

q: 沿用 2015 年前后的老系统设计材料，最大的风险是？

options_en: There's too much content to finish learning.

why:
硬件这十年进步巨大，老材料的容量/延迟假设已失效；要用最新的 numbers to know 校准决策。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
Hardware has advanced enormously in the last decade, so reasoning from outdated constraints makes your design choices look stale.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.

q: 系统设计完全零基础的候选人，建议的准备节奏是？

options: 一两天速成

options_en: Cram it in one or two days.

why:
零基础建议全职冲刺，或摊开到 3-4 周；已经熟悉核心概念、经验丰富的人一周内备好也很常见，这个节奏决定你怎么排学习日历。

数字小抄：先用平均 QPS/TPS × 峰值系数（常用 2-5x）估峰值；Redis 简单 GET/SET 约 100k+ ops/s/实例；单主 SQL 写事务常按 1k-10k+ TPS/主库估；Kafka 单 partition 常按 5k-10k msg/s 起算，靠 partitions/brokers 横向扩；API worker 吞吐取决于是否打 DB/外部 API；队列只能削峰和排队，不能提高下游真实处理能力。
why_en:
If system design is entirely new, plan either a dedicated sprint or three to four weeks, while experienced candidates often prepare in under a week.

Capacity cheat sheet: estimate peak as average QPS/TPS times a peak factor, often 2-5x. A Redis instance can handle roughly 100k+ simple GET/SET ops/s; a single SQL primary is often reasoned about as 1k-10k+ write TPS; one Kafka partition is often estimated around 5k-10k msg/s, scaling with partitions and brokers. API worker throughput depends on DB or external calls. Queues smooth bursts but do not increase downstream capacity.
